stem: Which culture most likely created the sandals shown in the picture?

options.A: Indian.
options.B: Greek.
options.C: Mesopotamian.
options.D: Roman.

figure.source: 大學入學考試中心 115 學年度起適用學科能力測驗參考試卷英文考科

ev.t: In the Greek version, the toe strap ran between the first and second toes, while Roman sandals had the strap between the second and third toes.

note: 圖裡的帶子夾在第二趾和第三趾之間，對照第 2 段，是羅馬式的涼鞋。這一題要把文字描述轉成圖像，三個錯誤選項都是同一段列出的其他文化：(A) 印度的「趾鈕」涼鞋在大拇趾和第二趾之間是一個鈕，不是帶子；(B) 希臘式的帶子在大拇趾和第二趾之間；(C) 美索不達米亞人的帶子在第三趾和第四趾之間。

stem: Why is the footwear discussed in the passage called “flip-flop”?

options.A: Because of the noise it makes.
options.B: Because of its changeable design.
options.C: Because of its simple structure.
options.D: Because of the comfort of wearing it.

ev.t: The name comes from the sound the sandals make when they slap the walking feet.

note: 名稱來自走路時發出的聲音，sound 在選項換成 noise。(C) 的 simple 取自第 1 段開頭 the simplest shoe，但那一句講的是鞋子的樣子，不是名稱的由來。(B) 第 4 段說人字拖後來重新設計，但那是傳到美國以後的事，和名稱無關；(D) 第 4 段說人字拖一直受歡迎是因為方便，講的是受歡迎的原因，文章也沒有談穿起來舒不舒服。

stem: Which of the following is true about the modern development of the flip-flop?

options.A: Modern flip-flops originated from Indian toe knob sandals.
options.B: Americans loved the Japanese flip-flop because of its bright colors.
options.C: Rubber became the major material of the flip-flop before World War II.
options.D: The sandals American soldiers brought home from Japan later became modern flip-flops.

ev.t: Modern flip-flops derive from Japanese zōris
In the 1950s, flip-flops became popular in the United States as soldiers returning from occupied Japan brought zōris home.

note: 第 3 段說現代人字拖源自日本草履，第 4 段說美國士兵把草履從日本帶回家，兩段合起來就是 (D)。(A) 的 toe knob 在第 2 段，和現代人字拖無關；(B) 鮮豔的顏色是後來重新設計才有的，不是美國人喜歡的原因；(C) 橡膠是戰後才取代稻草。
map: soldiers returning from occupied Japan brought zōris home
American soldiers brought home from Japan
Modern flip-flops derive from Japanese zōris

stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a concern of wearing the flip-flop?

options.A: Personal health.
options.B: Poor quality.
options.C: Social appropriateness.
options.D: Marine pollution.

ev.t: Their simple design is responsible for many foot injuries.
Another issue is the suitability of exposing feet on the street and places other than the beach.
Millions of plastic discards end up in landfills or the ocean, releasing chemicals and at the same time taking centuries to decompose.

note: 第 5 段提到三個問題，在選項裡都換了說法：foot injuries 是 (A) Personal health，suitability 是 (C) Social appropriateness，plastic discards end up in the ocean 是 (D) Marine pollution。只有 (B) 品質不好文章沒提。

stem: What is the passage mainly about?

options.A: A special profession.
options.B: Shipping and trading.
options.C: Guidelines for safe docking.
options.D: Protection of the marine environment.

note: 第 1 段引出引水人這個職業，第 2–3 段說這份工作為什麼需要、難在哪裡，第 4 段總結這份工作的要求和責任，所以全文介紹的是一種特殊的職業。(B) 航運與貿易是第 1 段開頭的引子，範圍比引水人大得多，太過廣泛；(C) 船隻靠港的難處只在第 2、3 段，文章也沒有列出什麼準則，(D) 海洋環境的保護只在第 2 段和第 4 段末尾帶到，兩個都過於狹隘。

stem: Which of the following is part of the knowledge that a marine pilot must have?

options.A: The value of the ships.
options.B: The content of the cargo.
options.C: The weather conditions.
options.D: The diversity of marine life.

ev.t: In addition to the shallower seabeds, tide and wind pose further challenges for bringing ships into a port.
controls the vessel based on his or her knowledge of the port and the situation at hand

note: 第 3 段說潮汐和風會改變船的方向，第 4 段說引水人要依當下的狀況操控船隻，所以天氣狀況是必備的知識，原文的 wind 在選項換成概括的 weather conditions。(B) 的 cargo 取自第 2 段，那裡講的是擱淺時貨物會受損，不是引水人要懂貨物內容。(A) 文章沒有提到船的價值；(D) 第 4 段說引水人要保護海洋環境，這是職責，文章沒有說引水人要懂海洋生物的多樣性。

stem: What does “a crucial time” in the last paragraph refer to?

options.A: When the vessel hits a flat.
options.B: When the channel is not deep enough.
options.C: When there is a collision of two ships.
options.D: When a ship is waiting to enter the port.

ev.t: But the captain of a ship is responsible for guiding the vessel until they hit a port, waiting to enter the harbor.
A marine pilot goes on board at a crucial time

note: 第 1 段說船長把船開到港口、等候進港時，就換引水人接手，這正是引水人登船的關鍵時刻；harbor 在選項換成 port。(B) 的 channel 取自第 2 段，講的是港口的地形，不是登船的時間點。(A) 的 hit 照抄第 1 段 until they hit a port，flat 是淺灘，船撞上淺灘就是第 2 段說的擱淺，那是引水人要避免的意外，不是引水人登船的時候；(C) 文章沒有提到兩艘船相撞。

stem: How does the author conclude the passage in the last paragraph?

options.A: By adding new details.
options.B: By predicting future development.
options.C: By summarizing the main points.
options.D: By giving advice to the general public.

ev.t: Marine pilotage is a job that requires a high degree of proficiency as well as quick and independent thinking.
The pilot is responsible for not only the safety of the ship but also the protection of the port and the marine environment.

note: 末段把前面講過的內容再收一次：專業知識對應第 2 段，迅速獨立的判斷對應第 3 段的潮汐和風，船和海洋環境的安全對應第 2 段的擱淺與貨物外洩，所以是總結重點。(A) 末段沒有新的細節；(B) 末段沒有談未來的發展；(D) 末段講的是引水人的職責，沒有給一般大眾任何建議。

stem: What can we learn about zebrafish from the passage?

options.A: How they should be studied in labs.
options.B: Where they derive their regenerative ability.
options.C: Why they share humans’ genetic code.
options.D: What they may offer in medical advancements.

ev.t: Scientists thus hope that understanding the self-healing mystery of the fish may one day allow humans to regenerate such organs as eyes, hearts, and spines.
it may give rise to new treatments for blindness caused by retinal damage

note: 第 2 段說斑馬魚或許能讓人類的器官再生，第 3 段說可能帶來治療失明的新療法，這些都是醫學上的進展。(A) 第 1 段的 study 講的是斑馬魚身體透明、容易研究，說的是為什麼常拿斑馬魚做研究，文章沒有說應該怎麼研究；(B) 文章只說 GABA 在視網膜再生中扮演重要角色，沒說再生能力從哪裡來；(C) 只說基因有 70% 相同，沒說為什麼相同。

stem: Which of the following statements is true regarding GABA in zebrafish?

options.A: Increasing GABA level facilitates neuron activities.
options.B: There is a high level of GABA in the brain of zebrafish.
options.C: Lowering GABA levels in the brain can stimulate retina regrowth.
options.D: GABA contains chemical elements that trigger the growth of neurons.

ev.t: They found that lowering GABA levels in zebrafish can trigger retina regeneration

note: trigger 在選項換成 stimulate，regeneration 換成 regrowth。(A) 方向相反，原文說 GABA 降低神經元的活動；(D) 照抄同一段的 chemical 和 trigger，可是會啟動再生的是降低 GABA，不是 GABA 含有什麼成分；(B) 文章沒有比較斑馬魚腦中 GABA 的高低。

stem: Which of the following is closest in meaning to “replicated” in the third paragraph?

options.A: Reproduced.
options.B: Reassembled.
options.C: Recycled.
options.D: Restored.

ev.t: If the process can be replicated in humans, it may give rise to new treatments for blindness caused by retinal damage.

note: 把斑馬魚視網膜再生的過程在人類身上「再做一次」，replicate 和 reproduce 都是複製、重現。(B) Reassembled 是把拆開的東西重新組裝，(C) Recycled 是回收再利用，兩個都不是把同一個過程再做一次。(D) Restored 照抄同一段 vision is restored，但恢復的是視力，不是把過程複製到人身上。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following is an opinion, but NOT a fact?

options.A: Humans and zebrafish have 70 percent of genes in common.
options.B: Zebrafish can quickly recover vision after damage to the retina.
options.C: Scientists are testing if the GABA theory works on mice as it does on zebrafish.
options.D: Understanding regeneration in zebrafish may allow humans to regrow their organs.

ev.t: Scientists thus hope that understanding the self-healing mystery of the fish may one day allow humans to regenerate such organs as eyes, hearts, and spines.

note: hope 和 may 表示的是科學家的期望和推測，還沒有證實，屬於意見。(A)、(B)、(C) 文章都當作研究結果或正在進行的事來陳述，是事實。
map: may one day allow humans to regenerate such organs
may allow humans to regrow their organs

stem: What is this passage mainly about?

options.A: A renowned Antarctic explorer.
options.B: The extreme weather in Antarctica.
options.C: A challenging voyage to Antarctica.
options.D: The amazing discovery of a sunken ship.

note: 第 1 段點出這是一段勇氣與毅力的傳奇，第 2–5 段依時間寫整趟航程從出發、受困、棄船到獲救，所以全文講的是一次艱難的南極航行。(D) 沉船的發現只講第 1 段，是用來引出故事的新聞，過於狹隘；(A) 文章沒有介紹 Shackleton 這個人的生平，(B) 天候只是航程的背景，這兩個選項都偏離主題。

stem: Which of the following idioms is closest in meaning to “exacerbated the situation” in the third paragraph?

options.A: Broke the ice.
options.B: Cost an arm and a leg.
options.C: Missed the boat.
options.D: Added fuel to the fire.

ev.t: Freezing water rushed in and exacerbated the situation.

note: 船板已經擠壞，冰水又灌進來，情況雪上加霜；exacerbate 是讓壞事變得更糟，和 add fuel to the fire（火上加油）意思相同。(A) break the ice 是打破僵局、化解尷尬，雖然第 3 段講的正是冰，但這個片語和冰塊無關；(B) cost an arm and a leg 是非常昂貴；(C) miss the boat 是錯失良機。三個片語都沒有「讓情況更糟」的意思。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about Shackleton and his Antarctic expedition?

options.A: His journey lasted more than two years.
options.B: He was the first man to cross over the Antarctic.
options.C: His team camped out on Elephant Island for five months.
options.D: He sent five crew members on a lifeboat to get help from a whaling station.

ev.t: On August 4, 1914, Sir Ernest Shackleton, along with a skilled crew of 27, set sail on the Endurance toward the South Pole, hoping to make the first land crossing over Antarctica.
On August 30, 1916, Shackleton finally got back to Elephant Island with a ship big enough to rescue the rest of his men.

note: 原文沒有直接寫「兩年」，要把第 2 段出發的日期和第 5 段救回所有人的日期相減，1914 年 8 月到 1916 年 8 月底，超過兩年。(B) 第 2 段只說他希望完成第一次徒步橫越南極大陸，船後來困在浮冰裡、沉沒，這個目標沒有達成。(C) 和 (D) 都照抄第 4 段的字詞，卻把事情接錯：在浮冰上紮營五個月的是船員，不是在象島；五名船員是跟著 Shackleton 一起去求救，不是他派出去的。

stem: Which of the following shows the correct route of the Endurance after leaving South Georgia?

options.A: （見圖）
options.B: （見圖）
options.C: （見圖）
options.D: （見圖）

figure.source: 大學入學考試中心 115 學年度學科能力測驗英文考科

ev.t: Two days after leaving South Georgia in December, the Endurance encountered floating ice, and was soon completely trapped in pack ice.
The worthy vessel held up for nine months, drifting down south slowly and then pushed northward by the ice.
Weeks later, they watched the Endurance sink beneath the Weddell Sea.

note: 題目問的是堅忍號這艘船的路線，不是船員的路線：船離開南喬治亞島後困在浮冰裡，先往南漂、再往北推，最後沉在威德爾海，沒有到過象島，對應 (C)。(A) 畫到象島再回南喬治亞島，那是第 4 段船員搭救生艇和 Shackleton 求救的路線。(B) 從南喬治亞島先往西經過象島，再往南繞回來，可是第 2–3 段說船離開南喬治亞島兩天就困在浮冰裡，跟著浮冰先往南漂，從來沒有到過象島；(D) 從南喬治亞島直接到象島再往南，是把船員到象島的地名套在船身上，船從來沒有到過象島。

stem: Which question can the passage answer?

options.A: Where was the first spiral staircase constructed?
options.B: Who was the first designer of the spiral staircase?
options.C: What is the world’s most famous spiral staircase?
options.D: Why is the spiral staircase popular in modern times?

ev.t: The timeless appeal of their classical design makes spiral staircases a much-desired feature in luxury homes, offices, and public buildings nowadays.

note: 最後一句說古典設計歷久不衰，所以螺旋梯現今很受青睞，回答了 (D) 的「為什麼」。(A) 文章只說最早的記載在舊約、現存最古老的在圖拉真柱，沒說第一座建在哪裡；(B)、(C) 文章都沒提。

stem: What does “them” in the third paragraph refer to?

options.A: Stairs.
options.B: Confines.
options.C: Attackers.
options.D: Defenders.

ev.t: The defenders, living in the castles, were familiar with the stair pattern and could retreat up them very swiftly

note: retreat up 後面要接可以往上退的地方，就是同一句前面 the stair pattern 說的樓梯。(B) confines 在 them 後面，是攻方在昏暗狹窄的樓梯間跌倒的地方，代名詞不會指後面才出現的字，retreat up 也要接可以往上走的樓梯。(D) Defenders 是這一句的主詞，(C) Attackers 在後半句，兩者都是人，不能「退到人上面」。

stem: According to the passage, which is a correct time sequence of the materials used in making spiral staircases?

options.A: stone → iron → steel → glass
options.B: stone → wood → iron → steel
options.C: iron → marble → wood → glass
options.D: marble → wood → stone → concrete

ev.t: The staircase was built in 113 AD, with a total of 185 steps carved in stone and marble.
In Victorian times, cast iron spiral staircases were popular for public buildings and homes for the rich.
In the latter half of the 20th century, steel frames became cost-effective, and thus affordable for a much wider staircase market.
Today, spiral staircases come in a wide variety of materials: steel, wood, concrete, and recently even glass.

note: 依時間把材料排出來：西元 113 年的石頭、維多利亞時期的鑄鐵、二十世紀的鋼、最近的玻璃。選項照用原文的材料名稱，難處在把散在兩段的時間點串起來。(B) 的木頭和 (D) 的混凝土只出現在第 4 段今天的材料清單裡，不會排在鐵或鋼之前；(C) 大理石和石頭同樣是第 2 段西元 113 年圖拉真柱的材料，不會排在維多利亞時期的鐵之後；(D) 把同一時期的大理石和石頭拆開，中間又插進今天才有的木頭，順序也不對。

stem: Which of the following statements can be inferred about spiral staircases in the Medieval Ages?

options.A: The staircase was too narrow to allow any quick retreat.
options.B: The clockwise design favored right-handed castle defenders.
options.C: The uneven steps made it easier to ascend than descend the stairs.
options.D: The staircase was dark enough for defenders to hide from attackers.

ev.t: Also, the stairs were designed to turn clockwise upwards.
This means that ascenders would have their right hand tight against the narrowest part of the staircases, close to the central pole, and as a result were unable to use their sword effectively.

note: 原文只說往上爬的攻方右手貼著中柱、揮不了劍；守方站在上面往下打，右手剛好在寬的那一側，所以推得出順時針的設計對慣用右手的守方有利。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 narrow 和 retreat，原文說狹窄讓攻方只能一次上來一個人，守方反而能很快往上退；(C) 照抄 uneven steps 和 ascend，原文說高低不平的台階讓攻方容易絆倒，沒有比較上樓和下樓哪個容易；(D) 原文說光線昏暗讓攻方更容易跌倒，沒有說守方躲在暗處。

stem: What is the passage mainly about?

options.A: Why east is referred to as the “Orient.”
options.B: How maps differ from GPS in function.
options.C: How map orientation evolved over time.
options.D: Why maps were important during the age of exploration.

note: 第 1 段提問地圖為什麼北方朝上，第 2–5 段依時間寫東方朝上、南方朝上、北方朝上到 GPS 隨路線轉向，所以全文講方位怎麼隨時代演變。(A) 只講第 2 段最後一句，(B) 只講第 5 段的 GPS，(D) 只講第 4 段的時代背景，三個錯誤選項都過於狹隘。

stem: What does “this” refer to in the second paragraph?

options.A: The word dakshina.
options.B: Physical evidence.
options.C: Ancient India.
options.D: East-orientation of maps.

ev.t: In ancient India, for example, maps were most likely oriented to the east.
Though there is no physical evidence to support this

note: 沒有實物證據可以支持的是前一句的整件事：古印度地圖很可能以東方為上方。(B) Physical evidence 是同一個子句裡的字，(A)、(C) 也都照抄這一段的字詞，但都不是要「證明」的那件事。
map: maps were most likely oriented to the east

stem: Which of the following is closest in meaning to “a blip” in the last paragraph?

options.A: A temporary state.
options.B: An urgent need.
options.C: A critical decision.
options.D: An advanced system.

ev.t: So, perhaps the north-on-top practice is less a rule and more a blip.

note: less A and more B 是「與其說是 A，不如說是 B」，blip 和 rule（長久的規則）相對；下一句又說我們回到了古代的起點，可見北方朝上只是一時的現象。(B) 急迫的需要、(C) 關鍵的決定都和 rule 構不成對比，也接不上「回到起點」；(D) 的 advanced 和下一句的 technological advancements 字形相近，但 blip 講的是北方朝上這個習慣維持不久，和技術先不先進無關。

stem: Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: Sailors took the North Star as their final destination.
options.B: The GPS system has a fixed direction for orientation.
options.C: South was placed at the top of maps in the pre-Biblical era.
options.D: Old Islamic maps put south at the top for religious purposes.

ev.t: Map makers in Arabia also drew maps with south on top since the earliest Muslims lived north of Mecca, and a south-oriented map would show the followers looking up toward their holy city.

note: 讓信徒抬頭望向聖城麥加，就是出於宗教的理由。(C) 照抄第 2 段的 pre-Biblical，但那個時代是東方朝上；(A) 北極星是用來辨認方向，不是目的地；(B) 第 5 段說 GPS 畫面隨路線轉向，不是固定方向。
map: drew maps with south on top
looking up toward their holy city

stem: What is this passage mainly about?

options.A: The evolution of traffic control systems.
options.B: The inventors of traffic lights in history.
options.C: The functions of different traffic signals.
options.D: The development of modern transportation.

note: 第 1 段講 Knight 仿照鐵路號誌設計出交通號誌，第 2 段講這套號誌裝在倫敦一個月就因為瓦斯外洩爆炸停用，第 3 段講美國各大城跟進，Potts 再加上黃燈成為三色號誌，第 4 段講自駕車出現後號誌可能不再需要。文章裡沒有一句話直接點出全文的主旨，可是四段依時間往下排，合起來講的就是交通號誌系統怎麼演變。(B) 發明者只寫到 Knight 和 Potts 兩位，(C) 各種號誌代表什麼意思只在第 1、3 段帶到，都過於狹隘；(D) 文章只講號誌，沒講整個現代交通運輸，太過廣泛。

stem: Which of the following pictures shows Knight’s proposed traffic signal?

options.A: （見圖）
options.B: （見圖）
options.C: （見圖）
options.D: （見圖）

figure.source: 大學入學考試中心 114 學年度學科能力測驗英文考科

ev.t: Thus, he proposed a signaling system based on the railway movable-arm signal: Arms extending horizontally commanded drivers to stop, whereas arms lowered to a 45-degree angle told drivers to move on, resembling a traffic director’s gestures.
Red and green gas lamps were added to the signal for use at night.

note: Knight 的號誌要同時有可以擺動的號誌臂和夜間用的燈，四張圖裡只有 (C) 兩者都有。(B) 只有臂、沒有燈，比較像他參考的鐵路號誌本身；(A) 只有燈；(D) 寫 STOP、GO 的牌子文章沒提。

ev.t: Secondly, as people are drawn into the story, they tend to take the perspective of the characters and rehearse the plot unconsciously.

note: 冒號後面就是解釋：街道又暗又難看，河是一條髒水，工業革命把這裡燻黑了，所以 blackened 指的是汙染嚴重。(B) 照抄 hole，但「洞」是形容大街的比喻；(C) 照抄 heart，但這裡的 heart 是「核心地帶」，不是人心。(D) 文章沒有提到工人的制服，blackened 形容的是整個地方，不是工人穿的衣服。

ev.t: Their hoops, often made of metal, were not merely toys for Greek children but served as exercise devices as well.

note: 希臘人的圈圈也是運動器材，exercise device 在選項換成 a tool for workout。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 medical，但醫療紀錄記的是玩圈圈玩到受傷；(B) 照抄第 3 段的 animals，但圈圈是用來象徵動物，不是訓練動物；(D) 照抄 circle of life，但那是北美原住民，不是夏威夷舞者。

stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a way of enjoying hula hoop fun?

options.A: Striking.
options.B: Twirling.
options.C: Spinning.
options.D: Kicking.

ev.t: Although the term did not emerge until the 18th century, toy hoops twirled around the waist, limbs, or neck can be traced back to ancient times.
They also struck them with sticks to roll them down the road.
Hoops spun their way through the cultures of pre-colonial America as well.

note: 有提到的三種玩法，選項都把原文的動詞改成動名詞：twirled 是 (B) Twirling，struck 是 (A) Striking，spun 是 (C) Spinning。用腳踢圈圈文章沒提。

stem: According to the passage, what materials have been used for making hoops?

options.A: reed, grapevine, bamboo, plastic
options.B: reed, grapevine, plastic, metal
options.C: reed, bamboo, plastic, animal skin
options.D: grapevine, plastic, metal, animal skin

ev.t: As early as 1000 BC, Egyptian children played with hoop toys of dried grapevine.
Their hoops, often made of metal
Dancers used small reed hoops as symbolic representations of animals such as eagles or snakes.
when a plastic version was successfully marketed by California’s Wham-O toy company

note: 四種材料散在三段：埃及的葡萄藤、希臘的金屬、北美原住民的蘆葦、Wham-O 的塑膠。選項照用原文的材料名稱，竹子和獸皮文章都沒提：(A) 有竹子，(C) 有竹子和獸皮，(D) 有獸皮。

stem: Why do farmers in Assam dig trenches in tea gardens?

options.A: To protect tea trees.
options.B: To trap elephants.
options.C: To expand tea farms.
options.D: To mark boundaries of tea gardens.

ev.t: Much of the forest land where tea is grown in Assam is flat and thus farmers must dig drainage trenches to prevent water from accumulating and hurting the shrubs.

note: 挖排水溝是為了不讓積水傷害茶樹，原文的 shrubs 在選項換成 tea trees。(B) 照抄下一句的 trap，但溝渠變成大象的死亡陷阱是意外，不是挖溝的目的。(C) 第 2 段開頭說茶園愈來愈多，那是茶園擴張破壞大象的棲地，挖溝並不能擴大茶園；(D) 的 mark 呼應同一段的 landmarks，可是拿茶園當地標的是大象，溝渠也不是用來標出茶園的邊界。
map: to prevent water from accumulating and hurting the shrubs

stem: Why are baby elephants easily injured in the Assam tea gardens according to the passage?

options.A: They cannot find a safe shelter when climbing out of the trenches.
options.B: They cannot locate the landmarks while trying to navigate forests.
options.C: They are trapped by the sharp branches of the tea trees.
options.D: They have difficulties moving around the uneven fields.

ev.t: But baby elephants, not used to negotiating rough ground, may easily fall into the trenches and get hurt

note: negotiate 在這裡是「通過、走過」，不是談判；小象不習慣走崎嶇的地面，在選項換成在不平的田裡行動有困難，rough 換成 uneven。(A) 照抄 safe shelter 和 climb out，但安全的庇護所是母象選來生產的地方；(B) 照抄 landmarks，那是成年大象辨認方向用的。(C) 文章沒有提到茶樹的枝條，小象受傷是因為掉進溝渠。

stem: Which of the following statements about elephants and the tea gardens is true according to the passage?

options.A: The elephants use the trenches to roam around the tea gardens.
options.B: The fast growth of the tea gardens destroys the elephants’ food source.
options.C: Elephants are unwilling to leave their injured members behind in the tea gardens.
options.D: Pregnant elephants avoid delivering babies in the tea gardens for fear of being disturbed.

ev.t: Furthermore, elephants are known to resist leaving their sick or dying behind, and a herd may linger at a trench with a trapped baby for hours, reluctant to move on until all hope is lost.

note: resist leaving 換成 unwilling to leave，sick or dying 換成 injured members。(D) 照抄 Pregnant，但原文正好相反，母象常到茶園生產；(A) 照抄 trenches，溝渠是陷阱，不是大象移動的路線；(B) 文章說茶園破壞的是棲地，沒說食物來源。
map: resist leaving their sick or dying behind
unwilling to leave their injured members behind

stem: What does “it” in the last paragraph refer to?

options.A: To certify elephant-friendly trenches and organizations.
options.B: To reward tea growers for protecting the environment.
options.C: To encourage consumers to choose high-quality brands.
options.D: To create a win-win situation for elephants and tea farms.

ev.t: Is it possible for elephants to coexist with the prosperous tea business?
Elephant Friendly Tea is an organization that takes the initiative to make it possible.

note: make it possible 回應前一句的問句 Is it possible …：讓大象和茶葉產業共存，也就是兩全其美。(A) 照抄同一段的 certification，可是第 3 段說認證的對象是做好保護措施的茶農和茶葉品牌，不是溝渠，也不是組織；(B)、(C) 照抄後一句組織的做法，那是達成目標的方法，不是 it 本身；(C) 的 high-quality 原文也沒提。
map: elephants to coexist with the prosperous tea business
a win-win situation for elephants and tea farms

stem: Which of the following is true about the earliest traders in Zanzibar?

options.A: The earliest traders arrived around 900 AD.
options.B: Most of the earliest merchants came from Africa.
options.C: Asian merchants arrived centuries before the African settlers.
options.D: Traders from Persia settled down permanently around 1000 AD.

ev.t: Traders from Asia had already visited the islands 900 years before the arrival of its first permanent settlers from the African mainland (around 1000 AD).

note: 非洲移民約西元 1000 年才定居，亞洲商人早了 900 年就來過，選項把 900 years 換成 centuries。(B) 第 2 段說最早來到這裡的是亞洲商人，從非洲大陸來的是約西元 1000 年才定居的移民，不是最早的商人。(A) 照抄 900，但 900 是相差的年數，不是西元年份；(D) 照抄 1000 AD 和 permanent，但 1000 年定居的是非洲移民，不是波斯商人。
map: first permanent settlers from the African mainland

stem: According to the passage, where is Zanzibar most likely located on the following map?

options.A: A
options.B: B
options.C: C
options.D: D

figure.source: 大學入學考試中心 112 學年度學科能力測驗英文考科

ev.t: Situated off the coast of Tanzania and washed by the warm, clean waters of the Indian Ocean, Zanzibar is a tropical archipelago comprised of several scattered islands.
thanks to its location on the trade route between Arabia and Africa

note: 坦尚尼亞在非洲東岸，桑吉巴在它的外海、臨印度洋，又位在阿拉伯和非洲之間的航線上，對應地圖上的 B。(D) 在非洲南端附近，不在坦尚尼亞外海；(C) 在亞洲印度的外海，不在非洲沿岸；(A) 在非洲西北角、臨大西洋，不臨印度洋。

stem: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage about Zanzibar?

options.A: For centuries, Zanzibar has been a heaven for beach lovers.
options.B: Cloves, vanilla, and cinnamon are common spices in Zanzibar.
options.C: Besides spices, Zanzibar is well known for a great variety of jewelry.
options.D: Vasco da Gama was Zanzibar’s first foreign ruler during the Age of Exploration.

ev.t: The unique cultural intersections, scented with the aroma of cloves, vanilla, and cinnamon floating in the air, give these jewels on the Indian Ocean an amazing charm that goes far beyond tropical beach fun.

note: 空氣裡隨時飄著丁香、香草和肉桂的香味，推得出這些香料在桑吉巴很常見。(A) 第 1 段說桑吉巴「現在」以海灘聞名，以前讓人想到的是財富，文章沒說它幾百年來一直是海灘愛好者的天堂。(C) 照抄 jewels，但這裡的珠寶是比喻這些島嶼，不是真的珠寶；(D) 照抄 Vasco da Gama，他只是抵達桑吉巴，統治者是之後的葡萄牙人、阿拉伯人和英國人。

stem: Which set of words is used in the passage to refer to Zanzibar?

options.A: islands, settlements, posts, crossroads
options.B: islands, posts, jewels, destination
options.C: archipelago, islands, jewels, destination
options.D: archipelago, settlements, paths, islands

ev.t: Zanzibar is a tropical archipelago comprised of several scattered islands.
This popular beach destination is now famous for its white sand beaches, slender palms, and turquoise seas.
give these jewels on the Indian Ocean an amazing charm

note: 同一個地方，作者換了四個說法來指桑吉巴，避免一直重複 Zanzibar：archipelago、islands、beach destination、jewels on the Indian Ocean。(A)、(D) 的 settlements、posts 是波斯商人在島上建的聚落和據點，paths 是宗教交會的路徑，都不是桑吉巴本身。(B) 其他三個說法都對，但同樣混進了 posts。

stem: What is the main purpose of the passage?

options.A: To explain the origin of the Swiss army knife.
options.B: To introduce the functions of the Swiss army knife.
options.C: To emphasize the importance of the Swiss army knife.
options.D: To tell a story about the designer of the Swiss army knife.

note: 從軍方需要一把刀、Victorinox 設計士兵刀、軍官刀上市，到美軍取名 Swiss army knife，全文依時間講瑞士刀的由來。(B) 刀有哪些功能，是交代由來時順帶提到的細節，過於狹隘；(D) Elsener 只出現在第 3 段，不是整篇的主角，同樣過於狹隘；(C) 文章沒有強調瑞士刀有多重要，偏離主題。

stem: What does “It” in the third paragraph refer to?

options.A: The Swiss army needed a knife for every soldier.
options.B: Every good Swiss citizen had a knife in his pocket.
options.C: Swiss knives were competing with imported knives.
options.D: Canned food was becoming popular in the Swiss army.

ev.t: Swiss generals decided to issue each soldier a standard knife to serve both as a screwdriver and a can opener.
It was a lifesaver for Swiss knife makers, who were struggling to compete with cheaper German imports.

note: 對瑞士刀具業者來說是救命稻草的，是前一段結尾的那件事：軍方決定發給每個士兵一把刀，等於送上一筆大訂單。(C) 照抄同一句後半的 imports，那是業者的困境，不是救命稻草；(D) 罐頭普及只是軍方需要刀的原因之一。(B) 照抄第 1 段的 every good Swiss citizen，那句俗話說的是今天瑞士刀有多普遍，不是當年救了刀具業者的那件事。
map: issue each soldier a standard knife
needed a knife for every soldier

stem: Why did the Swiss army NOT purchase the Swiss Officer’s Knife?

options.A: The design of the knife was too simple.
options.B: The knife was sold out to American soldiers.
options.C: The army had no budget to make the purchase.
options.D: The new design was not considered necessary for officers to own.

ev.t: The Swiss military purchasers considered the new model with a corkscrew for opening wine not “essential for survival,” so officers had to buy this new model by themselves.

note: 採購人員認為多了開瓶器的新款不是生存必需品，essential 在選項換成 necessary。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 simple，但那是士兵刀的設計；(B) 照抄 American soldiers，美軍大量購買是二次大戰後的事。(C) 文章沒有提到軍方的預算，不買的原因是採購人員認為開瓶器不是生存必需。

stem: Who gave the name “the Swiss army knife” to the knife discussed in the passage?

options.A: Carl Elsener.
options.B: Swiss generals.
options.C: American soldiers.
options.D: German businessmen.

ev.t: After the Second World War, a great number of American soldiers were stationed in Europe.
However, it seems that “Schweizer Offizier Messer” was too difficult for them to say, so they just called it the Swiss army knife, and that is the name it is now known by all over the world.

note: they 指前面幾句的美軍：瑞士德語的名字太難唸，他們乾脆叫它 Swiss army knife。其他三個選項都是文章出現過的人，但和取名無關：(A) Elsener 設計士兵刀，(B) 瑞士將領決定發刀給士兵，(D) 德國的刀具是和瑞士業者競爭的便宜進口貨。

stem: What is the passage mainly about?

options.A: The preparation of a health food.
options.B: A traditional delicacy from Java.
options.C: A gourmet guide for vegetarians.
options.D: The cultural heritage of Indonesia.

note: 第 1 段介紹天貝是印尼的傳統食物，第 2–5 段依序講源自爪哇的起源、營養、料理方式和文化價值，所以全文介紹的是一種來自爪哇的傳統美食。(A) 料理方式只講第 4 段，(C) 素食者只在第 3 段提到，都過於狹隘；(D) 印尼的文化遺產範圍比天貝大得多，第 5 段只說天貝有機會列入，太過廣泛。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about tempeh?

options.A: It is mainly served as a side dish.
options.B: It is formed from fermented soybeans.
options.C: It is discarded when fungi grow around it.
options.D: It has the same nutritional benefits as kimchi.

ev.t: tempeh is a fermented food originating from the island of Java
It was discovered during tofu production when discarded soybean residue caught microbial spores from the air and grew certain whitish fungi around it.

note: 天貝是豆渣沾上微生物發酵而成的食物，也就是由發酵的大豆做成。(C) 照抄 discarded 和 fungi，但丟棄的是豆渣，長出真菌後反而變成天貝；(A) 照抄第 4 段的 side dish，但天貝也可以當主菜、點心；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 kimchi，那只是拿來比喻同樣是國家的代表食物。

stem: What aspects of tempeh are discussed in paragraphs 2 to 4?

options.A: Origin → nutrition → cuisine.
options.B: Origin → cuisine → marketing.
options.C: Cuisine → nutrition → marketing.
options.D: Distribution → cuisine → nutrition.

ev.t: tempeh is a fermented food originating from the island of Java
Tempeh is high in protein and low in fat, and contains a host of vitamins.
In addition to its highly nutritional makeup, tempeh has diverse preparation possibilities.

note: 看每段的第一句就能抓出重點：第 2 段源自爪哇，第 3 段營養成分，第 4 段料理方式。第 4 段開頭 In addition to its highly nutritional makeup 先回顧上一段的營養，再轉到料理，正好把兩段接起來。(B)、(C) 的 marketing 文章沒有談，(B) 又把第 3 段的營養說成料理，(C) 把第 2 段的由來說成料理；(D) 的 distribution 可以對上第 2 段後半天貝傳遍印尼各地，但後面兩項順序顛倒，第 3 段才是營養、第 4 段才是料理。
map: originating from the island of Java
high in protein and low in fat

stem: Which of the following can be inferred from this passage?

options.A: Senior citizens will eat tempeh as vitamin supplement.
options.B: Tempeh will soon be more popular than kimchi or miso.
options.C: The nutrition of tempeh will be reduced with mass production.
options.D: Tempeh is likely to be recognized as an international cultural symbol.

ev.t: With the Indonesian traditional fabric batik being recognized by UNESCO as “Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity,” tempeh has great potential for this honor as well.

note: 蠟染已經列入人類非物質文化遺產，天貝也很有希望得到這項殊榮，換個說法就是很可能成為國際認可的文化象徵。(B) 照抄 kimchi，文章沒有比較誰比較受歡迎，還說天貝在國際上不算熱門；(A) 照抄 vitamin，文章沒提年長者；(C) 第 2 段說天貝是各地人家自己在家做的，文章沒有談大量生產，也沒說營養會因此減少。
map: has great potential for this honor

stem: Which of the following is the mission of IIHS?

options.A: Car crash investigations.
options.B: Vehicle crash testing.
options.C: Property damage compensation.
options.D: Independent research on insurance policies.

ev.t: Crash testing for vehicles is very important in helping minimize deaths, injuries, and property damage from vehicle crashes.
One unit of the U.S. government responsible for ensuring the correct undertaking of this task is the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS)

note: IIHS 負責的 this task，指前一句的車輛撞擊測試。(A) 照抄 crash，但 IIHS 做的是撞擊測試，用測試車模擬撞擊，不是調查已經發生的車禍；(C) 照抄 property damage，那是撞擊測試想減少的損失，IIHS 不負責賠償；(D) 照抄 independent 和 Insurance，但 independent 形容的是這個機構，名稱裡的保險也不表示它研究保單。

stem: How does the frontal impact test differ from the offset test?

options.A: The vehicle travels at a higher speed in the frontal test.
options.B: The vehicle receives fewer impact forces in the offset test.
options.C: Only a small part of the vehicle takes the impact forces in the offset test.
options.D: The front of a vehicle crashes into another vehicle only in the frontal test.

ev.t: It is important since impact forces in this kind of test remain the same as those with the frontal impact test, but only a small portion of the car absorbs all the force of the impact.

note: 兩種測試的撞擊力道相同，差別在偏置撞擊只由車子的一小部分承受，portion 換成 part，absorb 換成 take。(A) 文章沒有比較兩種測試的車速；(B) 照抄 impact forces，但原文說力道相同，不是比較小；(D) 原文說兩種測試都可能撞上另一輛車，不是只有正面撞擊。
map: only a small portion of the car absorbs
Only a small part of the vehicle takes

stem: What does “crumple zone” mean in the third paragraph?

options.A: The space in a car where drivers can move freely.
options.B: The device that warns the driver about a potential collision.
options.C: An exit of a vehicle for occupants to escape from in a crash.
options.D: An area of a vehicle that absorbs the forces from a collision.

ev.t: This happens because cars usually do not have a significant crumple zone on the side to cushion all the impact forces before the occupant is injured.

note: 不定詞 to cushion all the impact forces 說明 crumple zone 的作用：在乘客受傷前緩衝撞擊力，也就是吸收衝擊力的區域；crumple 是「壓皺、壓扁」。(A) 讓駕駛自由活動的空間、(B) 碰撞前警告駕駛的裝置，都和「緩衝撞擊力」無關，文章也沒提。(C) 照抄 occupant，但這個區域是用來保護乘客，不是讓乘客逃生的出口。
map: to cushion all the impact forces
absorbs the forces from a collision

stem: Which part of the vehicle is the focus of the rollover test? Choose the English letter linked to the part.

options.A: A
options.B: B
options.C: C
options.D: D

figure.source: 大學入學考試中心 111 學年度起適用學科能力測驗參考試卷英文考科

ev.t: A rollover test verifies the car’s ability to support itself, especially from the pillars supporting the roof, during a dynamic impact.

note: 翻滾測試的重點是支撐車頂的車柱，圖上 D 指的就是車頂和車身之間的柱子。(A) 是車頭，屬於正面和偏置撞擊測試；(C) 是車門，屬於側面撞擊測試；(B) 是輪胎，文章沒提。

stem: Which of the following pictures best represents the image of a typical Maasai warrior?

options.A: （見圖）
options.B: （見圖）
options.C: （見圖）
options.D: （見圖）

ev.t: The most recognizable piece of clothing is the shúkà, a sheet of fabric worn wrapped around the body.
A Maasai warrior is rarely seen without his spear and shield.

note: 典型的馬賽戰士要身裹一塊布，長矛和盾牌不離身，三樣都有的只有 (B)。(A) 拿的是弓箭，(C) 只有盾牌，(D) 只有長矛，也都沒有裹身的布。

stem: What can we learn from the passage about the Maasai people?

options.A: They have been urged by governments to leave behind their traditions.
options.B: They resist foreign influence because they were enslaved in the past.
options.C: A boy has to kill a lion by himself before becoming an adult.
options.D: A Maasai woman is usually good at beadwork and farming.

ev.t: and resisted the urging of the Kenyan and Tanzanian governments to adopt a more modern lifestyle

note: 政府勸他們改採現代的生活方式，換個說法就是要他們拋開傳統。(C) 照抄 kill a lion，但那是取得戰士身分的方法，不是成年的條件，而且原文說直到不久以前才是如此；(B) 照抄 resist，但原文沒說抗拒外來影響是因為曾經淪為奴隸；(D) 照抄 beadwork，務農文章沒提。

to adopt a more modern lifestyle

stem: Which of the following is true about Maasai clothing and beadwork?

options.A: Striped and patterned cloth is preferred by young adults.
options.B: Young men cannot wear black until they become warriors.
options.C: Colorful glass jewelry became popular after the 19th century.
options.D: The color of the shúkà represented one’s importance in the tribe.

ev.t: Natural materials such as clay, shells, and ivory were used before trading with the Europeans in the 19th century.
They were then replaced by colorful glass beads, allowing for more detailed beadwork and color patterns.

note: 19 世紀和歐洲人通商後，天然材料換成彩色玻璃珠，就是彩色玻璃飾品從 19 世紀以後開始流行。(A) 照抄 striped 和 patterned，但原文說偏好這類布料的是女性，不是年輕人；(B) 照抄 black，但年輕男子是行割禮後穿黑色；(D) 照抄 shúkà，原文沒說顏色代表身分地位。

stem: Why does the author quote Blixen’s comment at the end of the third paragraph?

options.A: To explain how Maasai warriors hunt for deer in the wild.
options.B: To exemplify the types of weapons used by Maasai warriors.
options.C: To emphasize that weapons are an inseparable part of a Maasai warrior’s outfit.

note: 有提到的用途在選項都換了說法：第 1 段的 eat it, drink it 是 (C) food and beverage，medicines 是 (A) treating illnesses，shampoos 是 (B) personal hygiene。用來園藝造景，文章沒提。

stem: Which of the following statements about the prickly pear cactus is true?

options.A: Its soft inner part is often discarded.
options.B: It was not discovered until the modern era.
options.C: It turns into 200,000 tons of waste in Mexico each year.
options.D: It appears in a prominent place on Mexico’s national flag.

ev.t: The prickly pear cactus is such a powerful symbol in Mexico that it occupies a prime spot on Mexico’s national flag.

note: prime spot 在選項換成 prominent place。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 soft inner，但丟掉的是外皮，嫩肉一直都在吃；(C) 照抄 200,000 tons，那是每年的產量，每天的廢棄物是 10 噸；(B) 照抄 modern，原文說古代阿茲特克人就把仙人掌視為神聖。

stem: What advantage does the prickly pear cactus have over other biofuel crops?

options.A: It generates more energy.
options.B: It will not influence food prices.
options.C: It may replace feed for livestock.
options.D: It can increase global food production.

ev.t: Therefore, using the plant as a fuel source will not put pressure on food prices.

note: 不會對糧食價格造成壓力，在選項換成不會影響糧食價格。(D) 照抄 food production，但原文說的是不會和糧食生產搶水搶地，不是增加糧食產量。(A) 文章沒有比較仙人掌和其他作物哪個發的電比較多；(C) 文章也沒提到牲畜的飼料，第 4 段說仙人掌的果肉仍然留給人吃。

stem: How is the information in the passage organized?

options.A: In order of time.
options.B: By cause and effect.
options.C: In order of importance.
options.D: By definition and illustration.

note: 全文依時間往下走：西元前 450 年的尼希米、中世紀的伊斯蘭國家和歐洲、15 世紀的亨利五世、一百年後出現 passport 這個詞，到第一次世界大戰，所以是依時間順序排列。交卷後「這一篇的文章結構」也把這篇歸為時序發展。(B) 文章沒有分析護照出現的原因和結果；(C) 各個時期只是依先後排列，沒有比較哪一個比較重要；(D) 第 1 段第一句雖然說明旅行文件是什麼，後面各段卻是依年代往下講，不是舉例說明一個定義。

stem: Which of the following statements is true about the earliest travel document?

options.A: It was issued by the king of Judah.
options.B: It was given to an official of Persia.
options.C: It appeared more than three thousand years ago.
options.D: It served to invite people to travel beyond the river.

ev.t: The Hebrew Bible states that Nehemiah, an official serving King Artaxerxes of ancient Persia, asked permission to travel to Judah.
The King agreed and gave Nehemiah a letter

note: 國王把信交給為古波斯國王效力的官員尼希米。(A) 照抄 Judah，那是尼希米要去的地方，發信的是波斯國王；(D) 照抄 beyond the river，那封信是寫給河那邊的省長，請他們放行，不是邀人去旅行；(C) 西元前 450 年距今大約兩千五百年，不到三千年。
map: an official serving King Artaxerxes of ancient Persia

stem: When did the term “passport” start being used?

options.A: In about 450 B.C.
options.B: During World War I.
options.C: In the 16th century.
options.D: During King Henry V’s reign.

ev.t: The earliest reference to these documents is found in a 15th-century Act of Parliament, while the term “passport” came into use about a century later.

note: 15 世紀的法案再過大約一百年，就是 16 世紀，要自己推算。(D) 照抄 King Henry V，那是發明護照的人，不是這個詞出現的時間；(B) 第一次世界大戰是護照普遍使用的時間；(A) 照抄第 1 段的 450 B.C.。

stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the passage as a form of passport?

options.A: A letter.
options.B: A receipt.
options.C: A proof of identity.
options.D: A list of seaports.

ev.t: The King agreed and gave Nehemiah a letter
Later, in the medieval Islamic Caliphate, a form of passport was the bara’a, a receipt for taxes paid.
and generally contained a list of towns and cities which the document holder was permitted to enter or pass through
as a way of helping his subjects prove who they were in foreign lands

note: 有提到的三種：第 1 段國王的信（(A) letter）、第 2 段的繳稅收據（(B) receipt）、第 3 段亨利五世的護照幫人證明身分（(C) proof of identity）。(D) 把第 2 段的 list 和 seaports 拼在一起：歐洲的文件列的是城鎮，前往海港反而不需要文件。

stem: Which of the following is the closest illustration of Benjamin Franklin’s invention?

options.A: （見圖）
options.B: （見圖）
options.C: （見圖）
options.D: （見圖）

figure.source: 大學入學考試中心 110 學年度學科能力測驗英文考科

ev.t: Franklin ran an iron rod through a hole in the top of each hemisphere so that they could nest together from largest to smallest.
He linked all of this to a device shaped like a spinning wheel, with a foot control that turned the rod, making the glass hemispheres rotate.

note: 要找一根軸串起由大到小的玻璃半球，再接上紡車形狀的輪子和腳踏板，四張圖裡只有 (D) 符合。(A) 是一排玻璃杯，就是富蘭克林原本聽到的玻璃杯樂器；(C) 是紡紗機本身，原文只說裝置的形狀像紡車；(B) 是編鐘。

stem: Which of the following statements is true about how the glass armonica works?

options.A: Water has to be poured into the glass hemispheres.
options.B: Colored paint makes it sound better and last longer.
options.C: An iron rod is used to strike the thicker glass hemispheres.
options.D: The performer’s fingers have to be slightly wet when playing it.

ev.t: Franklin moistened his fingers and held them against the rims of the glass hemispheres as they turned, producing a unique sound.

note: moisten 是把東西弄濕，在選項換成 slightly wet。(A) 第 2 段說弄濕的是演奏者的手指，文章沒有說要把水倒進玻璃半球裡；(B) 照抄 paint，但油漆是用來標示音符；(C) 照抄 iron rod 和 thick，但鐵棒是用來串起半球、帶動旋轉，不是敲打。
map: fingers have to be slightly wet

stem: According to the passage, why did the glass armonica lose its popularity?

options.A: The skill of playing the glass armonica was very hard to master.
options.B: Famous musicians like Beethoven had problems composing for it.
options.C: Concert halls became too big for its music to be heard by the audience.
options.D: Reviewers in that time indicated that it was clumsy and not fashionable.

ev.t: Music was moving out of the relatively small halls of Mozart’s day into the large concert halls of the 19th century, and without amplification, the glass armonica simply couldn’t be heard.

note: 音樂移到 19 世紀的大型音樂廳，沒有擴音就聽不見玻璃琴，這就是不再流行的原因。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 master，但原文說富蘭克林把這種樂器練得很純熟；(D) 照抄 fashion，但評論說的是聲音很美，只是聽不見；(B) 照抄第 1 段的 Beethoven，原文說貝多芬為玻璃琴作過曲。
map: to be heard by the audience

stem: What does the highlighted “they” in the second paragraph refer to?

options.A: Iron rods.
options.B: Hemispheres.
options.C: Colored notes.
options.D: Musical pitches.

ev.t: Franklin ran an iron rod through a hole in the top of each hemisphere so that they could nest together from largest to smallest.

note: 能夠由大到小一個套一個排在一起的，是同一句前面的玻璃半球。(A) 鐵棒只有一根，是用來串起半球的；(C)、(D) 照抄前兩句的 notes 和 pitches，那是半球發出的聲音，不是實物。

stem: What is the passage mainly about?

options.A: The new addition to Morgan’s Wonderland.
options.B: The establishment and features of a special theme park.
options.C: The advanced technological devices in Morgan’s Wonderland.
options.D: The needs of people who suffer from physical and mental disabilities.

note: 第 1 段講建園的緣由，第 2–4 段講樂園的特色和新開的園區，所以全文介紹一座特殊主題樂園的設立和特色。(A) 新園區只講第 4 段，(C) GPS 手環只講第 3 段，都過於狹隘；(D) 身心障礙者的需求範圍比這座樂園大得多，文章也沒有專門討論，太過廣泛。

stem: What does “ultra-accessible” in the second paragraph imply?

options.A: It’s easy for all visitors to use the facilities.
options.B: Admission is free for people young and old.
options.C: Wheelchairs are provided for every featured attraction.
options.D: Morgan’s Wonderland is situated in a convenient location.

ev.t: so that people of all ages and abilities can come together and play in a fun and safe environment
Completely wheelchair-accessible, the park features 25 acres of attractions
The rides are custom-designed to accommodate wheelchair riders so that every family member can enjoy the fun.

note: accessible 是「方便使用、可以到達」，ultra- 是「極度」；後文說全區輪椅都能通行、設施特別設計讓每一位家人都能玩，所以是所有遊客都能輕鬆使用設施。(B) 照抄 Admission，但免費的只有特殊需求的遊客；(C) 照抄 wheelchair，原文說設施能讓輪椅搭乘，沒說每項設施都提供輪椅；(D) 用的是 accessible「交通方便、容易到達」的意思，可是後文講的都是園區裡的設施人人能用，文章沒有談樂園的地點方不方便。
map: every family member can enjoy the fun
easy for all visitors to use the facilities

stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a fun activity in the park?

options.A: Fishing.
options.B: Driving.
options.C: Hiking.
options.D: Picnicking.

ev.t: the park features 25 acres of attractions including rides, playgrounds, a catch-and-release fishing lake, and picnic areas throughout the park
where guests can test their driving skills in sporty vehicles

note: 釣魚湖、測試駕駛技術、野餐區都在第 3 段，在選項換成 (A) Fishing、(B) Driving、(D) Picnicking。健行文章沒提。

stem: Which of the following statements is true about Morgan’s Wonderland?

options.A: Waterproof chairs enable visitors to roam all over the park.
options.B: Morgan’s Inspiration Island includes 25 acres of attractions.
options.C: The success of the park is exactly what Morgan intended to achieve.
options.D: GPS bands allow visitors to enjoy the convenience of the electronic devices.

ev.t: Moreover, each visitor is offered the option to wear a GPS Adventure Band, which allows them to keep track of each other while in the park.
The band also enables them to take part in electronic activities.

note: GPS 手環能掌握彼此的位置，也能參加電子互動活動，就是讓遊客享受電子裝置的便利。(A) 照抄 waterproof chairs，但防水椅只用在戲水區；(B) 照抄 25 acres，那是整座樂園的面積，不是靈感島；(C) 文章只說建園的靈感來自 Morgan，沒說這是 Morgan 想要達成的。
map: enables them to take part in electronic activities
enjoy the convenience of the electronic devices

stem: Which culture most likely created the sandals shown in the picture?

options.A: Indian.
options.B: Greek.
options.C: Mesopotamian.
options.D: Roman.

figure.source: 大學入學考試中心 109 學年度學科能力測驗英文考科

ev.t: In the Greek version, the toe strap ran between the first and second toes, while Roman sandals had the strap between the second and third toes.

note: 圖裡的帶子夾在第二趾和第三趾之間，對照第 2 段，是羅馬式的涼鞋。這一題要把文字描述轉成圖像，三個錯誤選項都是同一段列出的其他文化：(A) 印度的「趾鈕」涼鞋在大拇趾和第二趾之間是一個鈕，不是帶子；(B) 希臘式的帶子在大拇趾和第二趾之間；(C) 美索不達米亞人的帶子在第三趾和第四趾之間。

stem: Why is the footwear discussed in the passage called “flip-flop”?

options.A: Because of the noise it makes.
options.B: Because of its changeable design.
options.C: Because of its simple structure.
options.D: Because of the comfort of wearing it.

ev.t: The name comes from the sound the sandals make when they slap the walking feet.

note: 名稱來自走路時發出的聲音，sound 在選項換成 noise。(C) 的 simple 取自第 1 段開頭 the simplest shoe，但那一句講的是鞋子的樣子，不是名稱的由來。(B) 第 4 段說人字拖後來重新設計，但那是傳到美國以後的事，和名稱無關；(D) 第 4 段說人字拖一直受歡迎是因為方便，講的是受歡迎的原因，文章也沒有談穿起來舒不舒服。

stem: Which of the following is true about the modern development of the flip-flop?

options.A: Modern flip-flops originated from Indian toe knob sandals.
options.B: Americans loved the Japanese flip-flop because of its bright colors.
options.C: Rubber became the major material of the flip-flop before World War II.
options.D: The sandals American soldiers brought home from Japan later became modern flip-flops.

ev.t: Modern flip-flops derive from Japanese zōris
In the 1950s, flip-flops became popular in the United States as soldiers returning from occupied Japan brought zōris home.

note: 第 3 段說現代人字拖源自日本草履，第 4 段說美國士兵把草履從日本帶回家，兩段合起來就是 (D)。(A) 的 toe knob 在第 2 段，和現代人字拖無關；(B) 鮮豔的顏色是後來重新設計才有的，不是美國人喜歡的原因；(C) 橡膠是戰後才取代稻草。
map: soldiers returning from occupied Japan brought zōris home
American soldiers brought home from Japan
Modern flip-flops derive from Japanese zōris

stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a concern of wearing the flip-flop?

options.A: Personal health.
options.B: Poor quality.
options.C: Social appropriateness.
options.D: Marine pollution.

ev.t: Their simple design is responsible for many foot injuries.
Another issue is the suitability of exposing feet on the street and places other than the beach.
Millions of plastic discards end up in landfills or the ocean, releasing chemicals and at the same time taking centuries to decompose.

note: 第 5 段提到三個問題，在選項裡都換了說法：foot injuries 是 (A) Personal health，suitability 是 (C) Social appropriateness，plastic discards end up in the ocean 是 (D) Marine pollution。只有 (B) 品質不好文章沒提。

stem: What is the passage mainly about?

options.A: A special profession.
options.B: Shipping and trading.
options.C: Guidelines for safe docking.
options.D: Protection of the marine environment.

note: 第 1 段引出引水人這個職業，第 2–3 段說這份工作為什麼需要、難在哪裡，第 4 段總結這份工作的要求和責任，所以全文介紹的是一種特殊的職業。(B) 航運與貿易是第 1 段開頭的引子，範圍比引水人大得多，太過廣泛；(C) 船隻靠港的難處只在第 2、3 段，文章也沒有列出什麼準則，(D) 海洋環境的保護只在第 2 段和第 4 段末尾帶到，兩個都過於狹隘。

stem: Which of the following is part of the knowledge that a marine pilot must have?

options.A: The value of the ships.
options.B: The content of the cargo.
options.C: The weather conditions.
options.D: The diversity of marine life.

ev.t: In addition to the shallower seabeds, tide and wind pose further challenges for bringing ships into a port.
controls the vessel based on his or her knowledge of the port and the situation at hand

note: 第 3 段說潮汐和風會改變船的方向，第 4 段說引水人要依當下的狀況操控船隻，所以天氣狀況是必備的知識，原文的 wind 在選項換成概括的 weather conditions。(B) 的 cargo 取自第 2 段，那裡講的是擱淺時貨物會受損，不是引水人要懂貨物內容。(A) 文章沒有提到船的價值；(D) 第 4 段說引水人要保護海洋環境，這是職責，文章沒有說引水人要懂海洋生物的多樣性。

stem: What does “a crucial time” in the last paragraph refer to?

options.A: When the vessel hits a flat.
options.B: When the channel is not deep enough.
options.C: When there is a collision of two ships.
options.D: When a ship is waiting to enter the port.

ev.t: But the captain of a ship is responsible for guiding the vessel until they hit a port, waiting to enter the harbor.
A marine pilot goes on board at a crucial time

note: 第 1 段說船長把船開到港口、等候進港時，就換引水人接手，這正是引水人登船的關鍵時刻；harbor 在選項換成 port。(B) 的 channel 取自第 2 段，講的是港口的地形，不是登船的時間點。(A) 的 hit 照抄第 1 段 until they hit a port，flat 是淺灘，船撞上淺灘就是第 2 段說的擱淺，那是引水人要避免的意外，不是引水人登船的時候；(C) 文章沒有提到兩艘船相撞。

stem: How does the author conclude the passage in the last paragraph?

options.A: By adding new details.
options.B: By predicting future development.
options.C: By summarizing the main points.
options.D: By giving advice to the general public.

ev.t: Marine pilotage is a job that requires a high degree of proficiency as well as quick and independent thinking.
The pilot is responsible for not only the safety of the ship but also the protection of the port and the marine environment.

note: 末段把前面講過的內容再收一次：專業知識對應第 2 段，迅速獨立的判斷對應第 3 段的潮汐和風，船和海洋環境的安全對應第 2 段的擱淺與貨物外洩，所以是總結重點。(A) 末段沒有新的細節；(B) 末段沒有談未來的發展；(D) 末段講的是引水人的職責，沒有給一般大眾任何建議。

stem: What is the passage mainly about?

options.A: The flavor of olive oil.
options.B: The trade of olive oil.
options.C: The promotion of olive oil.
options.D: The quality of olive oil.

note: 第 1 段講橄欖油的等級，第 2 段講包裝和保存對品質的影響，第 3 段講國際橄欖油理事會想改進檢驗方法，三段都繞著橄欖油的品質，所以答案是 (D)。(A) 風味只在第 1 段談特級初榨的條件時提到，(B) 貿易、(C) 推廣都只出現在第 3 段最後一句，三個錯誤選項都過於狹隘。

stem: Which of the following statements is true about extra virgin olive oil?

options.A: It is free from any bitter flavor.
options.B: It is refined to remove its impurities.
options.C: It requires mixing of more than one kind of oil.
options.D: It has a lower acidity rate than virgin olive oil.

ev.t: Extra virgin oil, the finest grade, is made from the first pressing of the olives and has a very low acidity rate (under 1%).
It is also a first pressing, but has a slightly higher acidity level (under 2%).

note: 第 1 段說特級初榨的酸度低於 1%，初榨橄欖油的酸度略高、低於 2%，反過來說，就是特級初榨的酸度比初榨低。(A) 照抄 bitter flavor，原文說特級初榨要有討喜的苦味，不是沒有苦味；(B) 照抄 remove its impurities，那是精製橄欖油的做法；(C) 把幾種油調和在一起，說的也是精製橄欖油（blended），不是特級初榨。

stem: According to the passage, what is the best way to store olive oil?

options.A: In a plastic container in a damp cellar.
options.B: In a clear glass bottle near the kitchen stove.
options.C: In an airtight glass bottle in a kitchen cupboard.
options.D: In an airproof bottle next to a well-lighted window.

ev.t: Olive oil spoils quickly when exposed to direct sunlight, so it should be stored in the dark at 16-18°C.
Moisture and oxygen promote oxidation and therefore limit its shelf life.

note: 第 2 段說橄欖油要避光、存放在 16 至 18°C，濕氣和氧氣會加速氧化，塑膠容器也不適合。放在廚房櫥櫃裡的密封玻璃瓶，可以避光、隔絕空氣，溫度也不會太高，所以選 (C)。(A) 照抄 plastic container，原文正好說塑膠容器擋不住光、熱和濕氣，潮濕的地窖也不行；(B) 透明玻璃瓶擋不住光，放在爐子旁邊又太熱；(D) 窗邊光線充足，油很快就會變質。

stem: What is the IOC trying to do?

options.A: Train more qualified olive oil tasters.
options.B: Improve the ways of grading olive oil.
options.C: Look for new techniques to boost production.
options.D: Build better connections among industry members.

ev.t: Recently, however, the International Olive Council (IOC) is seeking input on test methods to improve the transparency of the testing process and boost the accuracy of the results.

note: 第 3 段說 IOC 正在徵詢對檢驗方法的意見，要讓檢驗更透明、結果更準確，也就是改進評定橄欖油等級的方式；test methods 在選項換成 ways of grading。(C) 照抄 boost，原文提升的是檢驗結果的準確性，不是產量；(D) 照抄 industry members，原文說業界成員希望藉此促進貿易，沒有說要加強彼此的聯繫；(A) 照抄 tasters，原文只說品油師一向用描述性的字眼評定品質，沒有說要訓練更多品油師。

stem: Why are deer attracted to train tracks?

options.A: They mate at night near railways.
options.B: They need nutrition from train tracks.
options.C: They like to snort at the passing train.
options.D: They sharpen their horns rubbing against the rails.

ev.t: Deer are attracted to railway lines because of a need for iron in their diets.
They lick the rails to pick up iron filings caused by the action of wheels against tracks.

note: 第 3 段第一句說鹿的飲食需要鐵質，下一句說牠們舔鐵軌上的鐵屑；選項把 a need for iron 換成 need nutrition。(D) 照抄 rails，原文是舔鐵軌，不是在鐵軌上磨角；(C) 照抄第 4 段的 snort，那是鹿察覺危險時警告同伴的叫聲，和鹿靠近鐵軌的原因無關；(A) 夜間交配，文章沒有提。
map: a need for iron in their diets

stem: What device has NOT been used to solve the railway problem in Japan?

options.A: Flashing lights.
options.B: Barking speakers.
options.C: Noisy train tracks.
options.D: Lion face paintings.

ev.t: Researchers in Japan have installed on a train a speaker that barks like a dog and snorts like a deer in order to prevent collisions with animals on the tracks.
In the past, flashing red lights and even lion faces have been unsuccessfully trialed in an attempt to keep deer off the tracks.

note: 三個有提到的裝置都換了說法：第 3 段的 flashing red lights 是 (A) Flashing lights，lion faces 是 (D) Lion face paintings；第 1 段裝在火車上、會學狗叫的 speaker 是 (B) Barking speakers。文章沒有提到會發出噪音的鐵軌，所以選 (C)。

stem: Which of the following is true about the deer issue discussed in the passage?

options.A: RTRI’s new invention prompts deer to run away.
options.B: People living near the tracks complain about deer snorts.
options.C: 45 percent of train delays in Japan was caused by deer collision.
options.D: A combination of sound and visual devices attracts more deer to the tracks.

ev.t: When the deer hear a combination of a 3-second-long recording of a deer’s snort and 20 seconds of a barking dog, they panic and flee rapidly.

note: 第 4 段說鹿聽到 3 秒的鹿鳴錄音加上 20 秒的狗吠，就會驚慌逃走；flee rapidly 在選項換成 run away。(C) 照抄第 5 段的 45 percent，原文說的是測試後看到鹿的次數減少 45%，不是火車延誤有 45% 是撞鹿造成的；(D) 照抄第 4 段的 combination，原文組合的是兩種聲音，而且是要把鹿趕走，不是吸引鹿；(B) 照抄 snort，第 5 段只說有住家的地區不會播放這些聲音，沒有說居民抱怨。

stem: What does the author mean by “the unforgiving nature of tons of onrushing rolling stock” in the third paragraph?

options.A: The heavy weight of iron materials.
options.B: The cruelty of a barking hound.
options.C: The battle between deer and other animals.
options.D: The danger of a fast-moving train.

ev.t: This dietary need has led to a constant battle to keep the deer separate from the unforgiving nature of tons of onrushing rolling stock.

note: rolling stock 指鐵路上的車輛，tons of onrushing 是重達數噸、迎面疾駛而來，unforgiving 是毫不留情，整個詞組說的就是高速行駛的火車有多危險。(C) 照抄同一句的 battle，原文是人想讓鹿遠離火車的長期抗戰，不是鹿和其他動物之間的戰鬥；(A) 照抄 iron，鐵質是鹿想吃的東西，不是這個詞組的意思；(B) 狗吠是第 4 段的新裝置，和這裡無關。

stem: What is the job of an angelfish in the sea?

options.A: Being a cleaner for other fish.
options.B: Being a bodyguard for other fish.
options.C: Being a gardener for roots and plants.
options.D: Being a caretaker for sponge and algae.

ev.t: Most of them act as cleaners for other fish and pick dead tissue from their bodies.

note: 第 2 段說大部分的神仙魚替其他魚當清潔工，啄掉牠們身上的死皮，選項幾乎照用原字。(C) 照抄第 1 段的 roots and plants，原文說神仙魚躲在樹根和植物之間避開危險，不是照顧植物；(D) 照抄 sponge and algae，那是神仙魚的食物，不是牠們照顧的對象；(B) 保護群體的「守衛」是第 3 段的雄魚，不是神仙魚替其他魚做的工作。

stem: Which of the following statements is true about the color of angelfish?

options.A: Female angelfish are blue in color.
options.B: The colors of the fish become less bright at night.
options.C: Male angelfish do not have black stripes on them.
options.D: The adult fish and the young ones have the same colors.

ev.t: At night, when these fish become inactive, their colors may become pale.

note: 第 1 段說神仙魚晚上不活動時，顏色可能會變淡；選項把 become pale 換成 become less bright。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 blue in color，但藍色的是雄魚，雌魚是黃色；(C) 照抄 black stripes，原文說黑色條紋出現就表示已經變成雄魚，正好相反；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 young ones，原文說幼魚和成魚的顏色常常不同。

stem: According to the passage, what triggers the gender change in the blackspot angelfish?

options.A: Dangers to the group.
options.B: Changes in the fish’s diet.
options.C: The birth of young angelfish.
options.D: The death of the male fish in a group.

ev.t: When the male dies, the group needs a new “security guard.”
This is when the largest female in the group begins to change in appearance.

note: 第 3 段說雄魚死掉之後，群體需要新的守衛，這時最大的雌魚就開始改變；the male dies 在選項換成 the death of the male fish。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 danger，原文說的是花紋幫助神仙魚躲避危險，和變性無關；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 diet，(C) 照抄第 1 段的 young，文章都沒有說這兩件事會引發變性。

stem: Which of the following describes the order of changes in the features of a blackspot angelfish during gender change?

options.A: Size → behavior → color → stripes.
options.B: Color → size → behavior → stripes.
options.C: Size → color → behavior → stripes.
options.D: Color → behavior → size → stripes.

ev.t: She begins to grow larger in size, and after a week, she starts changing color, from yellow to blue.
Slowly, her behavior toward the other fish also changes.
Two weeks later, black stripes appear on her body, indicating the gender change is complete.

note: 第 3 段依序寫出四個變化：先是體型變大（size），一週後變色（color），接著對其他魚的行為慢慢改變（behavior），兩週後出現黑色條紋（stripes）。after a week、Slowly、Two weeks later 這幾個表示先後的字詞標出了順序，所以是 (C)。(A) 把行為排在變色之前，可是變色是一週後，行為的改變在變色之後才慢慢出現；(B)、(D) 都從變色開始，可是原文先寫體型變大，一週後才變色，(D) 還把體型排到行為之後。

stem: Which of the following is the best title for this passage?

options.A: Totem Poles, the Legends of Aboriginal Peoples
options.B: Totem Poles: Their Functions
options.C: Totem Poles, Symbols of Historical Resistance
options.D: Totem Poles: Their Designs

note: 第 1 段說圖騰柱不只是藝術品，也是講述家族故事的方式；第 2–4 段依位置和用途，介紹迎賓柱、屋柱、紀念柱、墓葬柱和羞辱柱各有什麼作用，所以最好的標題是圖騰柱的功能。(D) 柱子的雕刻和色彩只在第 1 段帶到，(C) 抵抗殖民勢力只在第 5 段提到，都過於狹隘；(A) 圖騰柱記錄的是家族和氏族的歷史，文章沒有談原住民的傳說，偏離主題。

stem: How is the information about totem poles organized in Paragraphs 2 to 4?

options.A: In order of importance.
options.B: In order of time.
options.C: By cause and effect.
options.D: By classification.

note: 第 2 段一開頭就說圖騰柱可以依位置和場合分成幾類（can be grouped into specific categories），接著第 2 到 4 段逐一介紹迎賓柱、屋柱、紀念柱、墓葬柱和羞辱柱，所以是分類。交卷後「這一篇的文章結構」也把這篇歸為分類。(A) 文章沒有比較哪一種圖騰柱比較重要；(B) 各種柱子是依類別介紹，不是依出現的先後；(C) 文章說明各種柱子立在哪裡、為什麼而刻，但沒有把一件事當成原因、另一件事當成結果來推論。

stem: Which of the following is located at the edge of a body of water?

options.A: The house pole.
options.B: The shame pole.
options.C: The memorial pole.
options.D: The welcome pole.

ev.t: Welcome poles were traditionally placed on village beachfronts to greet visitors arriving by canoe.

note: 題幹的 at the edge of a body of water（水邊），是第 2 段 beachfronts（海灘邊）的換句話說；立在海灘邊、迎接划獨木舟來訪客人的是迎賓柱。(A) 屋柱在酋長家中，(C) 紀念柱立在房屋前面，(B) 羞辱柱現在只在博物館裡，都不在水邊。

stem: Which is closest in meaning to the word “encroachment” in the last paragraph?

options.A: Invasion.
options.B: Appointment.
options.C: Objection.
options.D: Enrichment.

ev.t: Despite the threats posed by cultural and political encroachment of colonial forces, the art of totem pole carving has survived.

note: Despite 表示讓步：儘管殖民勢力帶來威脅，雕刻藝術仍然流傳下來。會對原住民文化構成威脅的，是殖民勢力在文化和政治上的侵逼，所以 encroachment 最接近 invasion（侵略、侵入）。(D) enrichment 是使豐富，方向正好相反；(B) 任命、(C) 反對都談不上威脅。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about an earworm?

options.A: It is a creature living inside our ears.
options.B: It is a tune memorized in a personal way.
options.C: It is a melody repeating in our heads.
options.D: It is a commercial recalled through lyrics.

ev.t: Sometimes a tune intrudes on our thoughts and then plays, and replays, in a never-ending loop.
As the melody repeats, it becomes embedded into our mind.

note: 第 1 段說一段旋律闖進思緒後不停重播，旋律一再重複就嵌進腦海；選項的 a melody repeating in our heads 說的就是這件事。(A) 照抄 ears，原文說的是耳朵沒聽到、大腦還在播放，earworm 不是真的蟲；(D) 照抄第 2 段的 commercial，廣告歌曲只是容易變成耳蟲的一種歌；(B) 第 2 段說每個人都有自己的耳蟲歌，但沒有說耳蟲是用個人方式記住的旋律。

stem: Which of the following best defines “subject” in the first paragraph?

options.A: A kind of mental disease.
options.B: A course being taken.
options.C: A participant in an experiment.
options.D: A matter being studied.

ev.t: This interesting phenomenon becomes a subject explored by many scientists.

note: subject 有好幾個意思：學科、受試者、主題。這一句說這個現象成了許多科學家探究（explored）的 subject，所以是研究的主題，也就是 a matter being studied。(B) 課程、(C) 實驗的受試者，都是 subject 的其他常見意思，放進這一句說不通；(A) 文章說的是一種常見的現象，不是精神疾病。

stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a feature that would trigger earworms?

options.A: Tunes repeatedly encountered.
options.B: Melodies with smooth rhythms.
options.C: Fragments of songs recently heard.
options.D: Words similar to the lyrics of a song.

ev.t: Often those songs have a simple, upbeat melody and catchy, repetitive lyrics, such as popular commercial jingles and slightly annoying radio hits.
Recent or repeated exposure to a song or even a small part of a song can also trigger earworms, as can word associations, such as a phrase similar to the lyrics of a song.

note: 三個有提到的都換了說法：第 2 段的 repeated exposure to a song 是 (A) Tunes repeatedly encountered，recent exposure to a small part of a song 是 (C) Fragments of songs recently heard，a phrase similar to the lyrics of a song 是 (D) Words similar to the lyrics of a song。原文說的是 simple, upbeat melody（簡單輕快的旋律），沒有提到節奏流暢，所以選 (B)。

stem: What is the third paragraph mainly about?

options.A: Why people find earworms annoying.
options.B: How people react to earworms.
options.C: What people use to kill earworms.
options.D: When people start to notice earworms.

ev.t: How people cope with their earworms seems to depend on how they feel about them.

note: 第 3 段先說多數人覺得耳蟲愉快或無所謂，接著點出重點：人們怎麼應付耳蟲，取決於他們對耳蟲的感受，再分別說明有正面、負面感受的人怎麼做，所以這一段講的是人們對耳蟲的反應；cope with 在選項換成 react to。(A) 照抄 annoying，但這一段說的是大多數人並不覺得煩；(C) 唱歌、說話、祈禱只是部分人應付耳蟲的方法，原文沒說要消滅耳蟲；(D) 什麼時候開始注意到耳蟲，這一段沒有提。

stem: What is this passage mainly about?

options.A: Steps to get rid of bedbugs.
options.B: Ways to use foggers correctly.
options.C: The ineffectiveness of bug bombs.
options.D: The problems caused by insects.

note: 第 1 段說除蟲彈的效果和一般人想的正好相反，第 2 段用研究證明除蟲彈對床蝨幾乎無效，第 3 段再說除蟲彈有起火和危害健康的風險，應該是最後的手段，所以全文講的是除蟲彈沒有用。(D) 蟲咬造成皮膚起疹子只在第 1 段開頭帶到，過於狹隘；(A) 文章沒有教人怎麼一步一步消滅床蝨，只建議交給專業人員，(B) 文章也沒有說明除蟲彈的正確用法，這兩個選項都偏離主題。

stem: How do bedbugs react to foggers?

options.A: They remain motionless.
options.B: They retreat to safe places.
options.C: They stop biting people.
options.D: They escape into another house.

ev.t: Once the pests detect the chemical fog in the room, they’ll hide themselves in walls or other hideaways, where you’ll never be able to treat them effectively.

note: 第 1 段說害蟲一察覺室內的藥霧，就會躲進牆壁或其他藏身處；選項把 hide themselves in walls or other hideaways 換成 retreat to safe places。(D) 原文說牠們躲進牆裡和其他藏身處，沒說逃到別人家；(A) 一動也不動、(C) 停止咬人，文章都沒有提。
map: hide themselves in walls or other hideaways

stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements about foggers is true?

options.A: They can cause a fire.
options.B: They do not stay on furniture.
options.C: They can kill most insects.
options.D: They do not contain chemicals.

ev.t: First of all, the gases used in bug bombs are highly flammable and thus pose a serious risk of fire or explosion if the product is not used properly.

note: 第 3 段說除蟲彈的氣體非常易燃，使用不當有起火或爆炸的嚴重危險；選項把 pose a serious risk of fire 換成 can cause a fire。(B) 照抄 furniture，原文正好說藥劑會落在家具上、留下有毒物質；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 chemical，原文說除蟲彈放出的就是化學藥霧；(C) 照抄 insects，第 2 段的研究卻發現除蟲彈對床蝨幾乎沒有效果。
map: pose a serious risk of fire

stem: What does the author advise people to do with bedbug problems?

options.A: Choose the right fogger.
options.B: Clean the house regularly.
options.C: Close the doors when using pesticides.
options.D: Consult a pest-control expert.

ev.t: Therefore, it is suggested that people leave the problem to the professionals.

note: 第 3 段最後一句建議大家把問題交給專業人員處理；the professionals 在選項換成 a pest-control expert（除蟲專家）。(C) 照抄 pesticide，文章沒有教人使用殺蟲劑時要關門；(A) 文章說除蟲彈應該是最後的手段，沒有教人挑選除蟲彈；(B) 定期打掃房子，文章沒有提。

stem: What is the main idea of this passage?

options.A: Treatments do not always cause harmful side effects.
options.B: Patients tend to believe more testing is better treatment.
options.C: Too much medical care may not be beneficial to patients.
options.D: Doctors generally recommend office visits that are necessary.

note: 第 1 段開門見山：很多人相信醫療越多越好，但過度醫療可能造成傷害；第 2、3 段用 Power 太太的例子說明，太多檢查讓她身心受苦、幾乎破產，停掉例行檢查後病情反而穩定。全文要說的是太多醫療對病人未必有益，所以是 (C)。(B) 病人相信檢查越多越好，只是第 1 段第一句的說法，過於狹隘；(A) 說治療不一定有副作用、(D) 說醫生通常只建議必要的回診，都和文章的立場相反，偏離主題。

stem: Which of the following was a problem for Mrs. Power during her medical treatment?

options.A: She had to be hospitalized for three weeks whenever she had a cold.
options.B: She didn’t have any insurance, so she went broke because of her illness.
options.C: When test results showed she was fine, her doctor still ordered more tests.
options.D: Her doctor asked her to consult other specialists due to her constant complaints.

ev.t: Even when tests came back negative, more were ordered,

note: 第 2 段說就算檢查結果正常（tests came back negative），醫生還是安排更多檢查，選項換成 test results showed she was fine 和 still ordered more tests。(A) 照抄 three weeks，原文說每三週回診一次，感冒住院是為了預防萬一，沒說住院三週；(D) 照抄 specialists，原文說連小毛病（minor complaints）也轉診，不是因為她一直抱怨；(B) 原文說醫療費用讓這對夫妻幾乎破產，沒提到有沒有保險。
map: test results showed she was fine

stem: Who does “they” in the third paragraph most likely refer to?

options.A: Physicians.
options.B: Other patients.
options.C: Mr. and Mrs. Power.
options.D: The online support groups.

ev.t: “It’s a really hard thing to determine when they’ve crossed the line,” Mr. Power said.

note: they 出現在 Power 先生說的話裡：很難判斷 they 什麼時候越過了界線（crossed the line）。第 2 段一路寫的是醫生堅持回診、一再安排檢查和轉診，做得太多、越過界線的是醫生，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄前一句的 other patients，(D) 照抄 online support groups，這對夫妻是和其他病友交流之後才開始質疑，病友和互助團體不是安排檢查的人；(C) Power 夫婦是承受過度醫療的一方。

stem: Which of the following best describes the author’s attitude toward medical tests?

options.A: More tests than necessary are too much.
options.B: Medical tests are essential for disease prevention.
options.C: Many tests are needed for confirmation of diagnosis.
options.D: Doctors’ interpretations of test results are seldom wrong.

note: 第 1 段說過度醫療（太多掃描、太多抽血、太多醫療程序）可能造成傷害，一項檢查常會引出更多檢查；Power 太太的例子也說明檢查做得太多反而傷身又傷財，停掉例行檢查後病情穩定。作者認為超過需要的檢查就是太多了，所以是 (A)。(B)、(C) 強調檢查必要，和作者的立場相反；(D) 文章沒有談醫生判讀檢查結果準不準。

stem: What does the word “cash-strapped” in the second paragraph mean?

options.A: Making a lot of money.
options.B: Being short of money.
options.C: Being careful with money.
options.D: Spending little money.

ev.t: Perhaps the most striking thing about MOOCs, many of which are being taught by professors at prestigious universities, is that they’re free.
This is certainly good news for cash-strapped students.

note: 第 2 段說 MOOC 最引人注目的地方或許是免費，接著說這對 cash-strapped 學生當然是好消息。課程免費，最高興的會是缺錢的學生，所以 cash-strapped 是手頭很緊、缺錢，最接近 (B) Being short of money。(A) 賺很多錢，和「免費課程是好消息」接不上；(C) 用錢謹慎、(D) 花錢很少，說的是花錢的習慣，不是手頭缺錢。

stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the features of MOOCs?

options.A: It is free to take the courses.
options.B: Many courses are offered by famous universities.
options.C: Most courses address artificial intelligence.
options.D: Many students can take the course at the same time.

ev.t: Since the courses can be taken by hundreds of thousands of students at the same time,
many of which are being taught by professors at prestigious universities
is that they’re free.

note: 文章提到的三個特色在選項都換了說法：第 2 段說 MOOC 最引人注目的是免費（they’re free），是 (A)；許多課程由知名大學的教授授課（professors at prestigious universities），是 (B)；一門課可以同時讓數十萬名學生修讀，是 (D)。人工智慧只是 Thrun 教授開的那一門課，文章沒說大部分的課程都在講人工智慧，所以選 (C)。

stem: What is the second paragraph mainly about?

options.A: The impact of MOOCs.
options.B: The goal of MOOCs.
options.C: The size of MOOC classes.
options.D: The cost of MOOC courses.

ev.t: This new breed of online classes is shaking up the higher education world in many ways.

note: 第 2 段先說 MOOC 在 2011 年引起轟動，接著用 This new breed of online classes is shaking up the higher education world in many ways 點出重點：這種課程在許多方面撼動高等教育界。後面說的大學數量可能大減、全世界只需要 10 所大學、免費對手頭很緊的學生是好消息，都是它帶來的影響，所以是 (A)。(C) 課程規模和 (D) 費用都只是這一段用來說明影響的細節；(B) 目標是第 1 段的內容。

stem: Which of the following is mentioned in the passage as a problem of MOOCs?

Some critics worry that online students will miss out on the social aspects of college.

note: 第 3 段批評者說教授和學生之間真正的對話無可取代，也擔心線上學生會錯過大學的社交生活（social aspects of college），選項換成 lack of social interaction among students and professors。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 traditional course materials，原文說 MOOC 除了傳統教材之外還有論壇，教材並沒有消失；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 prestigious universities，知名大學的教授授課是 MOOC 的特色，不是問題；(B) 文章沒說課程數量有限，第 2 段說可能減少的是大學的數量。

stem: What is this article mainly about?

options.A: Why people are moving away from their own countries.
options.B: Why there are civil wars and violence in the Middle East.
options.C: Why many schools have become shelters for displaced families.
options.D: Why many children in the Middle East are not attending school.

note: 第 1 段開頭就說中東的衝突使超過 1,300 萬名兒童無法上學；第 2 段說明兩個原因：學校建築毀損、人口流離失所；第 3 段以敘利亞為例；第 4 段呼籲國際提供資源。全文要回答的是為什麼許多中東兒童沒有上學，所以是 (D)。(A) 人口遷離家園和 (C) 學校變成收容所，都只是第 2 段說明的原因，過於狹隘；(B) 文章沒有分析內戰和暴力為什麼發生，偏離主題。

stem: Why is “Iraq” mentioned in the second paragraph?

options.A: To convince people that temporary housing can be easily found.
options.B: To prove that classrooms there are big enough to host many families.
options.C: To give an example of why schools are not usable for children’s learning.
options.D: To show how structural damages of school can affect the quality of education.

ev.t: Across these countries, violence has made 8,500 schools unusable.
In certain cases, communities have relied on school buildings to function as shelters for the displaced, with up to nine families living in a single classroom in former schools across Iraq.

note: 第 2 段先說暴力使 8,500 所學校無法使用（unusable），接著用 In certain cases 帶出伊拉克的例子：學校成了收容所，一間教室住到九戶人家。提到伊拉克，是為了舉例說明學校為什麼不能用來上課，選項把 unusable 換成 not usable。(D) 照抄 structural damage，但伊拉克的例子說的是學校拿來安置流離失所的人，不是建築毀損，教育品質是第 3 段講敘利亞時才提到；(B) 照抄 families，一間教室住九戶人家是說擁擠，不是說教室夠大；(A) 文章沒說臨時住處很容易找到。

stem: What does the phrase “in the balance” in the last paragraph most likely mean?

options.A: Being well taken care of.
options.B: In an uncertain situation.
options.C: Under control by the authority.
options.D: Moving in the wrong direction.

ev.t: With more than 13 million children already driven from classrooms by conflict, it is no exaggeration to say that the educational prospects of a generation of children are in the balance.

note: 第 4 段說已經有超過 1,300 萬名兒童因為衝突離開教室，說一整個世代兒童的教育前景 in the balance 一點也不誇張。這麼多孩子失學，他們的教育前景會怎麼樣還說不定，in the balance 就是懸而未決、岌岌可危，最接近 (B) 處於不確定的狀況。(A) 得到妥善照顧、(C) 由當局控制，都和失學的處境不合；(D) 往錯誤的方向走，是把前景當成已經確定變壞，原文說的是結果還未定。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?

ev.t: The report pays particularly close attention to Syria, where a bloody civil war has displaced at least nine million people since the war began in 2011.

note: 第 3 段說敘利亞的血腥內戰從 2011 年開始，選項把 since the war began in 2011 換成 has been going on since 2011。(B) 照抄 nine，原文的 nine 是九百萬人流離失所和九個國家，無法使用的學校是 8,500 所，不到九千所；(C) 照抄第 2 段 forced migration 的 forced，1,300 萬是無法上學的兒童人數，不是離開家園的人數；(D) 40% 指的是中東地區的兒童，不是全世界的兒童。

stem: Which of the following is true about Homer’s career?

options.A: He achieved international fame with his vivid paintings of England.

options.D: He first established his reputation as an illustrator in his hometown of Boston.

ev.t: Born and raised in Boston, he began his career at age eighteen in his hometown, working as an apprentice at a printing company.
Skilled at drawing, he soon made a name for himself making illustrations for novels, sheet music, magazines, and children’s books.

note: 第 1 段說霍默在家鄉波士頓的印刷公司當學徒，很快就以繪製插畫出名（made a name for himself），選項換成 established his reputation as an illustrator。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 England，但讓他贏得國際肯定的是描繪北軍的畫作，不是描繪英國的畫；(B) 照抄 greatest，原文說他是最偉大的畫家（painter），不是最偉大的插畫家；(C) 照抄第 3 段的 watercolor，原文說他的插畫、油畫和水彩都同樣出色（excelled equally），沒說水彩比較有名。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following best characterizes Homer’s art?

options.A: His pictures vividly portrayed the life of nineteenth-century Americans.
options.B: His art thoughtfully expressed the voices of people suffering from war.
options.C: His style faithfully conformed to the artistic traditions of his time.
options.D: His paintings constantly reflected his desire to escape from society.

ev.t: Many of his works—depictions of children at play and in school, farm girls attending to their work, hunters and their prey—have become classic images of nineteenth-century American life.

note: 第 3 段說霍默的許多作品，像是孩子遊戲和上學、農家女孩工作、獵人和獵物，都成了 19 世紀美國生活的經典畫面，選項把 classic images of nineteenth-century American life 換成 vividly portrayed the life of nineteenth-century Americans。(B) 照抄 thoughtful，原文說他的作品表達深刻，沒說是替受戰爭之苦的人發聲；(C) 照抄 artistic，原文說他不受藝術傳統束縛（independence from artistic conventions），選項說他遵循傳統，方向正好相反；(D) 文章沒說他想逃離社會。

stem: What does “Others” in the third paragraph refer to?

options.A: Other artists.
options.B: Other themes.
options.C: Other works.
options.D: Other images.

ev.t: Many of his works
Others speak to more universal themes such as the primal relationship of humans to nature.

note: 第 3 段先說他的許多作品（Many of his works）成了美國生活的經典畫面，下一句接著說 Others 觸及更普遍的主題。Many of his works…Others… 前後對照，Others 是他的其他作品，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄 themes，主題是這些作品觸及的內容，不是 Others 本身；(D) 照抄 images，經典畫面是前一句對那批作品的評價；(A) 這一段沒有提到其他藝術家。

note: 第 1 段講白宮的興建：選址、設計比賽、動工到第一批住戶入住；第 2 段講歷任總統怎麼開放白宮、接待民眾；第 3 段講白宮名稱的演變。三段都是白宮兩百多年來發生的事，所以是白宮的歷史。(A) 設計和 (B) 位置都只在第 1 段帶到，過於狹隘；(C) 第 1 段第一句說白宮是總統、政府和人民的象徵，但全文沒有討論白宮為什麼重要，偏離主題。

stem: What does “this practice” refer to in the second paragraph?

ev.t: Thomas Jefferson held the first inaugural open house in 1805;
Abraham Lincoln did the same, but then the inaugural crowds became far too large for the White House to accommodate comfortably, and this also created a security issue.

note: this practice 指的是前面那個帶來人潮問題的做法：第 2 段說傑佛遜在 1805 年舉辦第一次就職開放日，林肯也照著做（did the same），後來就職的人潮多到白宮容納不下，還造成安全問題，所以 this practice 就是舉辦就職開放日。this practice 和它所指的事隔了好幾句，要往前找。(B) 照抄 comfortably，舒適地容納人潮正是做不到的事，不是那個做法；(D) 照抄 swearing-in ceremony，宣誓典禮在國會大廈舉行，不是讓白宮擠滿人的原因；(C) 布置白宮是這一段第一句說的總統個人風格，和人潮無關。

stem: Who initiated the construction of the White House?

ev.t: In 1790, President George Washington declared that the federal government would reside in a district “not exceeding ten miles square … on the river Potomac.”
Although President Washington oversaw the construction of the house, he never lived in it.

note: initiated 是「發起」，題目問的是決定蓋白宮、推動工程的人。第 1 段說 1790 年華盛頓總統宣布聯邦政府要設在波多馬克河畔的特區，籌備工作接著展開，他也監督了白宮的興建，所以是華盛頓。(B) 霍本是贏得設計比賽的建築師，負責的是設計；(A) 亞當斯是第一批搬進白宮的住戶；(D) 傑佛遜出現在第 2 段，是開放白宮讓民眾參觀的總統。

stem: What is this passage mainly about?

note: 第 1 段說明西尼羅病毒怎麼傳染、有哪些症狀；第 2 段說 2012 年達拉斯疫情嚴重；第 3 段說天氣和經濟危機讓蚊子大量繁殖；第 4 段說政府不作為也讓疾病擴散。第 3、4 段講的都是病毒在什麼條件下容易蔓延，所以是 (C)。(A) 對抗疾病的方法只在第 2、4 段帶到（空中噴藥、檢驗死鳥），(B) 政府效率只在第 4 段談到，都過於狹隘；(D) 把話題拉大到熱帶疾病整體，太過廣泛。這一題考後有人主張 (B) 也對，大考中心邀集專家討論後維持 (C)，說明試題文章是從原始報導大幅刪節改寫而成，作答要以考卷上這篇文章的脈絡為準。

stem: Which of the following statements is true about West Nile?

options.A: Its symptoms usually appear within two weeks.
options.B: It is spread through air and water in tropical areas.
options.C: Over 20% of people who contract it will suffer severe symptoms.
options.D: It comes from direct human contact with birds infected with the virus.

ev.t: Most people who contract West Nile do not experience any symptoms at all, but, if they do, symptoms typically develop between 3 to 14 days after a mosquito bite.

note: 第 1 段說症狀通常在蚊子叮咬後 3 到 14 天出現，也就是兩週以內；選項把 typically develop 換成 usually appear。(B) 照抄 tropical，但原文說病毒由鳥傳給蚊子、蚊子再叮人，不是經由空氣和水傳播；(D) 照抄 birds，人類是讓帶病毒的蚊子叮了才感染，不是直接接觸鳥類；(C) 大約五分之一的人只是發燒、頭痛，出現高燒、癱瘓這類嚴重症狀的是每 150 人中的 1 人，遠低於 20%。

stem: What did Dallas County do to fight off West Nile?

options.A: They sprayed pesticide from the air.
options.B: They asked citizens to stay away from dead birds.
options.C: They encouraged citizens to get vaccinations.
options.D: They drained the swimming pools in the county.

ev.t: The city declared a state of emergency and began aerial spraying of a pesticide to kill the mosquitoes, even though residents argued that the pesticide could be more dangerous than the disease.

note: 第 2 段說達拉斯市宣布緊急狀態，開始從空中噴灑農藥（aerial spraying of a pesticide），選項換成 sprayed pesticide from the air。(B) 照抄第 4 段的 dead birds，原文說達拉斯郡沒有檢驗死鳥，那是該做卻沒做的事；(D) 照抄第 3 段的 swimming pools，廢棄的游泳池是蚊子的繁殖場所，文章沒說郡政府去處理；(C) 接種疫苗文章沒提。

stem: Which of the following is a reason why Dallas was hit most seriously in the U.S. in 2012?

ev.t: An extremely mild winter allowed more mosquitoes than usual to survive,

note: 第 3 段說極為溫和的冬天讓比平常更多的蚊子活了下來，an extremely mild winter 在選項換成 not as cold as usual。(C) 照抄第 2 段的 residents，居民擔心的是噴藥的危險，這是政府處理疫情時的爭議，不是疫情嚴重的原因；(A) 照抄 Texas，文章沒說德州人口增加；(B) 第 4 段批評的是郡政府沒有檢驗死鳥、設置捕蚊器，不是沒有及時發布警告。

stem: What is the second paragraph mainly about?

ev.t: The problem is that the desalination of water requires a lot of energy.
The energy and technology to desalinate water are both expensive, and this means that desalinating water can be costly.

note: 第 2 段第一句先說淡化海水要去除鹽分，接著用 The problem is that 帶出這一段的重點：淡化需要大量能源，能源和技術都很昂貴，所以成本很高（costly），選項換成 high cost。(C) 照抄這一段第一句的 turn seawater into fresh water，但那句只是引出話題，迫切需要淡水是第 1 段的內容；(B) 照抄 chemical，化學鍵是用來解釋淡化為什麼耗費能源；(D) 照抄 energy，原文說的是淡化要消耗能源，不是產生能源，方向正好相反。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?

stem: Which of the following best describes the author’s attitude toward the future of desalination?

stem: Which of the following titles best describes the main idea of this passage?

note: 第 1 段以最早的巴比倫搖籃曲帶出搖籃曲常有陰暗的弦外之音；第 2 段說搖籃曲能安撫嬰兒，歌詞則能提供建議、反映照顧者的情緒；第 3 段說搖籃曲幫母親說出擔憂，是母親的心理治療。全文一路在談搖籃曲有什麼作用，所以是 (B)。(A) 起源和 (C) 帶有威脅的搖籃曲只是第 1 段的例子，(D) 催人入眠只對應第 2 段開頭安撫嬰兒的部分，都過於狹隘。

stem: Which of the following is closest in meaning to the word “undertones” in the first paragraph?
