options.B: Vocals.
options.C: Whispers.
options.D: Messages.

ev.t: It may have got the baby to sleep, but its message is far from comforting: If he/she does not stop crying, the demon will eat him/her.
This lullaby may sound more scary than sleep-inducing, yet it is true that many lullabies—including those sung today—have dark undertones.

note: 第 1 段說這首搖籃曲傳達的訊息（message）一點也不令人安心，接著說許多搖籃曲都帶著陰暗的 undertones；第 2 段也說歌詞可以解讀成照顧者情緒的反映。undertone 是話裡隱含的意思、弦外之音，最接近 (D) Messages。(A) 照抄同一段的 consequences，那是歌詞警告寶寶的可怕後果，不是弦外之音；(B) 歌聲和 (C) 耳語是從 tone 聯想到聲音，但這裡講的是歌詞的意思。

stem: What does the author use to support the idea that lullabies can have a soothing effect?

options.A: Research reports.
options.B: Examples found in history.
options.C: Stories of caretakers.
options.D: The author’s personal experiences.

ev.t: Research has shown that lullabies, when used correctly, can soothe and possibly even help to heal an infant;

note: 第 2 段一開頭就說研究顯示（Research has shown），搖籃曲用得正確可以安撫嬰兒，作者用的是研究報告，選項照用原字 Research。(C) 照抄 caretaker，原文說嬰兒回應的是照顧者的聲音，不是照顧者的故事；(B) 第 1 段的巴比倫搖籃曲是歷史上的例子，但用來說明搖籃曲帶有威脅意味，不是證明搖籃曲能安撫嬰兒；(D) 文章沒有寫到作者的親身經驗。

stem: According to this passage, which of the following statements is true?

options.A: Scary lullabies better help babies fall asleep.
options.B: Mothers prefer to sing lullabies with a joyful melody.
options.C: Lullabies comfort not only the baby but also the mother.
options.D: Babies react to both the music and the lyrics of lullabies.

ev.t: Research has shown that lullabies, when used correctly, can soothe and possibly even help to heal an infant;
Lullabies, therefore, serve as therapy for the mother.

note: 第 2 段說搖籃曲可以安撫嬰兒，第 3 段說搖籃曲幫母親說出擔憂，是母親的心理治療（therapy for the mother），所以搖籃曲安慰的不只是嬰兒，也有母親。(D) 照抄 lyrics，原文說嬰兒回應的是聲音和旋律，不是歌詞內容；(B) 照抄 melody，文章沒說母親喜歡唱旋律歡樂的搖籃曲；(A) 照抄第 1 段的 scary，原文只說那首巴比倫搖籃曲聽起來嚇人，沒說嚇人的搖籃曲比較能哄寶寶睡覺。

stem: What is the third paragraph mainly about?

options.A: The theory behind the questionnaire used in the Dognition test.
options.B: The procedure for evaluating a dog’s intellect on Dognition.
options.C: The products one can get by paying a fee to Dognition.
options.D: The characteristics of the activities Dognition offers.

ev.t: After you plunk your money down, Dognition’s website will take you through a questionnaire about your dog:
Then, Dognition guides you through tests that are as fun as playing fetch or hide-and-seek.
At the end, you get a report of your dog’s cognitive profile.

note: 第 3 段用 After、Then、At the end 標出先後：付錢之後先填問卷，接著帶狗做像遊戲一樣的測驗，最後拿到認知特質報告，講的是在 Dognition 評估狗狗智能的步驟，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄 questionnaire，但這一段只舉了問卷問些什麼，沒有談問卷背後的理論；(C) 付費後拿到的報告只是最後一步；(D) 測驗像遊戲一樣好玩，只是對其中一個步驟的描述。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?

options.A: Different dogs display strengths in different intelligences.
options.B: A dog’s cognitive profile is composed of nine cognitive skills.
options.C: The purpose of Dognition’s testing is to control a dog’s behavior.
options.D: A dog’s intelligence can be ranked based on the score of a Dognition’s test.

ev.t: Just as humans have a wide range of intelligences, so do dogs.
The question is what type your dog relies on more.

note: 第 2 段說就像人類有各式各樣的智能，狗也一樣，問題在於你的狗比較依賴哪一種；不同的狗擅長的智能不同，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄第 4 段的 nine，九種指的是狗的類型，不是認知特質由九種技能組成；(D) 原文說狗的智能沒辦法用單一數字描述，不能依分數排名；(C) 測驗的目的是了解狗，第 5 段說能讓狗和主人的關係更豐富，不是控制狗的行為。
map: what type your dog relies on more

stem: Which of the following is closest in meaning to the word “venture” in the second paragraph?

options.A: Creative measurement.
options.B: Risky attempt.
options.C: Non-profit organization.
options.D: New business.

ev.t: For US $60, a recently-founded company called Dognition will help you learn more about your dog’s cognitive traits.
Dr. Hare, one of the venture’s co-founders, says a dog’s intelligence can’t be described with a single number.

note: 第 1 段說 Dognition 是一家新成立的公司（a recently-founded company），第 2 段說 Hare 博士是這個 venture 的共同創辦人（co-founders）。共同創辦的就是第 1 段那家新公司，venture 是換個字再說一次，所以是 (D) New business。(B) 冒險的嘗試是 venture 另一個常見的意思，但這裡和 co-founders 連用，指的是新創事業；(C) Dognition 收費 60 美元，不是非營利組織；(A) 創新的評量在文章找不到依據。

stem: According to the passage, what would a Charmer most likely do?

options.A: Stay away from people whenever possible.
options.B: Imitate how other dogs solve problems.
options.C: Rely on its owner to point out where a treat is.
options.D: Follow its own senses to get what it wants.

ev.t: For example, a Charmer is a dog that trusts you so much that it would prefer to solve problems using information you give it rather than information it can get with its own eyes.

note: 第 4 段說 Charmer 型的狗非常信任主人，解決問題時寧可依靠主人給的資訊，也不用自己親眼看到的資訊；主人指出點心在哪裡，就是主人給的資訊，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄 its own，原文說這種狗不用自己親眼看到的資訊，選項說牠依靠自己的感官，正好相反；(B) 照抄 solve problems，但牠依靠的是主人，不是模仿其他狗；(A) 原文說牠非常信任主人，不會遠離人。

stem: What is the passage mainly about?

options.A: The history of Capoeira.
options.B: The values of Capoeira.
options.C: The contribution of Capoeira.
options.D: The techniques of Capoeira.

note: 第 1 段介紹卡波耶拉是什麼；第 2 段講它將近五百年前由巴西的非洲奴隸創造，從自衛變成反抗的武器；第 3 段講它從違法到成為巴西國技，再傳遍世界。全文依時間講卡波耶拉的發展，所以是 (A)。(D) 技巧只在第 1 段介紹，(B) 文化價值和 (C) 對舞蹈風格的影響只在第 3 段提到，都過於狹隘。

stem: Which of the following will probably NOT be found in the performance of Capoeira?

options.A: Singing with drums.
options.B: Sweeping with the legs.
options.C: Stabbing with swords.
options.D: Striking with the hands.

ev.t: Capoeira is a martial art that combines elements of fight, acrobatics, drumming, singing, dance, and rituals.
It involves a variety of techniques that make use of the hands, feet, legs, arms, and head.
in which people fought body to body, without weapons, in order to acquire a bride or desired woman.

note: 第 1 段說卡波耶拉結合擊鼓和歌唱（drumming, singing），是 (A)；技巧會用到手、腳、腿（hands, feet, legs），是 (B) 用腿掃和 (D) 用手打。文章沒有提到刀劍，第 2 段反而說它源自赤手空拳、不用武器的部落格鬥，所以 (C) 用劍刺最不可能出現。

stem: What is the author’s attitude toward Capoeira as a sport?

options.A: Admiring.
options.B: Objective.
options.C: Doubtful.
options.D: Harsh.

note: 全文介紹卡波耶拉的起源、演變和現況，只陳述事實，沒有表達作者自己的好惡；說到起源和影響，還用 It is believed、is also believed to 這類保留的說法。作者的態度是客觀的，所以是 (B)。(A) 欣賞容易誤選：第 3 段說卡波耶拉有很高的文化價值，但那是 Mestre Bimba 說服政府的理由，不是作者的評價；(C) 懷疑和 (D) 嚴厲，文章都找不到依據。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true about Capoeira?

options.A: It was greatly influenced by modern dancing styles.
options.B: It was initially created as a type of dance and ritual.
options.C: It was mainly performed to protect a bride or desired woman.
options.D: It was officially recognized in Brazil through the effort of Mestre Bimba.

ev.t: However, a man known as Mestre Bimba devoted a great deal of time and effort to convincing the Brazilian authorities that Capoeira has great cultural value and should become an official fighting style.
He succeeded in his endeavor and transformed the martial art into Brazil’s national sport.

note: 第 3 段說 Mestre Bimba 花了大量時間和心力說服巴西政府，最後成功讓卡波耶拉成為巴西國技，選項把 convincing the Brazilian authorities 換成 officially recognized in Brazil。(A) 照抄 dancing styles，原文說的是卡波耶拉影響了霹靂舞、嘻哈舞，選項把影響的方向說反了；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 bride or desired woman，那是非洲部落格鬥的目的，而且是為了娶到新娘，不是保護新娘；(B) 照抄第 1 段的 ritual，但第 2 段說卡波耶拉一開始是奴隸用來自衛的武術，歌舞是後來用來掩飾的。

stem: Where does this passage most likely appear?

options.A: On an ad featuring contemporary arts.
options.B: On a website of an art gallery.
options.C: In a booklet on American-born British artists.
options.D: In an encyclopedia on the art of printing.

note: 第 4 段說「這次為期兩週的展覽」呈現霍默的創作生涯，讓觀眾有機會欣賞他的作品；前三段介紹畫家的生平和作品特色，正是美術館網站介紹展覽的寫法，所以是 (B)。(D) 印刷只在第 1 段提到霍默當過印刷公司的學徒，過於狹隘；(A) 霍默是 19 世紀的畫家，不是當代藝術，(C) 霍默是美國畫家，只在英國住過兩年，都偏離主題。

stem: Which of the following is true about Homer’s career?

options.A: He achieved international fame with his vivid paintings of England.
options.B: He is considered the greatest illustrator in the history of American art.
options.C: He is better known for his watercolors than his illustrations and oil paintings.
options.D: He first established his reputation as an illustrator in his hometown of Boston.

ev.t: Born and raised in Boston, he began his career at age eighteen in his hometown, working as an apprentice at a printing company.
Skilled at drawing, he soon made a name for himself making illustrations for novels, sheet music, magazines, and children’s books.

note: 第 1 段說霍默在家鄉波士頓的印刷公司當學徒，很快就以繪製插畫出名（made a name for himself），選項換成 established his reputation as an illustrator。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 England，但讓他贏得國際肯定的是描繪北軍的畫作，不是描繪英國的畫；(B) 照抄 greatest，原文說他是最偉大的畫家（painter），不是最偉大的插畫家；(C) 照抄第 3 段的 watercolor，原文說他的插畫、油畫和水彩都同樣出色（excelled equally），沒說水彩比較有名。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following best characterizes Homer’s art?

options.A: His pictures vividly portrayed the life of nineteenth-century Americans.
options.B: His art thoughtfully expressed the voices of people suffering from war.
options.C: His style faithfully conformed to the artistic traditions of his time.
options.D: His paintings constantly reflected his desire to escape from society.

ev.t: Many of his works—depictions of children at play and in school, farm girls attending to their work, hunters and their prey—have become classic images of nineteenth-century American life.

note: 第 3 段說霍默的許多作品，像是孩子遊戲和上學、農家女孩工作、獵人和獵物，都成了 19 世紀美國生活的經典畫面，選項把 classic images of nineteenth-century American life 換成 vividly portrayed the life of nineteenth-century Americans。(B) 照抄 thoughtful，原文說他的作品表達深刻，沒說是替受戰爭之苦的人發聲；(C) 照抄 artistic，原文說他不受藝術傳統束縛（independence from artistic conventions），選項說他遵循傳統，方向正好相反；(D) 文章沒說他想逃離社會。

stem: What does “Others” in the third paragraph refer to?

options.A: Other artists.
options.B: Other themes.
options.C: Other works.
options.D: Other images.

ev.t: Many of his works
Others speak to more universal themes such as the primal relationship of humans to nature.

note: 第 3 段先說他的許多作品（Many of his works）成了美國生活的經典畫面，下一句接著說 Others 觸及更普遍的主題。Many of his works…Others… 前後對照，Others 是他的其他作品，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄 themes，主題是這些作品觸及的內容，不是 Others 本身；(D) 照抄 images，經典畫面是前一句對那批作品的評價；(A) 這一段沒有提到其他藝術家。

stem: How is this passage organized?

options.A: By cause and effect.
options.B: In the order of importance.
options.C: In the sequence of time.
options.D: By comparison and contrast.

note: 全文依時間先後排列：第 1 段是十七世紀凱薩琳王后帶動喝茶的風氣，第 2 段是 1800 年左右出現下午茶，第 3 段是十九世紀茶價下降、普及各階層，第 4 段是現在。seventeenth century、Around 1800、nineteenth century、Today 這些時間標記串起整篇，所以是 (C)。(A) 因果、(B) 重要性、(D) 比較對照都不是全文的組織方式。

stem: What does the phrase “a lasting British institution” in the first paragraph mean?

options.A: The most popular British organization.
options.B: A long-standing tradition in the UK.
options.C: The last tea company in London.
options.D: A well-established British business.

ev.t: Many employers served a cup of tea to their workers in the middle of the morning, thus inventing a lasting British institution, the “tea break.”

note: 第 1 段說許多雇主在上午工作到一半時請員工喝茶，因而開創了 a lasting British institution，也就是 tea break。上午喝茶休息是一種沿用下來的習慣做法：lasting 是持久的，institution 在這裡指制度、慣例，合起來就是 (B) 英國由來已久的傳統。(A) 組織和 (D) 企業，用的是 institution 另一個常見的意思「機構」；(C) 把 lasting 看成 last（最後的），文章也沒有談茶葉公司。

stem: According to the passage, why was tea NOT a common drink of everyday life in the seventeenth century?

options.A: It was only served at coffee houses in London.
options.B: It was taxed as an alcoholic drink.
options.C: It was forbidden outside of the business setting.
options.D: It was too expensive for most people.

ev.t: However, drinking tea in social settings outside the workplace was beyond the means of the majority of British people.
It came with a high price tag and tea was taxed as well.

note: 第 1 段說在工作場所以外的社交場合喝茶，大部分英國人負擔不起（beyond the means of the majority），因為茶的價格很高，還要課稅，選項換成 too expensive for most people。(A) 照抄 coffee houses，咖啡館是茶受歡迎的地方之一，原文沒說只在那裡供應；(B) 照抄 taxed，原文只說茶要課稅，沒說是當作酒類課稅；(C) 照抄 business，原文說人們在咖啡館談生意，沒說商業場合以外禁止喝茶。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true?

options.A: High tea was served later in the day than afternoon tea in the nineteenth century.
options.B: British people had tea breaks twice a day in the eighteenth century.
options.C: Princess Catherine brought tea to England after visiting Portugal.
options.D: The Earl of Sandwich started the afternoon tea ceremony.

ev.t: Around 1800, the seventh Duchess of Bedford, Anne Maria, began the popular practice of “afternoon tea,” a ceremony taking place at about four o’clock.
In working-class households, it was served with the main meal of the day, eaten when workers returned home after a day’s labor.

note: 第 2 段說下午茶大約在下午四點；第 3 段說勞工家庭的 high tea 搭配一天中最主要的那一餐，是工人做完一天的工作、回家後才吃的，可以推知 high tea 比下午茶晚，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄第 1 段的 tea break，原文說雇主在上午工作到一半時請員工喝茶，沒說一天兩次；(C) 照抄 Portugal，凱薩琳是在葡萄牙度過童年，不是去葡萄牙訪問之後才把茶帶到英國；(D) 照抄第 2 段的 Earl of Sandwich，三明治伯爵推廣的是三明治，開始下午茶習慣的是貝德福公爵夫人。

stem: What is the speaker’s attitude toward the blood-type belief in Japan?

options.A: Negative.
options.B: Defensive.
options.C: Objective.
options.D: Encouraging.

note: 作者介紹日本人對血型的看法時，用的是 popularly believed、is reported、reportedly 這類轉述的說法；第 1 段點出這種說法缺乏科學根據，第 4 段說有些人當作無傷大雅的娛樂，但可能演變成歧視，兩面都交代，沒有加上自己的褒貶，所以是 (C) 客觀。(A) 負面容易誤選：第 4 段提到血型騷擾和歧視，但作者是引述報導呈現這些現象，不是自己表態批評；(B) 辯護和 (D) 鼓勵都找不到依據。

stem: According to the examples mentioned in the passage, which blood type can we infer is the LEAST favored in Japan?

options.A: Type A.
options.B: Type B.
options.C: Type O.
options.D: Type AB.

ev.t: type Bs are cheerful but eccentric, individualistic, and selfish.
One former prime minister considered it important enough to reveal in his official profile that he was a type A, while his opposition rival was type B.
In his resignation speech, he blamed his failings on the fact that he was blood type B.

note: 文章舉的例子裡，B 型都是負面的：第 1 段說 B 型的人古怪、自私；第 3 段的前首相特地公開自己是 A 型、對手是 B 型；松本龍辭職時把過失歸咎於自己是 B 型。可以推論 B 型最不受歡迎。(D) AB 型在第 2 段是三菱電機組成全 AB 型團隊的正面例子；(A) A 型是前首相願意公開的血型；(C) O 型的例子文章沒有舉。

stem: Why did Prime Minister Ryu Matsumoto resign from office?

options.A: He revealed his rival’s blood type.
options.B: He was seen behaving rudely on TV.
options.C: He blamed his failings on local officials.
options.D: He was discriminated against because of blood type.

ev.t: In 2011, a minister, Ryu Matsumoto, was forced to resign after only a week in office, when a bad-tempered encounter with local officials was televised.

note: 第 3 段說松本龍和地方官員見面時脾氣暴躁（bad-tempered），畫面在電視上播出（was televised），上任一週就辭職，選項換成 behaving rudely on TV。這一段前後講了兩個人：(A) 照抄 rival，公開自己和對手血型的是前一句那位前首相；松本龍在原文是部長（a minister），題幹稱他 Prime Minister，別因此把兩人當成同一個人。(C) 照抄 blamed his failings on，他把過失歸咎於自己的血型，不是地方官員；(D) 原文是他自己拿血型當理由，不是別人因為血型歧視他。

stem: Which field is NOT mentioned in the passage as being affected by blood-type beliefs?

options.A: Education.
options.B: Sports.
options.C: Business.
options.D: Medicine.

ev.t: The women’s softball team that won gold for Japan at the Beijing Olympics is reported to have used blood-type theories to customize training for each player.
Some kindergartens have adopted teaching methods along blood group lines,
even major companies reportedly make decisions about assignments based on an employee’s blood type.

note: 有提到的三個領域在選項都換了說法：第 2 段壘球隊依血型安排訓練是 (B) Sports，幼稚園依血型採用教學方法是 (A) Education，大公司依血型分派職務是 (C) Business；第 3 段另外還提到政治。文章沒有說血型說影響醫療，所以選 (D)。血型本身是醫學名詞，但這一題問的是血型說影響了哪些領域。

stem: Why did Jeanie Low invent the Kiddie Stool, according to the passage?

options.B: She did not think that plastic stools were tall enough for her.
options.C: The stool in her bathroom was not firm and often got in the way.
options.D: She was invited to enter an invention contest held by her school.

ev.t: However, the plastic step-stool she had at home was unstable and cluttered up the small bathroom shared by her whole family.

note: 第 1 段說 Jeanie 家裡的塑膠踏凳不穩（unstable），又讓小浴室很擠（cluttered up），選項換成 not firm 和 often got in the way。(D) 照抄 invention contest held by her school，學校的發明比賽是她動手做的契機，她要解決的是凳子不穩又占空間的問題，而且原文說她決定參加，不是受邀參加；(A) 照抄 five-year-olds，原文只說她和許多五歲小孩一樣要踩凳子，沒說其他小孩有困難；(B) 照抄 plastic，原文沒說塑膠凳不夠高。

trap.t: invention contest held by her school

stem: Which of the following statements is true about how the Kiddie Stool works?

options.A: The Kiddie Stool will swing out only when the cabinet door opens.
options.B: It uses hinges and magnets to keep the wooden pieces in place.
options.C: It swings from left to right to be attached to the cabinet door.
options.D: The platform is supported by two pieces of metal.

ev.t: Using metal hinges, Jeanie attached one piece of the wood to the front of the cabinet door, and the second piece to the first.
When not in use, the hinges allowed the two pieces of wood to fold back up tightly against the cabinet, where they were held in place by magnets.

note: 第 2 段說 Jeanie 用金屬鉸鏈把兩片木板接起來，不用時鉸鏈讓木板摺回櫃門上，再用磁鐵固定（held in place by magnets），選項換成 uses hinges and magnets to keep the wooden pieces in place。(A) 照抄 cabinet door，凳子是從櫃門上往外展開，原文沒說要先打開櫃門；(C) 照抄 swing，原文說第一片木板水平展開、第二片往下擺，不是左右擺動；(D) 照抄 metal，金屬做的是鉸鏈，支撐平台的是兩片木板。
map: magnets to keep the wooden pieces in place

stem: What are the characteristics of Jeanie’s Kiddie Stool?

options.A: Permanent and foldable.
options.B: Fragile and eye-catching.
options.C: Conventional and touching.
options.D: Convenient and recyclable.

ev.t: Jeanie resolved to enter the contest by creating a stool that would be a permanent fixture in the bathroom, and yet could be kept out of the way when not in use.
When not in use, the hinges allowed the two pieces of wood to fold back up tightly against the cabinet, where they were held in place by magnets.

note: 第 1 段說 Jeanie 要做一張固定在浴室裡（permanent fixture）、不用時又能收起來的凳子；第 2 段說不用時兩片木板能摺回櫃門上（fold back），選項換成 Permanent and foldable。(D) 照抄第 2 段的 convenient，方便說對了一半，但 recyclable 可回收文章沒提；(B) fragile 脆弱，和原文說的 sturdy 穩固正好相反；(C) touching 感人說的是第 3 段大家對這個故事的感受，conventional 傳統的也和新發明接不上。

stem: Which of the following sayings best captures the spirit of Jeanie Low’s story?

options.A: Failure is the mother of success.
options.B: There’s nothing new under the sun.
options.C: Necessity is the mother of invention.
options.D: Genius is 1% inspiration and 99% perspiration.

note: 第 1 段說 Jeanie 因為家裡的凳子不穩又占空間，才想做一張更好的凳子；第 2 段說她怎麼做出兒童凳；第 3 段說兒童凳得獎、激勵許多人。整個故事是生活上有需要，才催生了發明，最貼切的是 (C) 需要為發明之母。(A) 失敗為成功之母，Jeanie 的發明一路得獎，文章沒有寫到失敗；(B) 太陽底下沒有新鮮事，和她做出新發明的故事不合；(D) 天才是 1% 的靈感加 99% 的汗水，強調的是苦幹，文章結尾強調的卻是想像力；三個選項都偏離主題。

stem: What is this article mainly about?

options.A: Why people are moving away from their own countries.
options.B: Why there are civil wars and violence in the Middle East.
options.C: Why many schools have become shelters for displaced families.
options.D: Why many children in the Middle East are not attending school.

note: 第 1 段開頭就說中東的衝突使超過 1,300 萬名兒童無法上學；第 2 段說明兩個原因：學校建築毀損、人口流離失所；第 3 段以敘利亞為例；第 4 段呼籲國際提供資源。全文要回答的是為什麼許多中東兒童沒有上學，所以是 (D)。(A) 人口遷離家園和 (C) 學校變成收容所，都只是第 2 段說明的原因，過於狹隘；(B) 文章沒有分析內戰和暴力為什麼發生，偏離主題。

stem: Why is “Iraq” mentioned in the second paragraph?

options.A: To convince people that temporary housing can be easily found.
options.B: To prove that classrooms there are big enough to host many families.
options.C: To give an example of why schools are not usable for children’s learning.
options.D: To show how structural damages of school can affect the quality of education.

ev.t: Across these countries, violence has made 8,500 schools unusable.
In certain cases, communities have relied on school buildings to function as shelters for the displaced, with up to nine families living in a single classroom in former schools across Iraq.

note: 第 2 段先說暴力使 8,500 所學校無法使用（unusable），接著用 In certain cases 帶出伊拉克的例子：學校成了收容所，一間教室住到九戶人家。提到伊拉克，是為了舉例說明學校為什麼不能用來上課，選項把 unusable 換成 not usable。(D) 照抄 structural damage，但伊拉克的例子說的是學校拿來安置流離失所的人，不是建築毀損，教育品質是第 3 段講敘利亞時才提到；(B) 照抄 families，一間教室住九戶人家是說擁擠，不是說教室夠大；(A) 文章沒說臨時住處很容易找到。

stem: What does the phrase “in the balance” in the last paragraph most likely mean?

options.A: Being well taken care of.
options.B: In an uncertain situation.
options.C: Under control by the authority.
options.D: Moving in the wrong direction.

ev.t: With more than 13 million children already driven from classrooms by conflict, it is no exaggeration to say that the educational prospects of a generation of children are in the balance.

note: 第 4 段說已經有超過 1,300 萬名兒童因為衝突離開教室，說一整個世代兒童的教育前景 in the balance 一點也不誇張。這麼多孩子失學，他們的教育前景會怎麼樣還說不定，in the balance 就是懸而未決、岌岌可危，最接近 (B) 處於不確定的狀況。(A) 得到妥善照顧、(C) 由當局控制，都和失學的處境不合；(D) 往錯誤的方向走，是把前景當成已經確定變壞，原文說的是結果還未定。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?

options.A: The war in Syria has been going on since 2011.
options.B: More than nine thousand schools have been destroyed by wars.
options.C: Thirteen million people have been forced to leave their homes in the Middle East.
options.D: Forty percent of all children in the world are not attending schools due to ongoing conflict.

ev.t: The report pays particularly close attention to Syria, where a bloody civil war has displaced at least nine million people since the war began in 2011.

note: 第 3 段說敘利亞的血腥內戰從 2011 年開始，選項把 since the war began in 2011 換成 has been going on since 2011。(B) 照抄 nine，原文的 nine 是九百萬人流離失所和九個國家，無法使用的學校是 8,500 所，不到九千所；(C) 照抄第 2 段 forced migration 的 forced，1,300 萬是無法上學的兒童人數，不是離開家園的人數；(D) 40% 指的是中東地區的兒童，不是全世界的兒童。

stem: What is the purpose of the study described in this passage?

options.A: To test if sea snakes lose body water at sea.
options.B: To see whether sea snakes drink water offered to them.
options.C: To find out if sea snakes are greatly reduced in population.
options.D: To prove that sea snakes drink only water coming from rivers.

ev.t: Thus, the team became interested in testing whether sea snakes became dehydrated at sea.

note: 第 2 段最後說研究團隊想知道海蛇在海上是否會脫水（became dehydrated），這就是研究目的，選項把 became dehydrated 換成 lose body water。(B) 照抄第 3 段的 offered to them，請海蛇喝淡水是研究的做法，不是目的；(C) 照抄第 3 段的 population，海蛇數量減少是研究結束後科學家提出的推測；(D) 原文說雨水是海蛇唯一的淡水來源，文章沒有提到河水。

stem: Which of the following is true about sea snakes?

options.A: Their salt glands can remove the salt in the seawater.
options.B: They can drink seawater when it mixes with rainwater.
options.C: The ocean is like a desert to them since they don’t drink seawater.
options.D: They usually live near the coastal area where there is more fresh water.

ev.t: However, the sea snake’s salt glands cannot handle the massive amounts of salt that would enter their bodies if they actually drank seawater.
But during the dry season when there is no rain, snakes presumably have nothing to drink.

note: 第 1 段說海蛇的鹽腺應付不了海水的鹽分，不能喝海水；第 2 段說乾季不下雨時，海蛇大概沒有水可以喝。身在一大片海水中卻沒水可喝，就像在沙漠裡一樣，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 salt glands，原文說的正好相反，海蛇的鹽腺排不掉喝海水帶進來的鹽；(D) 照抄第 2 段的 fresh water，原文說黃腹海蛇通常待在遠離陸地的海上；(B) 原文說下雨時海面會形成一層淡水，海蛇喝的是這層淡水，不是摻了雨水的海水。

stem: Which of the following is one of the findings of the study?

options.A: If a sea snake was dried and weak, it drank more fresh water.
options.B: If captured in the wet season, sea snakes drank a lot of fresh water.
options.C: Most of the sea snakes had lost a lot of body water when captured.
options.D: Dehydration is not a problem among sea snakes since they live at sea.

ev.t: A snake’s likelihood to drink also correlated with its body condition, with more withered snakes being more likely to drink, and to drink more.

note: 第 3 段說越乾瘦的海蛇（more withered）越可能喝水，也喝得越多，選項換成 dried and weak 和 drank more。(B) 照抄 wet season，原文說雨季時幾乎沒有海蛇喝水；(C) 照抄 body water，原文說的是乾季捕獲的海蛇體內水分比雨季少，不是大多數海蛇都失去很多水分；(D) 照抄 dehydration，研究發現海蛇會在海上脫水，脫水還可能造成某些地區海蛇減少，不是沒有問題。

stem: What can be inferred from the study?

options.A: Sea snakes can easily survive long years of drought.
options.B: Evolution will very likely enable sea snakes to drink seawater.
options.C: Sea snakes will be the last creature affected by global warming.
options.D: The sea snakes’ population distribution is closely related to rainfall.

ev.t: Because yellow-bellied sea snakes usually spend all of their time far from land, rain is the animals’ only source of fresh water.
Scientists believe that dehydration at sea may explain the declining populations of sea snakes in some parts of the world.

note: 第 2 段說雨水是黃腹海蛇唯一的淡水來源，第 3 段說科學家認為海上脫水可能是某些地區海蛇減少的原因。雨少的地方海蛇容易脫水、數量減少，可以推論海蛇分布在哪裡和雨量有密切關係，所以是 (D)。(A) 原文說海蛇只能在兩場雨之間忍受某種程度的脫水，不是能熬過多年乾旱；(B) 文章沒說海蛇會演化出喝海水的能力；(C) 文章沒有談全球暖化。

stem: Which of the following is true about Taiwu Elementary School Folk Singers?

options.A: The group was first established in 2009.
options.B: The group was founded by a PE teacher.
options.C: The singers usually sing popular folk songs.
options.D: The singers learn to sing from their parents.

ev.t: Camake Valaule, a physical education teacher and the founder of the Taiwu Elementary School Folk Singers,

note: 第 2 段介紹 Camake Valaule 是體育老師（physical education teacher），也是傳唱隊的創辦人（founder），選項換成 founded by a PE teacher。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 2009，那一年傳唱隊到歐洲演出，第 4 段說傳唱隊在 2006 年成立；(D) 照抄 parents，第 3 段說的正好相反，常常是孩子教父母唱；(C) 傳唱隊唱的是傳統古謠（traditional ballads），不是流行歌曲。

stem: On his first trip to Europe, why did Camake think the audience might fall asleep?

options.A: The average age of the audience was between fifty and sixty.
options.B: Most of the performance was not accompanied by any instrument.
options.C: Nobody could understand the language and the meaning of the songs.
options.D: The audience could not visualize the theme sung by the school children.

ev.t: He was worried that the audience would fall asleep since most of the 75-minute performance was a cappella, that is, singing without instrumental sound.

note: 第 2 段說 Camake 擔心觀眾睡著，因為 75 分鐘的演出大部分是 a cappella，原文緊接著用 that is 解釋：沒有樂器伴奏的清唱（without instrumental sound），選項換成 not accompanied by any instrument。(A) 五、六十歲是第 3 段說的部落長老的年紀，不是觀眾的平均年齡；(C) 文章沒說觀眾聽不懂歌詞；(D) 第 2 段說觀眾事後表示，透過演出就看見了傳唱隊的國家和村子，和選項說的正好相反。

stem: What does “the pieces of a blurred memory” in the third paragraph most likely refer to?

options.A: The children’s ignorance of their own culture.
options.B: The fading memories about old tribal people.
options.C: The broken pieces of knowledge taught at school.
options.D: The parents’ vague understanding of their own tradition.

ev.t: Now with the children performing the pieces, parents are beginning to ask, ‘Why do we not know how to sing these ballads?’
Many times nowadays, it is the children who teach the songs to their parents, putting back the pieces of a blurred memory.

note: 第 3 段說以前只有部落長老會唱古謠，現在家長聽到孩子唱，才問自己為什麼不會唱；接著說孩子教父母唱，把模糊的記憶（a blurred memory）拼回來。記憶模糊的是家長，模糊的是他們對自己文化的認識，選項把 blurred 換成 vague，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 children，把不懂文化的人從家長換成孩子，方向錯了，孩子反而是教唱的人；(B) 照抄 tribal，部落長老是記得這些歌的人，記憶模糊的不是他們；(C) 照抄 pieces，原文的 pieces 指的是一片一片拼回來的記憶，文章沒有談學校教的知識。

stem: What did Camake realize after the incident of Typhoon Morakot?

options.A: The significance of the relocation of Taiwu Elementary School.
options.B: The need to respect nature to avoid being destroyed by it.
options.C: The importance of passing on the traditional culture.
options.D: The consequence of building houses in the forest.

ev.t: The most important thing was to make children understand why they sing these songs and to preserve and pass on their culture.
We could not take the forest or our houses in the mountains with us; but we were able to bring our culture along.

note: 第 4 段說成立傳唱隊最重要的是保存、傳承文化（pass on their culture）；談到莫拉克颱風後遷校遷村，Camake 說森林和房子帶不走，文化卻帶得走，所以是 (C) 傳承傳統文化的重要。(A) 照抄 relocation，遷校遷村是颱風帶來的結果，他體會到的是文化帶得走；(D) 照抄 forest，帶不走森林是在對比文化帶得走，文章沒有談在森林裡蓋房子的後果；(B) 要尊重自然，以免大自然帶來災害，文章沒提。

stem: What is the main idea of this passage?

options.A: Treatments do not always cause harmful side effects.
options.B: Patients tend to believe more testing is better treatment.
options.C: Too much medical care may not be beneficial to patients.
options.D: Doctors generally recommend office visits that are necessary.

note: 第 1 段開門見山：很多人相信醫療越多越好，但過度醫療可能造成傷害；第 2、3 段用 Power 太太的例子說明，太多檢查讓她身心受苦、幾乎破產，停掉例行檢查後病情反而穩定。全文要說的是太多醫療對病人未必有益，所以是 (C)。(B) 病人相信檢查越多越好，只是第 1 段第一句的說法，過於狹隘；(A) 說治療不一定有副作用、(D) 說醫生通常只建議必要的回診，都和文章的立場相反，偏離主題。

stem: Which of the following was a problem for Mrs. Power during her medical treatment?

options.A: She had to be hospitalized for three weeks whenever she had a cold.
options.B: She didn’t have any insurance, so she went broke because of her illness.
options.C: When test results showed she was fine, her doctor still ordered more tests.
options.D: Her doctor asked her to consult other specialists due to her constant complaints.

ev.t: Even when tests came back negative, more were ordered,

note: 第 2 段說就算檢查結果正常（tests came back negative），醫生還是安排更多檢查，選項換成 test results showed she was fine 和 still ordered more tests。(A) 照抄 three weeks，原文說每三週回診一次，感冒住院是為了預防萬一，沒說住院三週；(D) 照抄 specialists，原文說連小毛病（minor complaints）也轉診，不是因為她一直抱怨；(B) 原文說醫療費用讓這對夫妻幾乎破產，沒提到有沒有保險。
map: test results showed she was fine

stem: Who does “they” in the third paragraph most likely refer to?

options.A: Physicians.
options.B: Other patients.
options.C: Mr. and Mrs. Power.
options.D: The online support groups.

ev.t: “It’s a really hard thing to determine when they’ve crossed the line,” Mr. Power said.

note: they 出現在 Power 先生說的話裡：很難判斷 they 什麼時候越過了界線（crossed the line）。第 2 段一路寫的是醫生堅持回診、一再安排檢查和轉診，做得太多、越過界線的是醫生，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄前一句的 other patients，(D) 照抄 online support groups，這對夫妻是和其他病友交流之後才開始質疑，病友和互助團體不是安排檢查的人；(C) Power 夫婦是承受過度醫療的一方。

stem: Which of the following best describes the author’s attitude toward medical tests?

options.A: More tests than necessary are too much.
options.B: Medical tests are essential for disease prevention.
options.C: Many tests are needed for confirmation of diagnosis.
options.D: Doctors’ interpretations of test results are seldom wrong.

note: 第 1 段說過度醫療（太多掃描、太多抽血、太多醫療程序）可能造成傷害，一項檢查常會引出更多檢查；Power 太太的例子也說明檢查做得太多反而傷身又傷財，停掉例行檢查後病情穩定。作者認為超過需要的檢查就是太多了，所以是 (A)。(B)、(C) 強調檢查必要，和作者的立場相反；(D) 文章沒有談醫生判讀檢查結果準不準。

stem: Which of the following best describes Cartier-Bresson’s family background?

options.A: His family was rich but was very economical.
options.B: His father went to Paris to open a textile factory.
options.C: His wealthy family went bankrupt and became poor.
options.D: His parents were very liberal in their ways of education.

ev.t: Cartier-Bresson’s family was wealthy—his father made a fortune as a textile manufacturer—but Cartier-Bresson later joked that due to his parents’ frugal ways, it often seemed as though his family was poor.

note: 第 2 段說布列松家境富裕（wealthy），但父母很節儉（frugal），選項換成 rich 和 economical。(B) 照抄 textile，原文只說父親經營紡織業發了財，去巴黎的是在巴黎受教育的布列松，不是父親去巴黎開工廠；(C) 照抄 poor，原文說的是父母節儉，家裡「看起來好像」很窮，不是真的破產；(D) 照抄第 3 段的 education，第 3 段說他反抗父母拘謹的教育方式，和選項說的開明正好相反。

stem: Which of the following is true about Cartier-Bresson’s career in photography?

options.A: He devoted himself to photography all his life.
options.B: He developed a passion for photography when he traveled to Africa.
options.C: He quit photography right after the publication of The Decisive Moment.
options.D: During World War II, he documented the everyday life of the Indian people.

ev.t: Cartier-Bresson traveled to Africa in 1931 to hunt antelope and boar.
And Africa fueled another interest in him: photography.

note: 第 4 段說布列松 1931 年到非洲打獵，非洲引發了他另一個興趣：攝影（fueled another interest in him），選項換成 developed a passion for photography。(C) 照抄書名 The Decisive Moment，這本書 1952 年出版，他到 1968 年才開始遠離攝影，不是一出書就放棄；(D) 照抄第 4 段的 everyday life，捕捉日常生活是他周遊世界時的作品，他去印度是在二戰結束後，拍的是甘地；(A) 第 7 段說他晚年轉向素描和繪畫，並沒有一輩子都投入攝影。

stem: What significance did Cartier-Bresson have to Gandhi of India?

options.A: He witnessed Gandhi’s assassination in 1948.
options.B: He was the first photographer to take Gandhi’s photo.
options.C: He used photos to document the effect of Gandhi’s death on India.
options.D: His photos told the world who was guilty of assassinating Gandhi.

ev.t: Cartier-Bresson’s subsequent work to document Gandhi’s death and its immediate impact on the country became one of Life Magazine’s most prized photo essays.

note: 第 5 段說布列松記錄了甘地之死，以及甘地之死對這個國家立即造成的衝擊（impact on the country），選項把 impact 換成 effect，把 the country 換成 India。(A) 照抄 assassination in 1948，原文說他在甘地遇刺前不久替甘地拍照，沒說他親眼目睹甘地遇刺；(B) 文章沒說他是第一個替甘地拍照的人；(D) 文章沒有談兇手是誰。

stem: Which of the following is true about Cartier-Bresson’s approach to photography?

options.A: He never waited for a decisive moment to shoot photos.
options.B: He preferred to edit his images carefully in his darkroom.
options.C: Most of his photos described things that happen every day.
options.D: He experimented with different ways and settled on being a naturalist.

ev.t: using a handheld camera to catch images from fleeting moments of everyday life.

note: 第 4 段說布列松用手持相機捕捉日常生活（everyday life）中稍縱即逝的瞬間，選項換成 things that happen every day。另外三個選項都照抄第 6 段：(B) 照抄 darkroom，原文說他不喜歡用暗房效果修飾過的照片，正好相反；(D) 照抄 naturalist，原文說他一生拍照的方式幾乎沒變，不是試過各種方法才決定當自然主義者；(A) 照抄 decisive moment，他說世上每件事都有決定性的瞬間，選項卻說他從不等待決定性的瞬間，和他的主張相反。

stem: What is the purpose of this passage?

options.A: To point out the challenges of the modern lifestyle.
options.B: To discuss how a modern epidemic may spread quickly.
options.C: To explore the effects of regular exercise to our body.
options.D: To explain the threat to our health from long hours of sitting.

note: 第 1 段點出久坐和許多致命疾病有關，專家稱為久坐病；第 2 段說明坐太久身體會產生哪些變化；第 3 段說就算有規律運動，也抵銷不了久坐的傷害；第 4 段給出解決方法。全文都在說久坐對健康的威脅，所以是 (D)。(A) 把話題拉大到現代生活的各種挑戰，太過廣泛；(C) 規律運動只在第 3 段談到，而且那一段要說的是運動抵銷不了久坐的傷害，過於狹隘；(B) 第 1 段用 epidemic 形容久坐病很普遍，文章沒有談流行病怎麼擴散，偏離主題。

stem: What does the word “sedentary” in the third paragraph most likely mean?

options.A: Modern.
options.B: Risky.
options.C: Inactive.
options.D: Epidemic.

ev.t: All the time that we spend rooted in the chair is linked to increased risks of so many deadly diseases
You needn’t worry about the harm of a sedentary lifestyle because you exercise regularly, right?

note: 第 3 段問：你有規律運動，所以不必擔心 sedentary 的生活方式帶來的傷害，對吧？前文一路講的都是坐在椅子上不動（rooted in the chair），規律運動是拿來對比的，可見 sedentary 是久坐不動、缺少活動的，最接近 (C) Inactive。(A) 和 (D) 照抄第 1 段的 modern-day 和 epidemic，那是在形容久坐病是現代的流行病；(B) 有風險是久坐的後果，不是 sedentary 這個字的意思。

stem: What is the best way to bring down high blood sugar level and blood pressure?

options.A: Exercising for 150 minutes or more every week.
options.B: Getting rid of the habit of car commuting and TV watching.
options.C: Interrupting sitting time with light activity as often as possible.
options.D: Standing or moving around for at least two or three minutes every day.

ev.t: Small amounts of regular activity, even just standing and moving around, throughout the day is enough to bring the increased levels back down.
30 minutes of light activity in two or three-minute bursts can be just as effective as a half-hour block of exercise.

note: 第 2 段說一整天裡（throughout the day）只要有少量、規律的活動，即使只是站起來走動，就能讓升高的血糖和血壓降回來；每次兩三分鐘、累積 30 分鐘的輕度活動，效果和一次運動半小時一樣。重點是不斷打斷坐著的時間，選項換成 interrupting sitting time as often as possible。(D) 照抄 two or three，原文說的是每次兩三分鐘、一天累積到 30 分鐘，不是每天只要兩三分鐘；(A) 照抄第 3 段的 150 minutes，第 3 段說的正好是每週運動 150 分鐘的人照樣每週坐 64 小時；(B) 改掉開車通勤和看電視的習慣，文章沒有這樣建議。

stem: Which of the following may be inferred about those who do serious exercise?

options.A: They often live longer than those who don’t exercise.
options.B: They tend to stand or move around less on days they work out.
options.C: They generally spend less time sitting than those who are inactive.
options.D: They usually do not meet the standard of exercise recommended by WHO.

ev.t: Regular exercisers, furthermore, are found to be about 30 percent less active on days when they exercise.

note: 第 3 段說規律運動的人在有運動的那幾天，活動量反而少了大約 30%（less active on days when they exercise），選項換成 stand or move around less on days they work out。(D) 照抄 recommended by，原文說不論有沒有達到世界衛生組織建議的運動量，人們每週都坐 64 小時，沒說認真運動的人通常達不到標準；(C) 原文說的正好相反，有沒有運動，坐的時間都差不多；(A) 壽命長短文章沒提。

stem: What is the passage mainly about?

options.A: The life of black people in the U.S.
options.B: The life of an African American writer.
options.C: The history of African American culture.
options.D: The history of the Nobel Prize in Literature.

note: 第 1 段寫摩里森的出生和成長，第 2 段寫她教書、結婚、加入寫作社團，第 3 段寫她離婚後專心寫作、出版小說，第 4 段寫她作品的主題和得獎。全文依時間寫一位非裔美國作家的一生，所以是 (B)。(A) 把話題拉大到美國所有黑人的生活，太過廣泛；(C) 非裔美國人的過去是她小說的題材，文章沒有交代非裔美國文化的歷史，偏離主題；(D) 第 4 段只說她得到諾貝爾文學獎，文章沒有談這個獎的歷史，也偏離主題。

stem: Why did Morrison join the writers’ group?

options.A: She wanted to publish The Bluest Eye.
options.B: She wanted to fight racial discrimination.
options.C: She wanted to be a professional writer.
options.D: She wanted to get away from her unhappy marriage.

ev.t: Several years later, her marriage began to fail.
For a temporary escape, she joined a small writers’ group

note: 第 2 段說摩里森的婚姻開始出問題（her marriage began to fail），為了暫時逃離（escape），她加入寫作社團，選項換成 get away from her unhappy marriage。(A) 照抄書名 The Bluest Eye，她在社團寫的只是一篇故事，而且寫完就收起來，離婚後才擴寫成小說；(B) 照抄第 1 段的 racial discrimination，種族歧視是她成長時的社會氣氛，和加入社團無關；(C) 原文說她以為那篇故事寫完就結束了，看不出她當時想當職業作家。

stem: According to the passage, what is one of the themes in Morrison’s works?

options.A: A search for African American values.
options.B: Divorced black women in American society.
options.C: Songs and stories of African Americans in Ohio.
options.D: History of African Americans from the 1970s through the 1990s.

ev.t: In her novels, Morrison brings in different elements of the African American past, their struggles, problems and cultural memory.
In Song of Solomon, for example, Morrison tells the story of an African American man and his search for identity in his culture.

note: 第 4 段說摩里森在小說裡融入非裔美國人的過去和文化記憶，並以《所羅門之歌》為例：一個非裔美國男子在自己的文化中尋找自我認同（search for identity in his culture）。在自己的文化裡找認同，就是在找非裔美國人的價值，所以是 (A)。(D) 照抄 1970，1970 到 1992 年是她陸續出版小說的期間，不是作品描寫的年代；(C) 照抄第 1 段的 songs and stories，那是她家裡的南方神話歌謠和故事，影響的是她的文字風格；(B) 照抄 divorced，離婚是她自己的經歷，文章沒說作品寫離婚的黑人女性。

stem: Which of the following statements is true about Toni Morrison?

options.A: She has been writing a lot since her adolescent years.
options.B: She suffered from severe racial discrimination in her family.
options.C: What she wrote in her novels are true stories of African Americans.
options.D: No African American woman ever received a Nobel Prize in Literature before her.

ev.t: She is the eighth woman and the first African American woman to win the honor.

note: 第 4 段說摩里森是第一位得到諾貝爾文學獎的非裔美國女性（the first African American woman），選項換個方向說：在她之前沒有一位非裔美國女性得過這個獎。(B) 照抄 racial discrimination，第 1 段說社會上有種族歧視，她的家庭生活卻很幸福，歧視並不是來自家裡；(A) 第 2 段說她婚姻出問題後加入寫作社團，才寫了第一篇故事，不是從青少年時期就大量寫作；(C) 第 3 段說她取材自童年記憶，再用想像力擴充，不全是真實故事。

stem: What does Zeke Emanuel have in mind when saying “What did Mom put in the cereal?”

options.A: The secret to bringing up successful kids.
options.B: The recipe for a breakfast food.
options.C: The difference among the brothers.
options.D: The questions from his kids.

ev.t: And then we began getting a lot of questions: What did Mom put in the cereal? Three successful brothers, all different areas.

note: 第 3 段說書出版後很多人來問：媽媽到底在麥片裡放了什麼？後面緊接著說三兄弟都很成功，而且在不同的領域。大家問的不是麥片，而是媽媽做了什麼，才養出三個成功的兒子，所以是 (A) 教出成功孩子的祕訣。(B) 只看字面，把 cereal 當成真的早餐；(D) 照抄 questions，這些問題是別人來問 Zeke 的，Zeke 的孩子是他寫故事的對象；(C) 三兄弟各在不同領域是問題的背景，大家想知道的是成功的原因。

stem: What does Zeke Emanuel think of the modern conveniences mentioned in the interview?

options.A: Better late than never.
options.B: Practice makes perfect.
options.C: One can live without many of them.
options.D: They are great inventions.

ev.t: I don’t own a TV. I don’t own a car. I don’t Facebook. I don’t tweet.
I’m down to two, thankfully.

note: 第 7 段 Zeke 說自己沒有電視、沒有車、不用臉書、不發推特；第 9 段說手機從四支減到兩支，還說了 thankfully（還好）。他少了這些東西照樣過日子，甚至樂於減少，所以是 (C) 很多東西沒有也能過活。(A) 遲做總比不做好、(B) 熟能生巧這兩句諺語和他的生活方式接不上；(D) 他不用這些東西，看不出他認為這些是偉大的發明。

stem: According to Zeke Emanuel, which of the following is a reason for the brothers’ success?

options.A: They defend themselves by attacking others.
options.B: They learn a lot from great people’s quotes.
options.C: They are committed to glorifying their parents.
options.D: They keep moving forward even after a big success.

ev.t: A second important thing is you never rest on the last victory.
There’s always more to do.

note: 第 5 段說第二個重點是永遠不因上一次的勝利停下來（never rest on the last victory），要做的事永遠還有，選項換成 keep moving forward even after a big success。(B) 照抄 quotes，put success in quotes 是把「成功」加上引號，表示他不敢自稱成功，不是向名人的名言學習；(A) 父親說的攻擊是最好的防禦，意思是主動出擊、不放棄，Zeke 接著就說「我們不放棄」，不是靠攻擊別人保護自己；(C) 母親給他們的是讓世界更好的期許，文章沒說三兄弟要替父母增光。

stem: Which of the following best summarizes Zeke Emanuel’s response to the last question?

options.A: The brothers look forward to a family trip on a cruise.
options.B: Nothing much will change in the near future for them.
options.C: Higher positions and more power will be their goals.
options.D: None of the brothers will go to the beach.

ev.t: Ari will be a superagent running the same company.
Rahm would still be mayor of Chicago.
I will probably continue to be my academic self.

note: 訪問者最後問五年後兄弟三人會在哪裡，Zeke 回答：Ari 還是經營同一家公司，Rahm 應該還是芝加哥市長，自己大概還是當學者。三個人都繼續做現在的事，所以是 (B) 近期不會有什麼改變。(A) 照抄 cruise，原文說的正好相反，三兄弟沒有人會去搭郵輪；(D) 照抄 beach，沒有人會坐在海灘上喝調酒，是用來說明他們不會停下來享樂，只是回答裡的一個細節，不能代表整段的意思；(C) Zeke 沒說三兄弟要追求更高的職位和權力。

stem: What does the word “cash-strapped” in the second paragraph mean?

options.A: Making a lot of money.
options.B: Being short of money.
options.C: Being careful with money.
options.D: Spending little money.

ev.t: Perhaps the most striking thing about MOOCs, many of which are being taught by professors at prestigious universities, is that they’re free.
This is certainly good news for cash-strapped students.

note: 第 2 段說 MOOC 最引人注目的地方或許是免費，接著說這對 cash-strapped 學生當然是好消息。課程免費，最高興的會是缺錢的學生，所以 cash-strapped 是手頭很緊、缺錢，最接近 (B) Being short of money。(A) 賺很多錢，和「免費課程是好消息」接不上；(C) 用錢謹慎、(D) 花錢很少，說的是花錢的習慣，不是手頭缺錢。

stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the features of MOOCs?

options.A: It is free to take the courses.
options.B: Many courses are offered by famous universities.
options.C: Most courses address artificial intelligence.
options.D: Many students can take the course at the same time.

ev.t: Since the courses can be taken by hundreds of thousands of students at the same time,
many of which are being taught by professors at prestigious universities
is that they’re free.

note: 文章提到的三個特色在選項都換了說法：第 2 段說 MOOC 最引人注目的是免費（they’re free），是 (A)；許多課程由知名大學的教授授課（professors at prestigious universities），是 (B)；一門課可以同時讓數十萬名學生修讀，是 (D)。人工智慧只是 Thrun 教授開的那一門課，文章沒說大部分的課程都在講人工智慧，所以選 (C)。

stem: What is the second paragraph mainly about?

options.A: The impact of MOOCs.
options.B: The goal of MOOCs.
options.C: The size of MOOC classes.
options.D: The cost of MOOC courses.

ev.t: This new breed of online classes is shaking up the higher education world in many ways.

note: 第 2 段先說 MOOC 在 2011 年引起轟動，接著用 This new breed of online classes is shaking up the higher education world in many ways 點出重點：這種課程在許多方面撼動高等教育界。後面說的大學數量可能大減、全世界只需要 10 所大學、免費對手頭很緊的學生是好消息，都是它帶來的影響，所以是 (A)。(C) 課程規模和 (D) 費用都只是這一段用來說明影響的細節；(B) 目標是第 1 段的內容。

stem: Which of the following is a problem of MOOCs mentioned in the passage?

options.A: The disappearance of traditional course materials.
options.B: The limited number of courses offered around the world.
options.C: The overreliance on professors from prestigious universities.
options.D: The lack of social interaction among students and professors.

ev.t: there is no replacement for true dialogues between professors and their students
Some critics worry that online students will miss out on the social aspects of college.

note: 第 3 段批評者說教授和學生之間真正的對話無可取代，也擔心線上學生會錯過大學的社交生活（social aspects of college），選項換成 lack of social interaction among students and professors。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 traditional course materials，原文說 MOOC 除了傳統教材之外還有論壇，教材並沒有消失；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 prestigious universities，知名大學的教授授課是 MOOC 的特色，不是問題；(B) 文章沒說課程數量有限，第 2 段說可能減少的是大學的數量。

stem: Which of the following statements is true about V2V?

options.A: V2V communication has been very well developed.
options.B: Through V2V, drivers can chat with each other on the road.
options.C: V2V is designed to decrease crashes by keeping safe distances.
options.D: Through V2V, a car can warn cyclists nearby of its approach.

ev.t: is being tested by automotive manufacturers as a way to help reduce the number of accidents.
so that they keep safe distances from each other.

note: 第 1 段說 V2V 的目的是減少事故的數量（reduce the number of accidents），做法是讓車輛之間互傳資訊、保持安全距離（keep safe distances），選項換成 decrease crashes by keeping safe distances。(A) 原文說 V2V 是發展中的技術（a developing technology），還在測試，不是已經發展得很成熟；(B) V2V 傳送的是位置、速度和方向，不是讓駕駛彼此聊天；(D) 原文講的是車和車之間，沒有提到騎單車的人。

stem: What does “infrastructure” in Vehicle-to-Infrastructure refer to?

options.A: Traffic facilities and information systems.
options.B: The basic structure of roads and bridges.
options.C: Knowledge and regulations about safe driving.
options.D: The traffic department of the government.

ev.t: V2I would allow vehicles to communicate with road signs or traffic signals and provide information to the vehicle about safety issues.
V2I could also request traffic information from a traffic management system and access the best possible routes.

note: 第 1 段說 V2I 讓車輛和道路標誌、交通號誌（road signs or traffic signals）溝通，也能向交通管理系統（traffic management system）要路況資訊。和車輛溝通的這兩類東西，選項概括成 traffic facilities and information systems，所以是 (A)。(B) 道路和橋梁的基本結構是 infrastructure 的一般意思，但這篇裡和車輛溝通的是號誌和系統，不是道路本身；(C) 安全駕駛的知識和法規、(D) 政府的交通部門，文章都沒提。

If this works, huge numbers of elderly and disabled people can regain their personal mobility.

stem: What can be inferred from the passage?

ev.t: Both V2V and V2I have the potential to reduce around 80 percent of vehicle crashes on the road.
brake automatically to avoid crashes

note: 第 1 段說 V2V 和 V2I 有潛力減少大約 80% 的車禍，第 2 段說新車已經能自動煞車避免撞車，再加上不需要人操控的無人車。這些技術一起發展下去，可以推論未來可能是沒有車禍的時代，所以是 (B)。(D) 照抄 driverless cars，原文說無人車預計五年內上市，不是還很遙遠；(A) 文章沒有談酒駕；(C) 原文說的是年輕人不必付高額保險費，沒說包括兒童在內每個人都買得起車。

stem: What does “It” in the third paragraph refer to?

options.A: The Swiss army needed a knife for every soldier.
options.B: Every good Swiss citizen had a knife in his pocket.
options.C: Swiss knives were competing with imported knives.
options.D: Canned food was becoming popular in the Swiss army.

ev.t: Swiss generals decided to issue each soldier a standard knife to serve both as a screwdriver and a can opener.
It was a lifesaver for Swiss knife makers, who were struggling to compete with cheaper German imports.

note: 對瑞士刀具業者來說是救命稻草的，是前一段結尾的那件事：軍方決定發給每個士兵一把刀，等於送上一筆大訂單。(C) 照抄同一句後半的 imports，那是業者的困境，不是救命稻草；(D) 罐頭普及只是軍方需要刀的原因之一。(B) 照抄第 1 段的 every good Swiss citizen，那句俗話說的是今天瑞士刀有多普遍，不是當年救了刀具業者的那件事。
map: issue each soldier a standard knife
needed a knife for every soldier

stem: Why didn’t the Swiss army purchase the Swiss Officer’s Knife?

options.A: The design of the knife was too simple.
options.B: The knife was sold out to American soldiers.
options.C: The army had no budget to make the purchase.
options.D: The new design was not considered necessary for officers to own.

ev.t: The Swiss military purchasers considered the new model with a corkscrew for opening wine not “essential for survival,” so officers had to buy this new model by themselves.

note: 採購人員認為多了開瓶器的新款不是生存必需品，essential 在選項換成 necessary。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 simple，但那是士兵刀的設計；(B) 照抄 American soldiers，美軍大量購買是二次大戰後的事。(C) 文章沒有提到軍方的預算，不買的原因是採購人員認為開瓶器不是生存必需。

stem: Who gave the name “the Swiss army knife” to the knife discussed in the passage?

options.A: Carl Elsener.
options.B: Swiss generals.
options.C: American soldiers.
options.D: German businessmen.

ev.t: After the Second World War, a great number of American soldiers were stationed in Europe.
However, it seems that “Schweizer Offizier Messer” was too difficult for them to say, so they just called it the Swiss army knife, and that is the name it is now known by all over the world.

note: they 指前面幾句的美軍：瑞士德語的名字太難唸，他們乾脆叫它 Swiss army knife。其他三個選項都是文章出現過的人，但和取名無關：(A) Elsener 設計士兵刀，(B) 瑞士將領決定發刀給士兵，(D) 德國的刀具是和瑞士業者競爭的便宜進口貨。

stem: What was the first piece of man-made space trash?

options.A: A camera.
options.B: A tool kit.
options.C: A fuel tank.
options.D: A broken satellite.

ev.t: The first piece of space junk was created in 1964, when the American satellite Vanguard I stopped operating and lost its connection with the ground center.

note: 第 2 段說第一件太空垃圾出現在 1964 年，是停止運作（stopped operating）、和地面失去聯繫的美國衛星先鋒一號，選項換成 a broken satellite。另外三個選項都照抄第 3 段：(A) 相機、(B) 工具箱、(C) 燃料箱是目前繞著地球的各種垃圾，不是第一件。

stem: Why were scientists NOT concerned about space trash in the beginning?

options.A: It no longer served any useful purpose.
options.B: It was millions of miles away from the Earth.
options.C: It did not cause any problems.
options.D: It was regarded as similar to comets and stars.

ev.t: However, since it kept orbiting around the Earth without any consequences, scientists became increasingly comfortable abandoning things that no longer served any useful purpose in space.

note: 第 2 段說先鋒一號一直繞著地球運行，沒有造成任何後果（without any consequences），科學家才越來越習慣把東西丟著不管，選項換成 did not cause any problems。(A) 照抄 no longer served any useful purpose，這是在說科學家丟掉的是什麼東西，不是他們不擔心的原因；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 comets and stars，那是一般人以為太空裡只有的東西，和科學家的想法無關；(B) 文章沒說垃圾離地球幾百萬英里。

trap.t: no longer served any useful purpose

stem: Which of the following statements is true about space junk?

options.A: It is huge, heavy machines.
options.B: It never changes position.
options.C: It floats slowly around the Earth.
options.D: It may cause problems for space shuttles.

ev.t: The major problem with the space trash is that it may hit working satellites and damage traveling spacecraft.
to prevent them from crashing into working satellites or space shuttles.

note: 第 4 段說太空垃圾的主要問題是可能撞上衛星、損壞航行中的太空船（damage traveling spacecraft），地面站監測垃圾也是為了防止垃圾撞上太空梭，選項換成 may cause problems for space shuttles。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 huge，原文說垃圾小到油漆碎片、大到燃料箱都有，不全是巨大的機器；(C) 照抄 around the Earth，垃圾確實繞著地球運行，但第 3 段說速度最高每小時 17,500 英里，不是慢慢飄；(B) 垃圾一直繞著地球轉，位置當然會改變。

stem: What has been done about the space trash problem?

options.A: Scientists have cleaned up most of the trash.
options.B: Large pieces of space trash are being closely watched.
options.C: Many nations have worked together to stop polluting space.
options.D: Ground stations are built to help store the trash properly in space.

ev.t: Ground stations have been built to monitor larger pieces of space trash

note: 題幹問的是已經做了什麼（What has been done），第 4 段只有地面站監測體積較大的垃圾是已經做到的（have been built），選項把 monitor 換成 closely watched。(C) 照抄 nations、(A) 照抄 clean：各國合作停止亂丟垃圾、清理已經在太空的垃圾，原文說是未來的計畫（Future plans），還沒做到；(D) 照抄 Ground stations，地面站是用來監測垃圾，不是在太空裡存放垃圾。

stem: For a person who just turned 20, what is the legal alcohol level allowed while driving in the US?

ev.t: while people under 21 are not allowed to drive a car with any level of alcohol in their body.

note: 第 1 段說美國 21 歲以上的人法定上限是 0.08%，未滿 21 歲的人只要體內有任何酒精（any level of alcohol）就不准開車。剛滿 20 歲還未滿 21 歲，允許的酒精濃度就是零，所以是 (A)。(C) 0.08% 是 21 歲以上的標準；(B) 和 (D) 照抄第 2 段的數字，那是能量飲料的酒精含量，不是法定上限。

stem: What is the purpose of the Missouri experiment?

options.A: To introduce a new method of calculating blood alcohol levels.
options.B: To discover the relation between energy drinks and ABT test results.
options.C: To warn about the dangers of drinking energy drinks mixed with alcohol.
options.D: To challenge the current legal alcohol limit for drivers in the United States.

ev.t: Can one of these energy drinks really cause someone to test positive on an ABT? Researchers in Missouri set up an experiment to find out.

note: 第 1 段最後問：喝能量飲料真的會讓人酒測呈陽性（test positive on an ABT）嗎？密蘇里州的研究人員設計實驗就是要找出答案，選項換成 discover the relation between energy drinks and ABT test results。(A) 照抄 blood alcohol，實驗沒有提出計算血液酒精濃度的新方法；(D) 照抄 legal，法定上限只是文章開頭的背景說明，實驗沒有挑戰這個標準；(C) 實驗測的是能量飲料本身含的酒精，不是摻了酒的能量飲料有什麼危險。

stem: What were the participants of the experiment asked to do after they finished their energy drink?

options.A: To line up in the laboratory.
options.B: To recall the drink brands.
options.C: To take an alcohol breath test.
options.D: To check their breath for freshness.

ev.t: They asked test subjects to drink a full can or bottle of an energy drink and then gave each subject an ABT one minute and 15 minutes after the drink was finished.

note: 第 2 段說受試者喝完能量飲料後，研究人員在 1 分鐘和 15 分鐘後各替每個人做一次 ABT。第 1 段開頭已經交代 ABT 就是 alcohol breath test（酒精呼氣檢測），選項把縮寫寫成全名，所以是 (C)。(A) 排隊、(B) 回想飲料品牌文章都沒提；(D) 呼氣檢測測的是酒精，不是口氣清不清新。

stem: What is the most important factor that affects the ABT test result for energy drink consumers?

options.A: The age of the person who takes the test.
options.B: The place where the test is given.
options.C: The equipment that the test uses.
options.D: The time when the test is taken.

ev.t: This shows that when the test is taken plays a crucial role in the test result.

note: 第 3 段說喝完 1 分鐘內檢測，有 11 種飲料測得出酒精，15 分鐘後檢測，全都測不出來；因此結論是什麼時候檢測（when the test is taken）對結果有關鍵的影響，選項換成 the time when the test is taken。(A) 年齡在第 1 段決定的是法定上限，和能量飲料的檢測結果無關；(B) 檢測地點和 (C) 檢測儀器，實驗都沒有比較。
map: The time when the test is taken

stem: Why did people in India start wearing a red dot on their forehead?

options.A: To indicate their social rank.
options.B: To show their religious belief.
options.C: To display their financial status.
options.D: To highlight their family background.

ev.t: While it is generally taken as an indicator of their marital status, the practice is primarily related to the Hindu religion.

note: 第 1 段說一般人常把紅點看作已婚的記號，但這個習俗主要和印度教有關（related to the Hindu religion）；第 2 段也說紅點象徵虔誠。選項換成 show their religious belief，所以是 (B)。(A) 社會階級、(C) 經濟狀況、(D) 家世背景，文章都沒提。

stem: What is the significance of the third eye in Hindu tradition?

options.A: To stay in harmony with nature.
options.B: To observe the outside world more clearly.
options.C: To pay respect to God.
options.D: To see things with a subjective view.

ev.t: the third one is there to focus inward toward God.
As such, the dot signifies piety and serves as a constant reminder to keep God in the front of a believer’s thoughts.

note: 第 2 段說第三隻眼用來向內專注於神，所以這個點象徵虔誠（piety），提醒信徒時時把神放在心上，選項換成 pay respect to God。(B) 照抄 outside world，看外在世界的是另外兩隻眼，第三隻眼是向內看的；(A) 和自然和諧相處、(D) 用主觀的角度看事情，文章都沒提。

stem: Why was red chosen as the original color of the bindi?

options.A: The red dot represented the blood of God.
options.B: Red stood for a wife’s love for her husband.
options.C: The word “bindi” means “red” in some Hindi dialects.
options.D: Red was supposed to bring blessings to a married couple.

ev.t: According to Hindu beliefs, the color red is believed to bring good fortune to the married couple.

note: 第 3 段說根據印度教的信仰，紅色會替夫妻帶來好運（bring good fortune to the married couple），選項把 good fortune 換成 blessings。(A) 照抄 blood，相傳點在妻子兩眼之間的是丈夫的血，不是神的血；(B) 照抄 wife，點血是為了替婚姻留下印記，原文沒說紅色代表妻子對丈夫的愛；(C) 照抄第 1 段的 Hindi dialects，原文說的是紅點在不同方言裡有不同的名稱，沒說 bindi 的意思是紅色。

stem: Which of the following statements is true about the practice of wearing a bindi today?

options.A: Bindis are worn anywhere on the face now.
options.B: Bindis are now used as a decorative item.
options.C: Most Indian women do not like to wear bindis anymore.
options.D: Wearing a bindi has become more popular among Indian men.

ev.t: Decorative or sticker bindis come in all sizes, colors and variations
Wearing a bindi has become more of a fashion statement than a religious custom.

note: 第 3 段說現在有裝飾用（decorative）的 bindi，大小、顏色、樣式應有盡有，戴 bindi 已經比較像是在展現時尚，選項換成 used as a decorative item。(C) 照抄第 1 段的 Indian women，原文說大部分印度女性都會點紅點，正好相反；(A) 第 2 段說 bindi 的位置有固定的標準，就在額頭正中央；(D) 第 1 段說男性點紅點的傳統逐漸式微，不是越來越流行。

stem: What’s the proper way of wearing the kilt?

options.A: It should be worn with underwear underneath it.
options.B: It should loosely fit on the body to be turned around.
options.C: It should be long enough to cover the wearer’s knees.
options.D: It should be wrapped across the front of the body two times.

ev.t: It is a tailored garment that is wrapped around the wearer’s body at the waist starting from one side, around the front and back and across the front again to the opposite side.

note: 第 1 段說蘇格蘭裙從身體一側開始圍在腰部，繞過前面和後面，再橫過前面一次（across the front again），前面一共橫過兩次，選項換成 wrapped across the front of the body two times。另外三個選項都照抄第 1 段：(A) 照抄 underwear，原文說內褲穿不穿依個人喜好，不是一定要穿；(B) 照抄 loose，原文說裙子不能鬆到能在身上轉動，正好相反；(C) 照抄 knees，原文說裙子蓋到膝蓋上方一點，沒有蓋住膝蓋。
map: across the front of the body two times

stem: Which of the following is a correct description about setts?

options.A: They were once symbols for different Scottish families.
options.B: They were established by the government for business purposes.
options.C: They represented different States and Provinces in the 19th century.
options.D: They used to come in one general pattern for all individuals and institutions.

ev.t: The association of particular patterns with individual families can be traced back hundreds of years.

note: 第 2 段說特定的方格圖案代表特定的家族（individual families），這種關聯可以追溯到幾百年前，選項換成 symbols for different Scottish families。這一段依時間講了三件事，三個錯誤選項都把時間或主角接錯：(B) 照抄 purposes，為了商業目的整理圖案的是十九世紀的紡織公司，不是政府；(C) 照抄 States and Provinces，代表州和省的圖案是現在（Today）才有的，不是十九世紀；(D) 照抄 general pattern，任何人都能穿的一般圖案也是現在才有，以前並不是只有一種圖案。

stem: Which of the following items is NOT typically worn with the kilt for decoration?

options.A: A pin.
options.B: A purse.
options.C: A ruby apron.
options.D: A silver knife.

ev.t: On the front apron, there is often a kilt pin, topped with a small decorative family symbol.
from fairly plain to quite elaborate silver- and jewel-ornamented designs.
The kilt can also be worn with a sporran, which is the Gaelic word for pouch or purse.

note: 第 3 段提到的配件，選項換了說法：kilt pin 是 (A) 裙針；sporran 是蓋爾語的錢包，也就是 (B) purse；小刀可以用銀裝飾，就是 (D) 銀製小刀。apron 是第 1 段說的裙子前面交疊的那幾層，本身就是裙子的一部分，不是另外配戴的飾品，文章也沒提到紅寶石，所以選 (C)。

stem: What is the purpose of this passage?

options.A: To introduce a Scottish garment.
options.B: To advertise a weaving pattern.
options.C: To persuade men to wear kilts.
options.D: To compare a skirt with a kilt.

note: 第 1 段說明蘇格蘭裙的穿法和長度，第 2 段說明裙子上的方格圖案，第 3 段說明可以搭配的配件。全文都在介紹這件蘇格蘭傳統服裝，所以是 (A)。(B) 方格圖案只在第 2 段介紹，而且文章是說明，不是替某種圖案打廣告，過於狹隘；(C) 文章沒有勸男性穿蘇格蘭裙，(D) 也沒有拿一般的裙子和蘇格蘭裙比較，兩個選項都偏離主題。

stem: In which of the following places has Wesla Whitfield worked?

options.A: A college.
options.B: A hospital.
options.C: A pizza parlor.
options.D: A news agency.

ev.t: when she took a job as a singing waitress at a pizza parlor.

note: 第 3 段說 Whitfield 18 歲時在一家披薩店（pizza parlor）找到工作，當會唱歌的服務生，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 college，大學是她念古典音樂的地方，不是工作的地方；(B) 照抄第 4 段的 hospital，她是住院接受治療的病人；(D) 為專欄採訪她的是作者，文章沒說她在新聞機構工作過。

stem: What does “when that happens” mean in the last paragraph?

options.A: When Wesla is losing her mind.
options.B: When Wesla is singing on the stage.
options.C: When Wesla is going out in her wheelchair.
options.D: When Wesla is watching other people dancing.

ev.t: she admitted to being frustrated occasionally, “especially when everybody’s dancing, because I love to dance.

note: 第 5 段 Whitfield 說她偶爾會覺得挫折，尤其是大家都在跳舞（everybody’s dancing）的時候，因為她很愛跳舞；緊接著說 when that happens，她就離開現場。that 指的就是前一句大家都在跳舞、她只能看的情況，選項換成 watching other people dancing。(A) 照抄 losing，原文說失去心智是人生唯一真正的殘缺，是她的看法，不是她遇到的情況；(B) 在台上唱歌、(C) 坐輪椅出門，都和她感到挫折的那一刻接不上。

stem: Which of the following statements is true about Wesla Whitfield’s physical disability?

options.A: It was caused by a traffic accident.
options.B: It made her sad and depressed at first.
options.C: It seriously affected her singing career.
options.D: It happened when she was a college student.

ev.t: she confessed that initially she didn’t want to face it.
After a year of depression she tried to kill herself.

note: 第 4 段說 Whitfield 癱瘓後一開始不想面對，接著憂鬱（depression）了一年，選項換成 made her sad and depressed at first。(D) 照抄第 3 段的 college，她是 29 歲排練完走路回家時遇上槍擊，那時已經大學畢業、在歌劇院合唱團唱歌；(A) 原文說是隨機槍擊，不是車禍；(C) 第 2 段說她在台上的歌聲讓全場的人忘了輪椅的存在，癱瘓並沒有嚴重影響她的歌唱事業。

stem: What advice would Wesla most likely give other disabled people?

options.A: Ignore what you have lost and make the best use of what you have.
options.B: Be modest and hard-working to earn respect from other people.
options.C: Acquire a skill so that you can still be successful and famous.
options.D: Try to sing whenever you feel upset and depressed.

ev.t: Whitfield said she came to understand that the only thing she had lost in this misfortunate event was the ability to walk.
But when that happens I just remove myself so I can focus instead on what I can do.

note: 第 5 段 Whitfield 說她失去的只有走路的能力，最寶貴的心智還在；看到大家跳舞覺得挫折時，她就離開現場，把心思放在自己能做的事情上。不去想失去的，把握還擁有的，所以她最可能給其他身障者的建議是 (A)。(B) 謙虛勤奮、贏得別人尊重，(C) 學一技之長才能成功出名，(D) 心情不好時就唱歌，都不是她在文章裡說的想法。

stem: What is the passage mainly about?

options.A: The different designs of forks.
options.B: The spread of fork-aided cooking.
options.C: The history of using forks for dining.
options.D: The development of fork-related table manners.

note: 第 1 段說叉子源自古希臘，原本是廚房切肉的工具；第 2、3 段說叉子從中東、義大利、法國一路傳到英國，成為餐桌上的用具；第 4 段說餐叉的形狀怎麼改良。全文依時間講人們用叉子吃飯的歷史，所以是 (C)。(A) 叉子的設計只在第 4 段談到，過於狹隘；(B) 用叉子幫忙烹調只出現在第 1 段，文章接下來講的是叉子在餐桌上怎麼傳開，(D) 用叉子的餐桌禮儀文章沒有談，兩個選項都偏離主題。

stem: By which route did the use of forks spread?

options.A: Middle East → Greece → England → Italy → France
options.B: Greece → Middle East → Italy → France → England
options.C: Greece → Middle East → France → Italy → Germany
options.D: Middle East → France → England → Italy → Germany

ev.t: Forks trace their origins back to the ancient Greeks.
By the 7th century A.D., royal courts of the Middle East began to use forks at the table for dining.
In the 11th century, a Byzantine wife brought forks to Italy;
Then in 1533, forks were brought from Italy to France.
In 1608, forks were brought to England by Thomas Coryate, who saw them during his travels in Italy.

note: 照文章的時間標記排：古希臘（第 1 段）→ 西元七世紀中東（第 2 段）→ 十一世紀傳到義大利 → 1533 年從義大利傳到法國 → 1608 年傳到英國（第 3 段），所以是 (B)。(A) 和 (D) 的起點不是古希臘；(C) 把義大利和法國的順序顛倒了，而且德國是在十九世紀發展出四齒叉，講的是叉子的改良，不是用叉子的習慣傳到哪裡。

stem: How did forks become popular in England?

options.A: Wealthy British were impressed by the design of forks.
options.B: Wealthy British thought it awkward to use their hands to eat.
options.C: Wealthy British gave special forks to the nobles as luxurious gifts.
options.D: Wealthy British considered dining with forks a sign of social status.

ev.t: Slowly, however, forks came to be adopted by the wealthy as a symbol of their social status.

note: 第 3 段說英國富人慢慢用起叉子，把叉子當作社會地位的象徵（a symbol of their social status），選項把 symbol 換成 sign。(A) 照抄 impress，原文說昂貴的叉子是用來讓客人留下深刻印象，不是富人自己對叉子的設計印象深刻，方向弄反了；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 awkward，覺得用叉子很彆扭的是法國人，不是英國人覺得用手吃飯彆扭；(C) 把叉子當禮物送給貴族，文章沒提。
map: a symbol of their social status

stem: Why were forks made into a curved shape?

options.A: They could be used to scoop food as well.
options.B: They looked more fashionable in this way.
options.C: They were designed in this way for export to the US.
options.D: They ensured the meat would not twist while being cut.

ev.t: the curved tines served as a scoop so people did not have to constantly switch to a spoon while eating.

note: 第 4 段說彎曲的叉齒可以當杓子用（served as a scoop），吃東西時不必一直換湯匙，選項換成 scoop food as well。(B) 照抄第 3 段的 fashionable，時尚說的是英國富人用叉子吃飯這件事，和叉齒的形狀無關；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 twist，讓肉不會扭動是古希臘兩齒廚房叉的用途；(C) 原文說四齒叉後來慢慢傳到美國，不是為了外銷美國才做成彎的。

stem: Why do some professional photographers NOT like to take pictures of pets?

options.A: Pets may not follow orders.
options.B: Pets don’t want to be bothered.
options.C: Pets may not like photographers.
options.D: Pets seldom change their expressions.

ev.t: However, because it’s hard to get them to sit still and “perform on command,” some professional photographers refuse to photograph pets.

note: 第 1 段說很難讓動物乖乖坐好、聽命令表演（perform on command），所以有些專業攝影師拒絕替寵物拍照，選項換成 may not follow orders。(B) 第 3 段說叫名字時可能吵醒寵物、拍到不耐煩的表情，那是一個拍照技巧可能遇到的情況，不是攝影師不拍寵物的原因；(D) 第 3 段說叫名字就能拍到寵物不同的表情，和選項正好相反；(C) 寵物不喜歡攝影師，文章沒提。

stem: What is the use of a biscuit in taking pictures of a pet?

options.A: To capture a cute look.
options.B: To create a special atmosphere.
options.C: To arouse the appetite of the pet.
options.D: To keep the pet from looking at the camera.

ev.t: One way to get an appealing portrait of a cat or dog is to hold a biscuit or treat above the camera.
The animal’s longing look toward the food will be captured by the camera,

note: 第 2 段一開頭就說，要拍出討人喜愛（appealing）的照片，方法是把餅乾或零食舉在相機上方，相機會拍下寵物望著食物的渴望眼神（longing look）。用餅乾的目的是拍到可愛的表情，所以是 (A)。(C) 引起寵物的食慾只是手段，拍下那個眼神才是目的；(D) 照抄 camera，零食舉在相機上方，寵物看零食時視線正好朝著鏡頭附近，不是要讓寵物別看相機；(B) 營造特別的氣氛，文章沒提。

stem: What is the advantage of calling your pet’s name when taking a shot of it?

options.A: To help your pet look its best.
options.B: To make sure that your pet sits still.
options.C: To keep your pet awake for a while.
options.D: To catch a different expression of your pet.

ev.t: You’ll get a different expression from your pet using this technique.

note: 第 3 段說叫寵物的名字後馬上按快門，用這個技巧可以拍到寵物不同的表情（get a different expression），選項把 get 換成 catch。(C) 照抄 awake，原文說的是可能把午睡的寵物吵醒，拍到不耐煩的表情，不是要讓寵物保持清醒；(B) 第 1 段說讓寵物乖乖坐好（sit still）正是很難做到的事，叫名字不是為了這個；(A) 原文說可能拍到一臉不耐煩，不一定是最好看的樣子。

stem: In what way is photographing zoo animals different from photographing pets?

options.A: You need to have fast film.
options.B: You need special equipment.
options.C: You need to stay close to the animals.
options.D: You need more time to watch and wait.

ev.t: Taking pictures of zoo animals requires a little more patience.
You may have to wait for a while until the animal does something interesting or moves into a position for you to get a good shot.

note: 第 4 段說拍動物園的動物需要多一點耐心，可能得等一陣子（wait for a while），等動物做出有趣的動作，選項換成 more time to watch and wait。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 fast film，高感光度底片是拍寵物時用的；(C) 照抄 close，原文說的正好相反，不要太靠近籠子；(B) 特殊器材文章沒提。

stem: Which of the following statements is true according to the passage?

options.A: Rapid speech without mistakes is a reliable sign of intelligence.
options.B: Women often play a more dominant role than men in a community.
options.C: Speaking slowly is more often a sign of lying than speaking quickly.
options.D: Touching tends to be initiated first by people of higher social positions.

ev.t: Speech that is slow, because it is laced with pauses or errors, is a more reliable indicator of lying than the opposite.

note: 第 3 段說說話慢、夾雜停頓或錯誤，比說話快更能可靠地看出對方在說謊（a more reliable indicator of lying），選項換成 more often a sign of lying than speaking quickly。(A) 照抄 reliable，原文用 reliable 形容說話慢是說謊的跡象，文章沒有談聰明；(D) 照抄第 2 段的 initiate，研究顯示主動觸碰的是地位較低的人，方向弄反了；(B) 第 2 段只說女性比男性更常主動觸碰，同一段也說主動觸碰的多半是地位較低的人，看不出女性比男性更有支配地位。
map: a more reliable indicator of lying
more often a sign of lying

stem: What is true about fixing your eyes on a person when you first meet him/her?

options.A: Fixing your eyes on the person will make him/her feel at ease.
options.B: It is more polite to fix your eyes on him/her as long as you can.
options.C: Most people feel uneasy to have eye contact for over a few seconds.
options.D: It doesn’t make a difference whether you fix your eyes on him/her or not.

ev.t: Most of us are comfortable with eye contact lasting a few seconds.
But eye contact which persists longer than that can make us nervous.

note: 第 1 段說大部分人能接受持續幾秒鐘的眼神接觸，超過這個時間（persists longer than that）就可能讓人緊張（make us nervous），選項換成 feel uneasy to have eye contact for over a few seconds。(A) 和 (B) 正是第 1 段要推翻的說法：一直盯著面試官看，很可能讓對方非常不自在；(D) 原文說盯著看會讓人不自在，不是沒有差別。

stem: Which of the following is NOT discussed in the passage?

options.A: Facial expressions.
options.B: Physical contact.
options.C: Rate of speech.
options.D: Eye contact.

ev.t: There is a long-held belief that when meeting someone, the more eye contact we have with the person, the better.
powerful people in a society—often men—show their dominance over others by touching them in a variety of ways.
The belief that rapid speech and lying go together is also widespread and enduring.

note: 三段各談一個常見的說法，選項換了說法：第 1 段 eye contact 是 (D)；第 2 段 touching 是 (B) Physical contact；第 3 段 rapid speech 是 (C) Rate of speech。臉部表情文章沒談，所以選 (A)。

stem: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.A: People have an instinct for interpreting non-verbal communication.
options.B: We should not judge the intention of a person by his body language.
options.C: A good knowledge of body language is essential for successful communication.
options.D: Common beliefs about verbal and non-verbal communication are not always correct.

note: 三段各提出一個普遍的說法，再用 However、In fact 推翻：第 1 段是眼神接觸越多越好，第 2 段是有權勢的人主動觸碰別人，第 3 段是說話快代表說謊。眼神和觸碰屬於非語言溝通，說話快慢屬於語言溝通，三段合起來就是 (D) 一般人對語言與非語言溝通的看法不一定正確。(B) 第 3 段反而說說話慢、停頓多比較可能是說謊，可見文章並不反對從這些線索判斷，偏離主題；(A) 文章說的正好相反，大家憑直覺相信的說法常常是錯的，也偏離主題；(C) 把話題拉大到肢體語言對成功溝通的重要，文章只破除三個常見的說法，太過廣泛。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true about Kamba and Maasai people?

options.A: Maasai people are a threat to elephants.
options.B: Kamba people raise elephants for farming.
options.C: Both Kamba and Maasai people are elephant hunters.
options.D: Both Kamba and Maasai people traditionally wear red clothing.

ev.t: Young Maasai men spear animals and thus pose a threat to elephants;

note: 第 2 段說年輕的馬賽族男性會用長矛獵殺動物，因此對大象構成威脅（pose a threat to elephants），所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 farm，坎巴族男性是農夫，原文沒說他們養大象來耕作；(D) 照抄第 4 段的 red clothing，原文說通常穿紅色的是馬賽族男性，不是兩個族群都穿；(C) 原文說坎巴族對大象沒有危險，獵殺動物的只有馬賽族。

stem: How did the elephants react to smell in the study?

options.A: They attacked a man with the smell of new clothing.
options.B: They needed time to relax when smelling something unfamiliar.
options.C: They became anxious when they smelled Kamba-scented clothing.
options.D: They were frightened and ran away when they smelled their enemies.

ev.t: When the elephants detected the smell of clothing worn by a Maasai man, they moved away from the smell faster and took longer to relax
Smelling a potential danger means that a threat is nearby and the best thing to do is run away and hide.

note: 第 3 段說大象聞到馬賽族男性穿過的衣服，離開得更快、也更久才放鬆；第 5 段解釋聞到潛在的危險就表示威脅在附近，最好逃跑躲起來。馬賽族就是大象的敵人，所以是 (D) 聞到敵人的氣味就害怕逃跑。(B) 照抄 relax，要更久才放鬆的是聞到馬賽族的氣味，不是聞到任何不熟悉的氣味；(C) 照抄 Kamba，大象對坎巴族的氣味反應和沒穿過的衣服差不多，不會焦慮；(A) 攻擊的反應出現在第 4 段大象看到紅色衣服時，而且對象是衣服，不是人。
map: moved away from the smell faster

stem: What is the main idea of this passage?

options.A: Elephants use sight and smell to detect danger.
options.B: Elephants attack people who wear red clothing.
options.C: Scientists are now able to control elephants’ emotions.
options.D: Some Kenyan tribes understand elephants’ emotions very well.

note: 第 1 段提出主題：大象能用視覺和嗅覺分辨誰會構成威脅；第 2 到 4 段用肯亞的實驗說明大象聞到和看到威脅時的反應；第 5 段解釋兩種反應為什麼不同。全文講的是大象用視覺和嗅覺察覺危險，所以是 (A)。(B) 大象攻擊紅色衣服只在第 4 段談到，而且對象是衣服不是人，過於狹隘；(C) 科學家控制大象的情緒、(D) 肯亞部落很了解大象的情緒，文章都沒談，偏離主題。

stem: What can be inferred about the elephant’s behavior from this passage?

options.A: Elephants learn from their experiences.
options.B: Elephants have sharper sense of smell than sight.
options.C: Elephants are more intelligent than other animals.
options.D: Elephants tend to attack rather than escape when in danger.

ev.t: They can use their sense of vision and smell to tell the difference between people who pose a threat and those who do not.
Young Maasai men spear animals and thus pose a threat to elephants; Kamba men are mainly farmers and are not a danger to elephants.

note: 第 2 段說會獵殺動物的是馬賽族，坎巴族是農夫，對大象沒有危險；大象聞到馬賽族的氣味、看到馬賽族常穿的紅色就有反應，對坎巴族卻不會。大象分得出哪些人危險、哪些人不危險，可以推論大象是從過去的經驗學來的，所以是 (A)。(D) 第 5 段說大象聞到危險時會逃跑，只有在風險低時才表現出攻擊性，和選項說的相反；(B) 文章說大象兩種感官都用，沒有比較哪一種比較敏銳；(C) 文章沒有拿大象和其他動物比聰明。

stem: What is the best title for this passage?

options.A: A Painful Mistake
options.B: A Great Adventure
options.C: A Lifelong Punishment
options.D: A New Direction in Life

note: 第 1、2 段寫 Deborah 從小夢想打籃球，第一場比賽就膝蓋受傷；第 3、4 段寫她一再受傷，常去物理治療診所，因而對這一行產生熱情；第 5 段寫她攻讀物理治療，打算幫助別人。她從籃球員轉向物理治療，最適合的標題是 (D) 人生的新方向。(A) 受傷是防守時發生的意外，不是她犯的錯；(B) 文章沒有寫冒險；(C) 她在傷痛中找到新目標，不是一輩子受罰；三個選項都偏離主題。

stem: How did Deborah feel when she first hurt her knee?

options.A: Excited.
options.B: Confused.
options.C: Ashamed.
options.D: Disappointed.

ev.t: Just like that, Deborah’s season was over.
Game after game, she could do nothing but sit on the sidelines watching others play the game that she loved so much.

note: 第 1 段說打高中籃球是 Deborah 從五歲就有的夢想，第 2 段說她第一場比賽就受傷，球季就這樣結束；第 3 段說她只能坐在場邊看別人打她熱愛的籃球。夢想一開始就落空，她的心情是 (D) 失望。(A) 興奮和受傷後的處境接不上；(B) 困惑、(C) 羞愧，文章都找不到依據，受傷是防守時發生的，她沒有做錯什麼。

stem: What is true about Deborah Duffey?

options.A: She didn’t play on the court after the initial injury.
options.B: She injured her knee when she was trying to block her opponent.
options.C: She knew that she couldn’t be a basketball player when she was a child.
options.D: She refused to seek professional assistance to help her recover from her injuries.

ev.t: As Deborah shuffled sideways to block the player, her knee went out and she collapsed on the court in burning pain.

note: 第 2 段說 Deborah 側身滑步要擋住對方球員（block the player）時，膝蓋受傷倒地，選項把 the player 換成 her opponent。(A) 照抄第 4 段的 on the court，原文說之後五年她的膝蓋又受傷三次，傷勢限制了她上場的時間，可見她後來還有上場；(D) 照抄 profession，她常去物理治療診所接受治療，正是接受了專業協助，還因此愛上這一行；(C) 第 1 段說她從五歲就夢想打籃球，不是小時候就知道自己當不成球員。

stem: What was the new light that Deborah saw in her life?

options.A: To help people take care of their bodies.
options.B: To become a teacher of Physical Education.
options.C: To become an outstanding basketball player.
options.D: To receive treatment in a physical therapy office.

ev.t: After she graduates, Deborah plans to use her knowledge to educate people how to best take care of their bodies

note: 第 4 段說 Deborah 常去物理治療診所，因而對這一行產生熱情，開始看見人生新的曙光（a new light）；第 5 段說明這道曙光是什麼：畢業後要教大家怎麼照顧好自己的身體（take care of their bodies），選項換成 help people take care of their bodies。(D) 照抄第 4 段的 receive treatment，接受治療是她受傷後的經歷，讓她看見新方向，不是新方向本身；(C) 照抄第 1 段的 outstanding，成為傑出球員是她受傷前的夢想；(B) 她攻讀的是物理治療，不是要當體育老師。
map: help people take care of their bodies

stem: Why were redwood trees more prominent in the forests of North America millions of years ago?

options.A: The trees were taller and stronger.
options.B: The soil was softer for seeds to sprout.
options.C: The climate was warmer and more humid.
options.D: The temperature was lower along the Pacific coast.

ev.t: A hundred million years ago, in the age of dinosaurs, redwoods were common in the forests of a much more moist and tropical North America.

note: 第 1 段說一億年前的北美洲比現在潮濕（moist）得多，屬於熱帶（tropical）氣候，當時紅杉在森林裡很常見，選項換成 warmer and more humid。(D) 照抄 Pacific coast，太平洋沿岸是氣候變乾冷之後紅杉退縮到的地方，時間和因果都接錯了；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 soft，柔軟的是紅杉的樹皮，不是土壤；(A) 文章沒有比較當時和現在的紅杉高矮。

stem: What does a “fairy ring” in the last paragraph refer to?

options.A: Circled tree trunks.
options.B: Connected root systems.
options.C: Insect holes around an old tree.
options.D: Young trees surrounding a mature tree.

ev.t: When the main tree dies, the sprouts are then free to grow as full trees, forming a “fairy ring” of trees around the initial tree.

note: 第 3 段說母樹死了以後，從樹幹基部長出的嫩芽長成大樹，在原來那棵樹的周圍（around the initial tree）形成一圈 fairy ring，選項換成 young trees surrounding a mature tree。(A) 照抄 trunk，嫩芽長在樹幹基部，圍成一圈的是新長出來的樹，不是樹幹；(B) 照抄 root system，母樹的根系是嫩芽養分的來源，不是那一圈樹；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 insect，原文說樹皮能讓老樹不受昆蟲侵害，文章沒有提到蟲洞。

stem: Which of the following is a function of the tree bark as mentioned in the passage?

options.A: It allows redwood trees to bear seeds.
options.B: It prevents redwood trees from attack by insects.
options.C: It helps redwood trees absorb moisture in the air.
options.D: It makes redwood trees more beautiful and appealing.

ev.t: It gives the older trees a certain kind of protection from insects,

note: 第 2 段說樹皮讓老樹在某種程度上不受昆蟲侵害（protection from insects），選項換成 prevents redwood trees from attack by insects。(A) 照抄 seeds，讓毬果張開、撒出種子的是火災的熱氣，不是樹皮；(D) 照抄 beautiful，原文用 beautiful 形容樹皮的樣子，沒說樹皮的功能是讓紅杉更好看；(C) 吸收空氣中的水分，文章沒提。

stem: Why do redwood trees grow to live that long according to the passage?

options.A: They have heavy and straight tree trunks.
options.B: They are properly watered and nourished.
options.C: They are more resistant to fire damage than other trees.
options.D: They produce many young trees to sustain their life cycle.

ev.t: This fire resistant quality explains why the giant redwood grows to live that long.

note: 第 2 段說樹皮很厚，能在森林火災中保護樹心，這種耐火（fire resistant）的特性就是紅杉能活那麼久的原因，選項換成 more resistant to fire damage than other trees；同一段也說其他樹木會毀於火災。(A) 照抄 straight，粗壯筆直的樹幹是紅杉的外觀，不是長壽的原因；(B) 照抄第 3 段的 nourished，靠母樹的根系提供養分的是嫩芽；(D) 照抄 cycle，嫩芽長成新樹、循環不息說的是紅杉怎麼繁衍，不是一棵紅杉為什麼長壽。

stem: Which of the following titles best describes the passage?

options.A: The History of Ocarinas
options.B: Materials Used to Make Ocarinas
options.C: Ocarinas in Asia and Europe
options.D: The Ocarina: A Nintendo Product

note: 第 1 段說陶笛從石器時代就存在；第 2 段講中國的塤；第 3 段講陶笛從馬雅人傳到歐洲、在義大利發展、二戰時傳入美國；第 4 段講二十世紀陶笛音樂延伸到電玩。全文依時間講陶笛的歷史，所以是 (A)。(B) 製作陶笛的材料只在第 1 段帶到；(C) 亞洲和歐洲只是第 2、3 段的一部分，文章還談到南美洲和美國；(D) 任天堂的遊戲只在第 4 段舉例，陶笛也不是任天堂的產品；三個選項都過於狹隘。

stem: Which of the following is mentioned in the passage as a use of ocarinas by the Chinese?

options.A: The Chinese used ocarinas in their worship music.
options.B: Ancient Chinese used the instrument to perform magic.
options.C: The Chinese used the flute-like ocarina, or xun, when hunting.
options.D: Ancient Chinese musicians used the xun to imitate bird calls on stage.

ev.t: the instrument has played an important role in the imperial orchestra for religious worship and palace entertainment.

stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about the parents in the study?

note: 第 3 段說三國的子女都形容母親溫暖、開放（warm and open），加拿大的子女也和父親有很深的情感連結；第 2 段又說加拿大的父母比較寬容。加拿大的父親和母親都和子女親近，所以是 (B)。這一段把母親和父親、法國和其他兩國分開講，三個錯誤選項都把人接錯：(A) 照抄 cold，態度冷淡的是法國父親，不是義大利父親；(C) 照抄 distant，法國子女覺得疏遠的是父親，母親反而越來越親近；(D) 照抄 close，法國父親和子女保持距離，不是三國的父母都和子女親近。

stem: What does the word gauge mean in the second paragraph?

options.A: Control.
options.B: Restore.
options.C: Increase.
options.D: Measure.

ev.t: For one thing, it’s difficult to scientifically gauge happiness.
In recent years, however, researchers have developed a few accurate measurements of happiness.

note: 第 2 段說正向心理學的第一個障礙是很難用科學方法 gauge 快樂，接著舉例：朋友說很好卻一直哭，要評為快樂還是難過？我的「8」怎麼確定比你的「6」快樂？這些都是在說快樂難以測量。第 3 段開頭也呼應：近年研究人員發展出幾種準確測量快樂的方法（measurements）。可見 gauge 是 (D) 測量。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 control，那是說假笑的人控制不了嘴邊的肌肉；(C) 增加快樂是正向心理學的目標，不是第 2 段說的障礙；(B) 恢復，和上下文接不上。

stem: What is the third paragraph mainly about?

options.A: One problem in research on happiness.
options.B: A new method used to assess happiness.
options.C: An interesting way to enhance happiness.

ev.t: In recent years, however, researchers have developed a few accurate measurements of happiness.
One of the techniques involves looking at how often people genuinely smile in their daily lives.

note: 第 3 段第一句就是主題句：近年研究人員發展出幾種準確測量快樂的方法（measurements），接著舉觀察真心微笑的頻率為例。選項把 measurements 換成 a new method used to assess happiness，所以是 (B)。(A) 研究快樂遇到的問題是第 2 段；(C) 提升快樂的方法是第 4 段；(D) 第 1 段只說快樂是熱門的研究主題，沒有說明正向心理學受歡迎的原因。

stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the passage as one of the ways to enhance happiness?

ev.t: expressing optimism about your future
extending gratitude to people who help you
and exercising regularly.

note: 第 4 段列出的方法，選項換了說法：expressing optimism about your future 是 (B) 對未來抱持正面的態度；extending gratitude 是 (D) 對幫助你的人表達感謝；exercising regularly 是 (A) 養成運動的習慣。原文只說讓親友在生活中占重要的位置，沒有提到定期和朋友出國旅行，所以選 (C)。

ev.t: Likewise, on a scale of 1 to 10, how can we be sure that my “8” is happier than your “6”?

note: 第 2 段問：在 1 到 10 的量表上，我們怎麼能確定我的「8」比你的「6」快樂？每個人打分數的標準不同，可以推論快樂量表有它的問題，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄第 4 段的 frequently，原文說經常替別人做好事的人最快樂，正好相反；(D) 照抄第 3 段的 corner，會牽動眼角的是真心的笑容，假笑的人控制不了這些肌肉，方向弄反了；(C) 第 1 段說不久之前心理學家還認為快樂不值得研究，不是幾十年來都很熱門。

stem: What is the purpose of this passage?

note: 第 1 段先說家長和教育工作者對電玩的批評；第 2 段用 However 轉折，報導一項新研究：玩某些動作遊戲能讓人做決定更快、更準確；第 3 段說明人怎麼做決定。全文在報導玩電玩有什麼影響的新發現，所以是 (D)。(C) 第 2 段比較了動作遊戲和《The Sims 2》，但只是研究結果的一部分，過於狹隘；(A) 文章沒有推銷新遊戲，(B) 第 1 段的批評只是研究的背景，文章並沒有勸孩子別玩電玩，兩個選項都偏離主題。

ev.t: However, a recent study from cognitive science suggests that there may be a benefit in playing some action games.
Only those who played fast-moving action video games such as “Call of Duty 2” and “Unreal Tournament” saw an improvement in their decision-making skills.

note: 第 2 段說玩某些動作遊戲可能有好處，只有玩快節奏動作遊戲的人決策能力有進步（saw an improvement in their decision-making skills），選項換成 playing some video games may help us improve our decision-making skills。(C) 照抄 fast-moving，玩快節奏動作遊戲的人做決定更準確，選項說的正好相反；(B) 照抄 same，原文說玩《The Sims 2》的人沒有得到同樣的好處，可見不是所有遊戲都有這個效果；(A) 不玩電玩的人在幾週內接受 50 個小時的訓練就能看到效果，不需要好幾年。

stem: What is the main idea of the last paragraph?
