options.C: book review
options.D: magazine on international trade

note: 第 1 段開頭寫明地震發生的日期、死亡人數和受災情形；第 2 到 4 段交代巴姆的建築和歷史背景，說明為什麼災情這麼嚴重；第 5 段報導救援物資星期天運抵、精神領袖誓言重建。這是報導一場剛發生的災難的寫法，最可能出自 (A) 報紙。(B) 城堡和絲路的歷史只是第 3、4 段的背景，過於狹隘；(D) 絲路貿易站只在第 4 段提到，文章的重點不是國際貿易，也過於狹隘；(C) 文章沒有評論任何一本書，偏離主題。

stem: What was Bam most famous for?

options.A: Beautiful palm trees.
options.B: Frequent earthquakes.
options.C: An old mud and straw castle.
options.D: Treasures from the Far East.

ev.t: Bam was best known for its 2,000-year-old castle built out of mud, straw, and the trunks of palm trees.

note: 第 3 段說巴姆最有名的（best known for）是那座有 2,000 年歷史、用泥土和稻草（mud, straw）建成的城堡，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 palm trees，棕櫚樹幹是蓋城堡的材料之一，不是巴姆出名的東西；(D) 照抄第 4 段的 treasures from the Far East，遠東的珍寶是經過巴姆運往歐洲的貨物；(B) 照抄第 1 段的 earthquake，原文說這是十多年來最嚴重的地震，沒說巴姆常常地震。

stem: The use of baked mud for buildings explains ______.

options.A: why the earthquake occurred
options.B: why Bam collected so many treasures
options.C: why Bam developed into a trading post
options.D: why the earthquake caused such damage

ev.t: One reason the earthquake caused such damage was that Bam's buildings were made mostly from baked mud.

note: 第 2 段說地震造成這麼嚴重的破壞（caused such damage），原因之一是巴姆的建築大多是用烤乾的泥土造的，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄第 4 段的 trading post、(B) 照抄第 4 段的 treasures，巴姆成為貿易站、有珍寶經過，是因為位在絲路上，和建築材料無關；(A) 建築材料說明的是破壞為什麼嚴重，不是地震為什麼發生。

stem: Which of the following is CORRECT about the earthquake in Bam?

options.A: About 50,000 people survived the earthquake.
options.B: Not many countries sent food and supplies to Bam.
options.C: The 2003 earthquake was the first one in its history.
options.D: The city of Bam would be deserted after the earthquake.

ev.t: At least 25,000 people died in the quake—nearly a third of the city's population.

note: 第 1 段說至少 25,000 人在地震中喪生，將近全城人口的三分之一。死亡的人占三分之一，倒推全城人口大約是 25,000 × 3＝75,000 人，活下來的大約是三分之二，也就是 50,000 人左右，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄第 5 段的 supplies，原文說食物和物資來自世界各地，不是沒有多少國家援助；(C) 照抄 2003，原文說這是十多年來最嚴重的地震，可見以前也有地震，不是第一次；(D) 第 5 段精神領袖誓言要把巴姆重建得比以前更堅固，不會把城市廢棄。

stem: A traveler who suffers from jet lag has problems in ______.

options.A: adjusting his biological clock
options.B: knowing the direction of a jet
options.C: knowing the distance of his flight
options.D: getting used to the weather of a new place

ev.t: It is caused by disruption to the internal biological clock
The body takes about one day to get over each hour of time difference.

note: 第 1 段說時差是體內的生理時鐘（biological clock）失調造成的；第 2 段說每差一個小時，身體大約要一天才能恢復。有時差的旅客，問題就在調整生理時鐘，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄第 2 段的 direction，旅行的方向會影響時差有多嚴重，不是說旅客不知道飛機往哪個方向飛；(C) 飛行的距離、(D) 適應新地方的天氣，原文都沒有提到。

stem: If one travels across three time zones, he needs about ______ hours to get over his jet lag problem.

ev.t: The body takes about one day to get over each hour of time difference.

note: 跨越一個時區，時間就差一個小時，跨越三個時區就差三個小時。第 2 段說每差一個小時，身體大約要一天才能恢復，三個小時就要三天，3 × 24＝72 小時，所以是 (D)。這一題要先把時區換成小時，再把天數換成小時：(A) 24 只算了一個小時時差要的一天；(B) 36、(C) 48 都算錯了天數。

stem: A person may suffer the most serious case of jet lag when he takes a ______ journey.

options.A: east-to-west
options.B: west-to-east
options.C: north-to-south
options.D: south-to-north

ev.t: A west-to-east journey, on the other hand, makes us late compared to the local time.
It often demands even greater effort in adjustment since we are not quick enough to catch up with the new time schedule.

note: 第 2 段說往西走可能出現問題；從西往東（west-to-east）的旅程，通常需要花更大的力氣（even greater effort）調整，因為我們追不上新的時間表；最後還舉例說洛杉磯到紐約比紐約到洛杉磯問題多。時差最嚴重的是 (B)。(C) 照抄 north、(D) 照抄 south，原文說往北或往南通常沒有時區變化，不會注意到任何差別；(A) 從東往西也可能有問題，但 even greater 比較的結果是從西往東比較嚴重。

stem: The main purpose of the passage is to ______.

options.A: explain the cause of jet lag problems
options.B: teach us how to avoid jet lag problems
options.C: explain the differences between time zones
options.D: show the ways to lessen the degree of jet lag problems

note: 第 1 段說時差是生理時鐘失調造成的，會引起哪些問題；第 2 段說明時差的嚴重程度和跨越幾個時區、往哪個方向旅行有關。全文在解釋時差問題是怎麼來的，所以是 (A)。三個錯誤選項都偏離主題：(B) 怎麼避免時差、(D) 怎麼減輕時差，文章都沒有教；(C) 文章談的是跨越時區對身體的影響，不是比較各個時區有什麼不同。

stem: When was the first nest of the red ant found in the United States?

options.D: After 1975.

ev.t: but the first colony of the red ants was not found until 1942 by a 13-year-old boy in his backyard.

note: 第 1 段說第一個紅火蟻的蟻窩直到 1942 年才由一個男孩發現（not found until 1942），所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄 1930s，1930 年代末期是紅火蟻搭貨船進入美國的時間，不是發現蟻窩的時間；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 1975，那時紅火蟻已經占據超過 5,200 萬公頃；(D) 1975 年以後，紅火蟻早就散布各地了。

stem: Which of the following is TRUE according to the article?

options.A: Each nest of the red ant has one queen.
options.B: The red ant was originally found in North America.
options.C: The red ant can reproduce young ants very quickly.
options.D: The red ant does not build mounds inside the house.

ev.t: With multiple queens at work, its population increases rapidly.

note: 第 3 段說有多隻蟻后同時工作，蟻群的數量增加得很快（increases rapidly），選項換成 reproduce young ants very quickly，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 one queen，原文說以前每個蟻窩只有一隻蟻后，現在常常有多隻；(D) 照抄 mounds，原文說紅火蟻在室內也會築蟻丘，正好相反；(B) 照抄第 1 段的 America，紅火蟻原產於南美洲，北美洲是牠們入侵的地方。

stem: What kinds of problems can the red ant cause?

options.A: Health, social, and agricultural.
options.B: Health, social, and environmental.
options.C: Social, environmental, and agricultural.
options.D: Health, agricultural, and environmental.

ev.t: They construct their colonies on precious farmland, invading crops while searching for insects underground.
Small birds such as baby quails are fair game to the expanding colony.
Worst of all, their stings can be fatal to livestock and humans.

note: 第 4 段列出紅火蟻造成的問題，要自己歸類：侵害農地上的農作物、把果樹的果實吃光，是農業問題（agricultural）；侵擾草坪和牧場、捕食小鳥，是環境問題（environmental）；螫人可能讓人喪命，是健康問題（health）。所以是 (D)。原文沒有提到社會問題（social），(A)、(B)、(C) 都有 social，可以直接排除。

stem: What is the purpose of the article?

options.A: To ask for help to kill the red ant.
options.B: To urge people to protect the red ant.
options.C: To provide information about the red ant.
options.D: To seek help from the government to control the red ant.

note: 第 1、2 段說紅火蟻從哪裡來、怎麼進入美國、擴散得多快；第 3 段說牠們怎麼築巢、繁殖；第 4 段列出牠們造成的問題。全文在介紹紅火蟻，所以是 (C)。三個錯誤選項都偏離主題：(A) 文章沒有請大家幫忙消滅紅火蟻；(B) 文章列出紅火蟻的種種危害，不會呼籲保護牠們；(D) 文章沒有提到政府。

stem: This article is mainly about ______.

options.A: the danger of heart transplant surgery
options.B: becoming young by getting a new heart
options.C: the effect of genetics on the heart
options.D: the twin brothers who received heart transplants

note: 第 1 段介紹這對雙胞胎兄弟先後接受心臟移植，創下紀錄；第 2 段是 Alfred 拿新心臟開的玩笑；第 3 段說兩人心臟出問題的原因；第 4、5 段說兩人復原的情形和兄弟感情。全文寫的是這對接受心臟移植的雙胞胎兄弟，所以是 (D)。(B) 換了心臟變年輕，只是第 2 段 Alfred 開的玩笑，過於狹隘；(C) 遺傳對心臟的影響，只在第 3 段提到一句，也過於狹隘；(A) 文章沒有談心臟移植手術的危險，偏離主題。

stem: What did Alfred and Anthony have in common?

options.A: Lifespan.
options.B: Career goals.
options.C: A sense of humor.
options.D: Love for bicycling.

ev.t: A sense of humor is just one of the many things shared by Alfred and Anthony Melillo

note: 第 1 段第一句就說幽默感（sense of humor）是兩兄弟許多共同點（shared by）當中的一個，所以是 (C)；第 2 段 Alfred 對記者開玩笑、記者頻頻大笑，也是例證。(B) 照抄第 5 段的 goal，那是 Alfred 希望自己覺得比兄弟更好，不是職業目標；(D) 第 4 段說騎腳踏車的是 Anthony 的運動計畫，不是兩人的共同點；(A) 壽命，文章沒有提到。

stem: What did Alfred and Anthony think caused their heart problems?

options.A: Exercise.
options.B: Diet.
options.C: Surgery.
options.D: Medicines.

ev.t: they recognized that their eating habits might have also contributed to their heart problems.

note: 第 3 段說兩兄弟承認飲食習慣（eating habits）可能也是心臟出問題的原因，還說在牛排上抹半磅奶油、好吃的東西都吃過了頭，選項換成 Diet，所以是 (B)。同一句前面提到的遺傳（genetics）不在選項裡。(A) 照抄第 4 段的 exercise，運動是 Anthony 移植後復原的方法，不是心臟出問題的原因；(C) 手術、(D) 藥物，都是心臟出問題以後的事。

stem: Why did Alfred say, “I’m 15 minutes older than him, but now I’m younger because of my heart” ?

options.A: His heart transplant surgery was more successful than Anthony’s.
options.B: His recovery from the heart surgery was faster than Anthony’s.
options.C: His exercise program was better than Anthony’s.
options.D: His new heart was younger than Anthony’s.

ev.t: Anthony had a heart transplant from a 21-year-old donor.
Alfred received a 19-year-old heart

note: 第 1 段說 Anthony 移植的心臟來自 21 歲的捐贈者，Alfred 移植的是 19 歲的心臟。Alfred 雖然早出生 15 分鐘，換上的心臟卻比 Anthony 的年輕兩歲，所以開玩笑說自己現在比較年輕，答案是 (D)。(B) 照抄第 4 段的 recovery，原文說 Alfred 才剛進入復原初期、吃的藥比 Anthony 多，正好相反；(C) 照抄 exercise program，那是 Anthony 的運動計畫；(A) 哪一次手術比較成功，文章沒有比較。

stem: What reason do the major museums provide for not handing back the ancient objects?

options.A: Only in the leading museums can the objects be fully appreciated by the world.
options.B: It is better for those objects to remain at a certain place than to be moved around.
options.C: They need those well-known ancient objects to attract people from all over the world.
options.D: Ancient civilizations can only be admired if they are removed from their home countries.

ev.t: They say people all over the world have only been able to fully appreciate ancient civilizations because these museums have provided access to these artistic objects.

note: 第 1 段說這些博物館的理由是：全世界的人能充分欣賞（fully appreciate）古代文明，只因為（only…because）博物館讓大家看得到這些藝術品。選項把 only 移到句首、改成倒裝句 Only in the leading museums can…，主詞也從人換成文物，句型變了，意思相同，所以是 (A)。(D) 照抄 admired，原文說的是文物在各大博物館展出，古代文明才這麼受推崇，沒有說非得離開原屬國才能受推崇；(C) 照抄 well-known，well-known 在原文是說埃及文化因此出名，不是博物館需要有名的文物來吸引人；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 remain，那是大英博物館館長說雕塑要留在館裡才能達成宗旨，不是說文物留在一處比搬來搬去好。

stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as one of the “countries of origin” in the article?

options.A: Turkey.
options.B: Britain.
options.C: Egypt.
options.D: Greece.

ev.t: handed over 363 pieces of gold, silver, precious stones, paintings, and sculptures back to Turkey
Egyptian culture would not have become so well-known if the museums had not put Egyptian mummies on show.
sculptures taken from the Parthenon in Athens, Greece, in the 19th century.

note: countries of origin 是文物原本所屬的國家。第 1 段大都會藝術博物館把文物歸還給 (A) 土耳其；埃及木乃伊來自 (C) 埃及；第 2 段埃爾金石雕是從 (D) 希臘雅典的帕德嫩神殿拿走的。英國只以大英博物館的身分出現，是收藏文物的一方，不是文物的原屬國，所以選 (B)。

stem: What does “the world” mean in “show the world to the world”?

options.A: The global village.
options.B: The leading museums.
options.C: The ancient civilizations.
options.D: The international public.

ev.t: which is to show the world to the world,
They say people all over the world have only been able to fully appreciate ancient civilizations because these museums have provided access to these artistic objects.

note: show A to B 是把 A 展示給 B 看。第 1 段說博物館讓全世界的人（people all over the world）看得到這些藝術品，因而能欣賞古代文明。展示出來的第一個 the world，是各地的古代文明，所以是 (C)；展示的對象，也就是第二個 the world，才是全世界的人。(D) 照抄第 1 段的 international public，那是第二個 the world 的意思，把兩個 the world 弄反了；(B) 照抄 leading museums，博物館是做展示的一方；(A) 地球村，原文沒有提到。

stem: Which of the following is the best title for the article?

options.A: Mating of Flashlight Fish and Fireflies.
options.B: Darkness and Light.
options.C: Living Lights and Animal Communication.
options.D: Life on Land and in the Sea.

note: 第 1 段總說有些動物會發光，用光傳遞訊號、引誘獵物或逃離捕食者；第 2 段舉海裡的燈眼魚，第 3、4 段舉陸地上的螢火蟲，說明牠們怎麼用光和同伴、獵物、敵人溝通。全文講的是生物發光和動物之間的溝通，所以是 (C)。(A) 交配只出現在第 3 段螢火蟲的部分，燈眼魚發光不是為了交配，過於狹隘；(B) 黑暗與光、(D) 陸地和海裡的生物，範圍都比文章大得多，太過廣泛。

stem: Flashlight fish in the Red Sea give out light at night ______.

options.A: when they come out for food
options.B: as they try to look for their companions
options.C: because they want to get rid of the bacteria
options.D: so that they can get close to other flashlight fish

ev.t: tiny flashlight fish rise to the surface for food,

note: 第 2 段說夜幕籠罩紅海時，燈眼魚游到海面上覓食（rise to the surface for food），選項換成 come out for food，所以是 (A)。(D) 照抄 close to，原文說燈眼魚用光溝通，是為了避免彼此靠得太近（too close to each other），方向正好相反；(C) 照抄 bacteria，光就是住在眼睛下方的細菌發出的，不是要擺脫細菌；(B) 原文說的是和同伴保持距離，不是尋找同伴。

stem: According to the passage, NEITHER flashlight fish NOR fireflies send out light to ______.

options.A: attract a mate
options.B: lure their prey
options.C: escape from their enemies
options.D: find their way home

ev.t: use light to attract a mate.
some female fireflies lure the males of other species to them.
flashing its light on and off very quickly to confuse the animal pursuing it.

note: 題目問燈眼魚和螢火蟲都不會為了什麼發光。第 3 段螢火蟲用光吸引配偶，是 (A)；第 4 段雌螢火蟲用假訊號引誘其他種類的雄蟲來吃，是 (B) 引誘獵物；第 2 段燈眼魚遇到捕食者威脅時快速閃光，讓追趕的動物摸不著方向，是 (C) 逃離敵人。文章沒有提到用光找路回家，所以選 (D)。

stem: Which of the following statements about fireflies is true?

options.A: All kinds of fireflies use the same signals.
options.B: Fireflies use their headlamps to communicate.
options.C: Male fireflies may deceive females with false signals.
options.D: Female fireflies respond from the ground to males’ signals.

ev.t: female fireflies gather on the ground.
a female signals back to the male,

note: 第 3 段說雌螢火蟲聚集在地面上（on the ground），認出同種的閃光密碼，就發出訊號回應（signals back）雄蟲，選項換成 respond from the ground，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄第 4 段的 false，發假訊號騙人的是雌螢火蟲，上當的是雄蟲，選項把兩者弄反了；(A) 照抄 signal，原文說每一種的雄蟲都發出自己特有的訊號，不是都一樣；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 headlamps，「頭燈」是燈眼魚眼睛下方的發光器官，螢火蟲是從身體下方發光。

stem: Which book is the thickest?

options.A: Everywhere.
options.B: Tuck Everlasting.
options.C: The Table Where Rich People Sit.
options.D: Beyond the Ridge.

ev.t: 180 pages.

note: 書最厚，就是頁數最多。四本書的書目資料最後都列了頁數：(A)《Everywhere》70 頁、(B)《Tuck Everlasting》180 頁、(C)《The Table Where Rich People Sit》52 頁、(D)《Beyond the Ridge》32 頁，最多的是 (B)。這一題要看懂書目的寫法：作者、書名、出版社、出版年、ISBN、頁數，依序排列。

stem: Which book is published in 1990?

options.A: Everywhere.
options.B: Tuck Everlasting.
options.C: The Table Where Rich People Sit.
options.D: Beyond the Ridge.

ev.t: Brooks, Bruce. Everywhere. HarperCollins, 1990.

note: 書目資料裡，出版社後面接的是出版年。第 1 段《Everywhere》由 HarperCollins 在 1990 年出版，所以是 (A)。其他三本的出版年：(B)《Tuck Everlasting》是 1975 年，(C)《The Table Where Rich People Sit》是 1994 年，(D)《Beyond the Ridge》是 1989 年。

stem: Who wrote the book about Native Americans’ view of death?

options.A: Bruce Brooks.
options.B: Natalie Babbitt.
options.C: Byrd Baylor.
options.D: Paul Goble.

ev.t: Goble, Paul. Beyond the Ridge.
based on the customs of the Plains Indians in America.
expressing specific beliefs about dying.

note: 第 8 段說《Beyond the Ridge》根據美洲平原印第安人（the Plains Indians in America）的習俗，表達對死亡的信念（beliefs about dying）；題目換成 Native Americans’ view of death。這本書的作者是第 7 段的 Paul Goble，所以是 (D)。書目資料把姓放在前面、名放在後面，Goble, Paul 就是 Paul Goble。(B) Natalie Babbitt 的《Tuck Everlasting》寫的是喝了泉水長生不死，不是印第安人怎麼看死亡。(A) Bruce Brooks 的《Everywhere》雖然寫到祖父可能過世，講的是男孩在朋友陪伴下發現希望和愛的力量，也和印第安人無關；(C) Byrd Baylor 的《The Table Where Rich People Sit》寫的是一家人怎麼看待財富。

stem: Who wrote the book which shows that money is not the only way to measure wealth?

options.A: Bruce Brooks.
options.B: Natalie Babbitt.
options.C: Byrd Baylor.
options.D: Paul Goble.

ev.t: Baylor, Byrd. The Table Where Rich People Sit.
Soon, she realizes that her poor family is rich in things that matter in life.

note: 第 6 段說小女孩原本要爸媽多賺錢，後來明白自己貧窮的家，在人生真正重要的東西上很富有（rich in things that matter in life）；題目換成錢不是衡量財富的唯一方式。這本《The Table Where Rich People Sit》的作者是第 5 段的 Byrd Baylor，所以是 (C)。(B)《Tuck Everlasting》雖然寫到有人想把泉水賣給出價最高的人，但全書講的是長生不死的秘密，不是怎麼衡量財富；(A)《Everywhere》講的是希望和愛的力量，(D)《Beyond the Ridge》講的是印第安人怎麼看死亡，都和財富無關。

stem: The passage is mainly about ______.

options.A: a beautiful gift
options.B: an empty house
options.C: a sad goodbye
options.D: a sweet memory

note: 第 1 段 Amy 和朋友 Laura 道別，不知道還會不會回來；第 2 段媽媽催她出門，她們只能帶拿得動的東西；第 3 段母女最後一次看看屋子和花園，Amy 覺得孤單。全文寫的是一場令人難過的離別，所以是 (C)。(A) 金手鍊只是第 1、2 段的細節，過於狹隘；(B) 空蕩蕩的屋子只在第 3 段出現，也過於狹隘；(D) 第 3 段 Amy 想起爸爸送花給媽媽，那只是一段回憶，而且回想之後的心情是孤單，不是甜蜜，過於狹隘。

stem: Which of the following statements is explicitly mentioned in the passage?

options.A: Amy’s father planted carnations in the garden.
options.B: All of Amy’s friends knew that she was leaving.
options.C: Amy’s mother sold all the furniture before they left.
options.D: Amy and her mother carried only a few suitcases with them.

ev.t: They could take only what they could carry, and her two suitcases were already full.

note: 題幹問的是原文明白寫出來的（explicitly mentioned）。第 2 段說她們只能帶自己拿得動的東西，Amy 的兩個行李箱已經裝滿了，選項換成只帶了幾個行李箱，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 carnations，原文只說要是爸爸在，會摘康乃馨送媽媽，沒有說花是爸爸種的；(C) 照抄 furniture，原文說 Amy 回想房間擺滿家具時的樣子，沒有說家具都賣掉了；(B) 原文只寫到 Laura 來道別，沒有說所有朋友都知道。

stem: Which of the following is NOT true according to the passage?

options.A: Amy treasured the gold bracelet Laura gave her.
options.B: Amy turned and walked backwards as she left.
options.C: Amy’s father was not around when they were leaving.
options.D: Amy did not know if she could keep her promise to Laura.

ev.t: She watched as Laura walked down the block, turning and waving and walking backwards until she got to the corner.

note: 第 1 段說 Amy 看著 Laura 沿著街道走去，一邊轉身揮手，一邊倒退著走。倒退著走的是 Laura，不是 Amy，所以和原文不符的是 (B)。其他三個選項都和原文相符：Amy 一看就愛上手鍊，出門前還確定手鍊牢牢戴好，是 (A)；第 3 段說要是爸爸在這裡，可見爸爸不在，是 (C)；第 1 段 Amy 答應會回來看 Laura，卻不知道還會不會回來，是 (D)。

stem: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.A: Asians have used soybean produce for thousands of years.
options.B: Health-conscious Americans are using more tofu in their diet.
options.C: The soybean provides food for the world’s growing population.
options.D: The soybean is healthful and has become popular in the western world.

note: 第 1 段說西方世界重新發現了黃豆；第 2 段說黃豆幾乎是完美的蛋白質來源，對健康有種種好處；第 3 段說美國培育出好品種，黃豆成了健康食品的代表。全文的重點是黃豆有益健康，在西方世界流行起來，所以是 (D)。(A) 亞洲人用了黃豆幾千年、(C) 黃豆能為世界人口提供糧食，都只是第 1 段的細節，過於狹隘；(B) 美國人吃更多豆腐，只是第 3 段的例子，也過於狹隘。

stem: One major advantage of the soybean as a food source is that ______.

options.A: it is free of oil
options.B: it is cheap to produce
options.C: it is low in protein
options.D: it is high in cholesterol

ev.t: Since it is cheap to produce and rich in protein, and has many uses,

note: 第 1 段說黃豆生產成本低（cheap to produce）、富含蛋白質、用途又多，所以是 (B)。另外三個選項都是對的東西放錯地方：(A) 照抄第 2 段的 free of，不含的是膽固醇，第 3 段還說美國培育出含油量高的品種；(C) 照抄 protein，原文說富含（rich in）蛋白質，選項卻說含量低；(D) 照抄第 2 段的 cholesterol，原文說黃豆不含膽固醇，還能降低膽固醇。

stem: The soybean helps to keep cholesterol down mainly because it contains ______.

options.A: rich protein
options.B: rich vitamin
options.C: some fatty acids
options.D: high fiber content

ev.t: the soy oil contains some special substances, called Omega 3 fatty acids, which reduce cholesterol

note: 第 2 段說黃豆油含有 Omega 3 脂肪酸（fatty acids），可以降低膽固醇（reduce cholesterol），所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄 high fiber content，高纖維說的是預防消化方面的疾病，和膽固醇無關；(A) 照抄 protein，第 2 段最後一句雖然說每天吃 25 公克黃豆蛋白能降低膽固醇，但題幹問的是主要原因（mainly because），原文直接說明能降低膽固醇的成分是脂肪酸；(B) 維生素，原文沒有提到。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?

options.A: Tofu is a rich protein source.
options.B: Soybean protein prevents digestive problems.
options.C: The United States exports most of its soybean produce to Canada.
options.D: Vegetarians should eat less than 25 grams of soy protein every day.

ev.t: The soybean is an almost perfect source of protein.
tofu, the most popular soybean product,

note: 第 2 段說黃豆幾乎是完美的蛋白質來源；第 3 段說豆腐是最受歡迎的黃豆製品。把兩句合起來，豆腐是豐富的蛋白質來源，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 digestive，能預防消化疾病的是黃豆的纖維，不是蛋白質；(C) 照抄第 3 段的 Canada，加拿大是和美國一起做研究的國家，原文沒有說美國把黃豆出口到加拿大；(D) 照抄 25 grams，原文說的是膽固醇過高的人每天至少（a minimum of）吃 25 公克，不是吃素的人要少於 25 公克。

stem: The passage is mainly about ______.

options.A: the personality tendencies of older children
options.B: the personality tendencies of younger children
options.C: the relation between birth rank and job success
options.D: the relation between birth rank and personality

note: 第 1 段寫哥哥姊姊的個性傾向，第 2 段用 By contrast 轉到後來出生的孩子，兩段對照出生順序和個性的關係，所以是 (D)。(A) 只講年紀大的孩子，是第 1 段的內容，過於狹隘；(B) 只講年紀小的孩子，是第 2 段的內容，也過於狹隘；(C) 文章雖然提到老大傾向教書、從政，後來出生的孩子可能是好的推銷員，但說的是個性適合哪些工作，沒有談工作成不成功，偏離主題。

stem: According to the passage, the first child tends to be ______.

options.A: creative
options.B: sociable
options.C: persuasive
options.D: conservative

ev.t: Research also suggests that firstborn children generally become more conservative than other children

note: 第 1 段說研究指出老大一般比其他孩子保守（more conservative），所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 creative、(B) 照抄 sociable，第 2 段說傾向創作領域、善於交際的是後來出生的孩子，第 1 段反而說老大比較不善交際；(C) 第 2 段說說服是後來出生的孩子面對哥哥姊姊的工具，也不是老大的特質。

stem: It can be inferred from the passage that a younger child is more likely to be a good ______.

options.A: librarian
options.B: doctor
options.C: writer
options.D: teacher

ev.t: This may help explain why younger children tend to favor the creative fields such as music, art, and writing.

note: 第 2 段說年紀小的孩子傾向選擇音樂、藝術、寫作（writing）這類創作領域，從事寫作就是作家（writer），所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄第 1 段的 teaching，傾向教書、從政的是習慣照顧別人的老大；(A) 圖書館員、(B) 醫生，原文都沒有提到。

stem: From the passage, we learn that ______.

options.A: children’s personalities depend entirely on parental attitudes
options.B: artists do not usually like to make decisions for other people
options.C: older children are used to taking care of people and are fun to be with
options.D: younger children are particularly weak in delivering a speech in public

ev.t: may be uncomfortable making decisions for others.
This may help explain why younger children tend to favor the creative fields such as music, art, and writing.

note: 第 2 段說後來出生的孩子替別人做決定（making decisions for others）時可能會不自在，接著用 This may help explain why 說明，這也許就是他們傾向音樂、藝術、寫作這類創作領域的原因。也就是說，從事藝術的人通常不喜歡替別人做決定，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 parental，原文說父母的期望和管教有影響，選項卻說個性完全（entirely）取決於父母的態度，說得太過頭；(C) 習慣照顧別人的是老大，大家喜歡相處（enjoyable to be around）的卻是第 2 段年紀小的孩子，選項把兩者接在一起；(D) 當眾演講，原文沒有提到。

stem: What is the major message the author is trying to convey to readers?

options.A: All people, especially those working in the hospitals, should reduce the use of plastics.
options.B: Americans should lead the world to fight dioxin pollution, or mankind will die out soon.
options.C: We had better eat more vegetables than meat in order to reduce the risk of dioxin pollution.
options.D: We had better not breastfeed our babies, since babies are most likely to be poisoned by dioxin.

note: 第 1 段說醫院大量使用的 PVC 塑膠燃燒後產生戴奧辛，散布到全世界，每個人都不斷接觸到；第 2 段說醫療廢棄物裡的塑膠愈來愈多，最後呼籲醫師和護理師帶頭減少醫院裡的塑膠用量。作者要傳達的是大家，尤其是醫院裡的人，應該少用塑膠，所以是 (A)。三個錯誤選項都偏離主題：(B) 原文沒有要美國領導全世界，也沒有說人類快要滅亡；(C) 原文說的是戴奧辛透過飼料進入肉類和乳製品，沒有建議多吃蔬菜；(D) 第 1 段雖然說嬰兒最容易受害，卻沒有叫大家不要餵母奶。

stem: Dioxin is produced ______.

options.A: when plastics are burned
options.B: in the making of hospital blood bags
options.C: when reusables are disposed of
options.D: in the handling of all kinds of medical waste

ev.t: Dioxin is an unwanted byproduct that is created when PVC is burned.

note: 第 1 段說戴奧辛是燃燒 PVC 時（when PVC is burned）產生的副產品，PVC 就是一種塑膠，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 blood bags，血袋是用 PVC 做的，製造血袋時不會產生戴奧辛，燒掉時才會；(D) 照抄 medical waste，醫療廢棄物是戴奧辛的主要來源，原因是裡面的塑膠拿去燒，不是處理任何醫療廢棄物都會產生；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 reusables，可重複使用的用品是作者希望恢復使用的，方向正好相反。

stem: What does it in the last line refer to?

options.A: Dioxin.
options.B: Cancer.
options.C: Medical waste.
options.D: Use of plastics.

ev.t: After all, they can’t be treating cancer on the inside of hospitals and contributing to it on the outside.

note: 最後一句把醫院裡和醫院外對照：在醫院裡治療癌症（treating cancer on the inside），在醫院外又助長它（contributing to it on the outside）。治療和助長的是同一樣東西，it 指的就是前面的 cancer，所以是 (B)。另外三個選項 (A) Dioxin、(C) Medical waste、(D) Use of plastics 都在第 2 段出現過，但醫院裡治療的是病，不是戴奧辛、醫療廢棄物或塑膠的使用；它們是在醫院外助長癌症的原因，填進 it 的位置，前後的對照就接不上。

stem: Which of the following statements can be inferred from the article?

options.A: Living in the countryside will keep one safe from dioxin poisoning.
options.B: Dioxin can be released from our bodies, if we drink a lot of clean, pure water.
options.C: Using reusables as people did in the old days will help lessen dioxin pollution.
options.D: You have to lose weight, or the amount of dioxin in your body fat will kill you.

ev.t: Plastics used to account for as little as 10% of medical waste in the late 1970s, before disposables began rapidly replacing reusables.
Dioxin is an unwanted byproduct that is created when PVC is burned.

note: 第 2 段說 1970 年代末期拋棄式用品開始取代可重複使用的用品（reusables）之前，塑膠只占醫療廢棄物的 10% 左右，現在多達 30%；第 1 段說戴奧辛是燃燒 PVC 塑膠產生的。塑膠廢棄物變多，是因為改用拋棄式用品，像以前一樣用可重複使用的東西，就能減少戴奧辛汙染，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄 fat，原文說戴奧辛儲存在脂肪裡，沒有說減重能解決問題；(A) 第 1 段說戴奧辛散布到全世界，每個人都不斷接觸到，住在鄉下也一樣；(B) 喝水能排出戴奧辛，原文沒有提到。

stem: The passage is written mainly to describe ______.

options.A: what the author looks like
options.B: what “life” means to the author
options.C: what a typical day is like for the author
options.D: what kinds of people the author works with

note: 第 1 段依時間順序寫作者一天的作息：幾點到公司、換制服、值班、吃午餐、休息、下班；第 2 段寫上班時做些什麼、遇到哪些人。全文描述的是作者典型的一天，所以是 (C)。(A) 照鏡子確定自己看起來整齊，只是第 1 段的細節，過於狹隘；(B)「上上下下」的生活只在第 2 段最後一句出現，也過於狹隘；(D) 各式各樣的乘客只是第 2 段的內容，也過於狹隘。

stem: We may infer from the passage that the author is a(n) ______.

options.A: policeman
options.B: driver
options.C: floor cleaner
options.D: elevator operator

ev.t: I always call out floors very clearly
Most men take off their hats in my car,
my life can be described as consisting of a series of “ups” and “downs.”

note: 第 2 段有三個線索：作者總是把樓層報得很清楚（call out floors）、男士進了他的車廂（car）會脫帽、他的生活是一連串的「上上下下」。報樓層、有車廂、整天上上下下，作者是電梯操作員，所以是 (D)。這裡的 car 指電梯車廂，不是汽車，所以不是 (B) 司機。(C) 照抄 floor，floor cleaner 是清潔地板的人，原文的 floors 是樓層；(A) 警察，原文沒有線索。

stem: The expression “constantly on the move” in the passage refers to the fact that ______.

options.A: the author always calls out floors very clearly
options.B: the author seldom stays in one place for a long while
options.C: the author meets all kinds of people and talks to everyone
options.D: the author frequently helps passengers move their baggage

ev.t: I always call out floors very clearly, and I am constantly on the move.

note: on the move 是一直在移動。電梯操作員整天跟著電梯上上下下，很少在一個地方停留很久，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄同一句前半的 floors very clearly，那是 and 前面的另一件事；(C) 照抄 all kinds of people，那是他喜歡這份工作的原因；(D) 照抄 move，move their baggage 是搬行李，原文沒有說作者幫乘客搬東西。

stem: What is the best title for the passage?

options.A: Magical Tricks
options.B: A Great Magician
options.C: Magic as Entertainment
options.D: The History of Magic

note: 第 1 段從西元前 1700 年的埃及說起，第 2 段寫古希臘和羅馬，第 3 段寫 1800 年代以前、19 世紀到今天。全文依時間順序介紹魔術的發展，所以是 (D)。(A) 戲法只是第 1、2 段舉的例子，過於狹隘；(B) 偉大的魔術師只講到第 3 段的 Robert Houdin，也過於狹隘；(C) 魔術成為娛樂只是第 3 段最後一句，也過於狹隘。

stem: In ancient Greece, what did the priests do to show people they had unusual power?

options.A: They performed magical tricks to entertain people.
options.B: They made the statues in the temples drink wine as they wished.
options.C: They treated the people with wine flowing down from statues’ mouths.
options.D: They built magic devices in the temples to make doors open by themselves.

ev.t: This explains why at that time the priests even built magic devices into their temples.
These devices made it possible for doors to open by themselves
This was done mainly to convince people that the priests were powerful.

note: 第 2 段說祭司在神殿裡裝了魔法機關，能讓門自己打開（open by themselves），這麼做主要是要讓人們相信祭司的法力強大，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 entertain，表演給人看的是埃及的魔術師 Dedi，不是希臘的祭司；(C) 照抄 statues’ mouths，原文說酒從雕像嘴裡流出來，是用來顯示法力，不是請人喝酒；(B) 照抄 statues，原文是酒從雕像裡流出來，不是讓雕像喝酒，方向弄反了。

stem: What did people think of magic before 1800?

options.A: Magic should be used only in temples.
options.B: Magic could only be performed in a circus.
options.C: Magic was performed by freaks and doctors.
options.D: Magic was the major daily activity for the pharaohs.

ev.t: Magicians were thought of as freaks and were only allowed to perform in a circus.

note: 第 3 段說 1800 年代以前，魔術師只准在馬戲團表演（only allowed to perform in a circus），所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 freaks，同一句說魔術師給人看成怪胎，但魔術師能加上 Dr. 或 MD 的頭銜，是 19 世紀 Robert Houdin 出現以後的事；(A) 照抄第 2 段的 temples，在神殿裡裝機關是古希臘、羅馬祭司的做法，不是只能在神殿用；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 pharaoh，原文只說 Dedi 曾為法老表演。

stem: Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: Magic began about 3,700 years ago.
options.B: Dedi of Dedsnefu performed magic for kings only.
options.C: Robert Houdin was the first magician to perform magic.
options.D: The “Cups and Balls” trick has been performed for about 1,700 years.

ev.t: Magic is believed to have begun with the Egyptians, in 1700 BC.

note: 第 1 段說魔術起源於西元前 1700 年。從西元前 1700 年到這份考卷的年代，大約是 1700＋2000＝3,700 年，所以是 (A)。(D) 把西元前 1700 年當成 1,700 年前，「杯與球」是 Dedi 擅長的戲法，也有大約 3,700 年了；(B) 照抄 king，原文說 Dedi 也表演給建造金字塔的奴隸看，不是只為國王表演；(C) 照抄第 3 段的 Robert Houdin，他是改變大家看法的魔術師，最早的魔術師是第 1 段的 Dedi。

stem: Doctor medicine ______.

options.A: has a longer history than folk medicine
options.B: has been practiced for around 1,600 years
options.C: bases its treatments on observation and logic
options.D: was very successful in curing sicknesses in ancient times

ev.t: Scientific doctors try to observe sicknesses, look for logical patterns, and then find out how the human body works.

note: 第 1 段說科學派的醫生觀察（observe）疾病、尋找合乎邏輯（logical）的規律，再推敲出哪些療法可能有效，選項換成名詞 observation and logic，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄 successful，原文說這種醫學今天很成功，在古代治好的病人卻不多；(A) 照抄第 2 段的 folk medicine，原文說民俗醫學在科學醫學之前很久就很興盛，歷史比較長的是民俗醫學；(B) 原文說始於西元前 4 世紀，到今天大約 2,300 多年，不是 1,600 年。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT used in health spas?

options.A: Magic power.
options.B: Various herbs.
options.C: Religious faith.
options.D: A healthy life style.

ev.t: Other times, a magician may make you a magic charm, or say a spell, to cure you.
Some religious groups organize special healing shrines for the sick.
In these places people rest, get plenty of sleep, eat healthy food, drink water instead of wine, and exercise in various ways.

note: 第 3 段介紹健康療養所：魔法師做護身符、唸咒語，是 (A) 魔法；宗教團體設立療養聖所、向神明祈禱，是 (C) 宗教信仰；在那裡休息、睡飽、吃健康的食物、運動，是 (D) 健康的生活方式。各種草藥是第 2 段民俗醫學用的方法，不屬於健康療養所，所以選 (B)。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?

options.A: Folk healers choose different herbs to cure diseases without any sound basis.
options.B: People who practice folk medicine need lots of formal education on herbs.
options.C: The success of folk medicine led to the development of doctor medicine.
options.D: Natural cures worked better than scientific medicine in ancient times.

ev.t: was more successful in ancient times than doctor medicine.

note: 第 2 段說民俗醫學在古代比醫生醫學更成功（more successful），自然療法就是民俗醫學，醫生醫學就是科學醫學，選項換成 worked better，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 herbs，原文說民俗療者也運用觀察和邏輯，試到有效才一直用，不是毫無根據；(C) 照抄 development，原文只說民俗醫學在科學醫學發展之前就很興盛，沒有說前者促成了後者；(B) 原文說用草藥治病的是教育程度比較低的人，正好相反。

stem: The author’s primary purpose in this passage is to ______.

options.A: describe different types of medicine
options.B: argue for the importance of medicine in health care
options.C: show the crucial role religion plays in medical treatments
options.D: compare the educational background of three different types of patients

note: 第 1 段開頭說醫學有三個分支，接著第 1、2、3 段依序介紹醫生醫學、民俗醫學和信仰治療。作者寫這篇文章是要說明不同種類的醫學，所以是 (A)。(C) 宗教只出現在第 3 段的信仰治療，過於狹隘；(B) 文章只是說明，沒有主張醫學在保健上有多重要，偏離主題；(D) 文章比較的是三種醫學，提到教育程度的是第 2 段的民俗療者，不是病人，也偏離主題。

stem: What is the best title for this passage?

options.A: The Importance of Marketing
options.B: The Power of Youth Culture
options.C: The Popularity of Hip-hop Fashion
options.D: The Success of Tommy Hilfiger

note: 第 1 段說行銷人員利用青少年文化推銷產品，第 2 段說饒舌音樂和瑪丹娜的例子，正好說明青少年文化影響力多大，第 3 段說 Tommy Hilfiger 非常清楚青少年文化的力量。三段都在講青少年文化的影響力，所以是 (B)。(C) 嘻哈服飾只是第 1 段的例子，過於狹隘；(D) Tommy Hilfiger 的成功只是第 3 段的例子，也過於狹隘；(A) 行銷的重要性，範圍比文章大得多，太過廣泛。

stem: How much money do sales of rap music and videos together make each year?

options.A: More than $1 billion.
options.B: Between $750 million and $1 billion.
options.C: Between $500 million and $750 million.
options.D: Less than $500 million.

ev.t: It is reported that hip-hop fashion alone generates $750 million to $1 billion annually.
Sales of rap music and videos each exceed that amount.

note: 這一題要分清楚兩句話各在說什麼。第 1 段說光是嘻哈服飾（hip-hop fashion alone）每年就有 7.5 億到 10 億美元；下一句說饒舌音樂和音樂錄影帶的銷售額各自（each）都超過這個數字（that amount）。題目問的是饒舌音樂和音樂錄影帶加起來（together）的金額：兩樣各自超過 7.5 億，加起來至少超過 15 億，一定超過 10 億美元，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 $750 million to $1 billion，那是嘻哈服飾的營收，不是音樂和錄影帶的；(C) 5 億到 7.5 億、(D) 不到 5 億美元，連其中一樣的銷售額都不到，和「各自超過 7.5 億」矛盾。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?

options.A: The purchasing power of teenagers has been decreasing over the years.
options.B: Many teenagers make a lot of profits in the fashion market today.
options.C: Madonna led the fashion of wearing underwear outside clothes.
options.D: Marketers recognize youth culture as a part of hip-hop culture.

ev.t: Soon after that, adolescent girls around the world began wearing their underwear outside their clothes.

note: 第 2 段說瑪丹娜露出胸罩登上排行榜，不久之後（Soon after that）世界各地的少女開始把內衣穿在衣服外面，可見這股風潮是瑪丹娜帶起來的，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄第 1 段的 hip-hop culture，原文說嘻哈文化是青少年文化的一個例子，選項卻反過來說青少年文化是嘻哈文化的一部分；(B) 照抄 profit，原文說獲利最高的是青少年消費市場，賺錢的是做生意的人，不是青少年；(A) 原文說青少年市場是有史以來獲利最高的，購買力並沒有下降。
map: wearing their underwear outside their clothes

stem: It can be inferred from the passage that Hilfiger ______.

options.A: believed that MTV stars could drive fashion trends among teens
options.B: sold Nintendo terminals together with teens’ clothes in his stores
options.C: sponsored a Nintendo competition out of his own interest in computer games
options.D: was rated by teens and adults as the best designer of jeans around the world in 2000

ev.t: Fashion designer Tommy Hilfiger was fully aware of the power of youth culture.
He marketed his brand by giving clothes to famous MTV stars and featuring teen stars in his print ads.

note: 第 3 段說 Hilfiger 非常清楚青少年文化的力量，所以送衣服給有名的 MTV 明星，請青少年明星拍廣告。他這樣做，可見他相信 MTV 明星能帶動青少年的時尚潮流，所以是 (A)。(C) 照抄 computer games，喜歡電玩的是青少年，不是 Hilfiger 自己；(B) 照抄 Nintendo terminals，遊戲機是裝在店裡吸引青少年的，原文沒有說拿來賣；(D) 照抄 2000，2000 年的調查是青少年把 Hilfiger 牛仔褲評為第一名的品牌，評分的只有青少年，也不是全世界最好的設計師。

stem: Folk tales are usually the stories of ______.

options.A: wise scholars
options.B: brave princes
options.C: greedy folk
options.D: ordinary people

ev.t: They often concern very strong or clever people who come from humble backgrounds.

note: 第 1 段說民間故事的主角常常是出身卑微（come from humble backgrounds）的人；第 2 段也說民間故事能把平凡的小人物（humble people）變成英雄。選項換成 ordinary people，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄 folk，folk tales 的 folk 是「民間的」，原文沒有說故事寫的是貪心的人；(A) 有學問的學者、(B) 勇敢的王子，原文都沒有提到，而且王子正好不是出身卑微的人。

stem: Which of the following statements about tall tales is NOT TRUE?

options.A: Tall tales are factual stories.
options.B: It takes imagination to create tall tales.
options.C: Tall tales overstate the power of humans.
options.D: People are serious when telling tall tales.

ev.t: Many folk tales are also tall tales—stories of unbelievable events told with perfect seriousness.
A tall tale, in other words, is a story in which the truth has been exaggerated.

note: 第 2 段說誇張故事講的是令人難以置信的事件，換句話說，是把事實誇大了（the truth has been exaggerated）的故事。民間故事原本也許有事實根據，但說成誇張故事以後，已經不是照事實講的故事，所以和原文不符的是 (A)。其他三個選項都和原文相符：同一段說靠著想像的力量，民間故事能把小人物變成英雄，是 (B)；事實誇大了，就是 (C) 把人的能力說得太過頭；用一本正經的口氣講（told with perfect seriousness），是 (D)。

stem: According to this passage, folk tales ______.

options.A: are written by native writers
options.B: explain the origin of world literature
options.C: reveal people’s ideas about life
options.D: teach people how to survive

ev.t: By reading and listening to folk tales, we may gain a better understanding of the true values, beliefs, and goals of a people.

note: 第 3 段說閱讀和聆聽民間故事，能讓我們更了解一個民族真正的價值觀、信仰和目標（values, beliefs, and goals），選項換成 ideas about life，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄 literature，原文說民間故事是一個文化的文學裡重要的部分，沒有說它說明了世界文學的起源；(A) 第 1 段說民間故事是口耳相傳的，不是由當地作家寫成的；(D) 教人怎麼活下去，原文沒有提到。

stem: In the past, the signatures of athletes and VIPs ______.

options.A: were highly priced
options.B: cost nothing at all
options.C: attracted great attention
options.D: were for sale to the public

ev.t: It used to be that athletes and VIPs gave away their signatures for free,

note: 第 1 段說以前（It used to be that）運動員和名人都是免費（for free）送簽名的，選項換成 cost nothing，所以是 (B)。(A) 價錢很高、(D) 公開販售，都是 But nowadays 之後第 2 段說的現在的情形，把時間弄反了；(C) 原文說以前簽名的東西只是擺在架子上積灰塵，並沒有引起很大的注意。

stem: According to this passage, many people now collect athletes’ and VIPs’ signatures ______.

options.A: for their artistic value
options.B: to show them off to their friends
options.C: as historical documents
options.D: to be associated with famous people

ev.t: To connect with someone famous, or maybe even to imagine themselves as the hero they admire.

note: 第 4 段問收藏家想要簽名真正的原因是什麼，接著回答：為了和名人有所連結（connect with someone famous），選項換成 to be associated with famous people，所以是 (D)。(C) 歷史文件容易聯想到第 3 段愛因斯坦的手稿和達文西的筆記，但那是說簽名的東西能賣到多少錢，不是收藏的原因；(A) 藝術價值、(B) 向朋友炫耀，原文都沒有提到。

stem: The overall tone (attitude) of this passage is ______.

options.A: factual
options.B: ironic
options.C: negative
options.D: enthusiastic

note: 第 1 段對比以前和現在，第 2、3 段列出簽名的價錢和實例：愛因斯坦手稿賣 398,500 美元、比爾蓋茲花 3,080 萬美元買達文西的筆記，第 4 段說明收藏的原因。全文用事實和數字說明簽名成了大生意，作者沒有加上自己的褒貶，所以語氣是 (A) 就事論事。作者沒有嘲諷收藏家，不是 (B)；沒有批評，不是 (C)；也沒有熱烈鼓吹大家去收藏，不是 (D)。

stem: Recently a health survey was carried out in Taiwan to determine ______.

options.A: why people ignore their health
options.B: when to teach health education
options.C: what people know about health
options.D: who is more likely to become ill

ev.t: More than 2,000 adults took part in the survey to find out about their knowledge of diet, healthcare, disease control, and medication.

note: 原文說超過 2,000 名成年人參加調查，目的是了解他們在飲食、保健、疾病防治和用藥方面的知識（their knowledge），選項換成 what people know about health，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄 health education，健康教育的前景是調查結果帶出來的看法，不是調查要了解什麼時候教；(A) 開頭說大家忽略健康，是因為忙著讀書和工作，這是作者的說明，不是調查的目的；(D) 調查問的是知識，不是誰比較容易生病。

stem: According to the article, which of the following is TRUE about medicines for colds?

options.A: They can cure the common cold.
options.B: Many Taiwanese take too many of them.
options.C: Doctors often refuse to sell them.
options.D: About 51 percent of patients use them.

ev.t: The problem is made worse by doctors who give their patients large doses of useless drugs.

note: 原文說感冒吃藥完全沒有用，有些醫生卻給病人開大量沒有用的藥，讓問題更嚴重。醫生開了大量的感冒藥，可見很多人吃了太多感冒藥，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄 cure，原文說的是感冒沒有藥能治好（has no cure），正好相反；(C) 照抄 doctors，原文說醫生開大量的藥，不是拒絕賣藥；(D) 照抄 51 percent，51% 是知道感冒沒有藥能治好的受訪者，不是吃感冒藥的病人。

stem: According to the survey, most Taiwanese believe that ______.

options.A: nicotine alone makes people fall victim to cancer
options.B: only a small percentage of smokers will develop cancer
options.C: smoking fewer cigarettes decreases the risk of cancer
options.D: other chemicals besides nicotine cause lung diseases

ev.t: More than two-thirds believe that it is only the nicotine in cigarettes rather than the other chemicals that cause cancer.

note: 原文說超過三分之二的人相信，香菸裡只有尼古丁（only the nicotine）會致癌，選項換成 nicotine alone，所以是 (A)。(D) 照抄 other chemicals，原文說這些人相信致癌的不是其他化學物質，正好相反；(C) 照抄 cigarettes，他們以為抽尼古丁比較少的「淡菸」不會得癌症，說的是菸的種類，不是抽的數量；(B) 照抄 percent，26% 是台灣成年人抽菸的比例，不是抽菸的人得癌症的比例。

stem: The results of the survey show that ______.

options.A: the health statistics in Taiwan are neglected
options.B: there is hope for improvement in the younger generation
options.C: the older generation depends on the healthcare system
options.D: many people value a career over their health

ev.t: But the outlook for health education in Taiwan is not all negative.
The survey concludes that younger Taiwanese have a better understanding of health concerns than their parents,

note: 原文說台灣健康教育的前景並不全然悲觀（not all negative），調查的結論是年輕一代對健康問題的了解比父母好，選項換成年輕一代還有改善的希望（hope），所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄 neglected，原文說大家忽略的是健康問題，不是健康統計數字；(D) 開頭說大家忙著讀書和工作而忽略健康，這是作者的說明，不是調查的結果，題幹問的是調查顯示什麼；(C) 原文說年紀最大的人了解得最少，沒有說他們依賴醫療體系。

stem: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of the digital camera over the film camera?

options.A: The user has to spend additional money for it.
options.B: It comes in many models for the customer.
options.C: It saves money from unwanted pictures.
options.D: Its pictures can be sent by e-mail.

ev.t: Although there are extra costs involved in going digital
And there are plenty of models from which to choose
With digital cameras, you aren’t spending money on film for wasted pictures,
or sent by e-mail.

note: 第 3 段說改用數位相機會有額外的花費（extra costs），像是記憶卡和特殊相紙，這是數位相機的缺點，不是優點，所以選 (A)。其他三個都是原文說的優點：第 2 段可以選擇的機型很多，是 (B)；第 1 段不必把錢花在白費照片的底片上，是 (C)；第 3 段照片可以用電子郵件寄出去，是 (D)。

stem: According to this passage, the American households using digital cameras will increase if ______.

options.A: their producers invest more money
options.B: their operation becomes simpler
options.C: their salesmen are more friendly
options.D: their quality keeps improving

ev.t: as manufacturers introduce more and more cameras whose quality is as good as film cameras.

note: 第 4 段說隨著（as）製造商推出愈來愈多畫質（quality）和底片相機一樣好的機種，使用數位相機的家庭一定會增加，選項換成品質不斷提升，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄第 2 段的 simple，簡單相機只是各種機型當中的一種，原文沒有說操作變簡單就會增加；(C) 照抄第 5 段的 salesmen，業務員只是預期數位相機會是熱門禮物；(A) 原文說的是製造商推出好的機種，不是投資更多錢。

stem: Which of the following is NOT TRUE about film cameras?

options.A: Their pictures can be printed at a photo shop.
options.B: Their pictures can be enlarged as desired.
options.C: Their pictures can be seen before they are printed.
options.D: Their pictures can be stored for a long time.

ev.t: Digital cameras offer more than just the instant previewing of pictures on small color screens.

note: 第 3 段說數位相機能在小螢幕上立即預覽（instant previewing）照片，這是數位相機才有的功能；底片相機的照片要沖洗出來才看得到，所以和事實不符的是 (C)。(A) 在相片沖印店印照片、(B) 照片可以放大、(D) 照片可以保存很久，文章雖然沒有提到，卻都是底片相機做得到的事，和原文也不衝突。

stem: According to this article, digital cameras nowadays are used mainly by ______.

options.A: professionals
options.B: amateurs
options.C: housewives
options.D: students

ev.t: to $1,000 wonders with all the features that any advanced amateur could want.
Soon, even professionals will use them.

note: 第 2 段說最高檔的機種具備進階業餘玩家（advanced amateur）想要的所有功能；第 4 段說不久之後，連（even）專業攝影師也會用數位相機。不久之後才會用，表示專業攝影師現在還不太用，目前使用數位相機的主要是業餘的人，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄第 4 段的 professionals，那是將來的事；(C) 家庭主婦、(D) 學生，原文都沒有提到。

stem: With a digital camera, it is necessary to ______.

options.A: carry a lot of film
options.B: print pictures at a photo shop
options.C: have a memory card
options.D: spend more time in using it

ev.t: the cost of memory cards for storage
With a large memory card to store pictures,

note: 第 3 段說改用數位相機要多花錢買儲存用的記憶卡（memory cards）；第 5 段也說有了大容量的記憶卡，就能一直拍照。用數位相機一定要有記憶卡，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 5 段的 film，帶 30 捲底片旅行是底片相機的麻煩；(B) 照抄 print，第 3 段說數位相機的照片在家裡就能輕鬆印出來，不必到相片沖印店；(D) 花更多時間使用，原文沒有提到。

stem: How long had Tim and Dom been at sea when their boat was hit by a fishing boat?

options.A: One month.
options.B: Two months.
options.C: Three months.
options.D: Four months.

ev.t: They set out from Japan on May 17, 2001.
their boat was hit by a fishing ship on September 17, 2001.

note: 第 2 段說他們 5 月 17 日從日本出發，9 月 17 日一艘漁船撞上他們的船。從 5 月 17 日到 9 月 17 日，剛好是 6、7、8、9 四個月，所以是 (D)。(A) 一個月只到 6 月 17 日，(B) 兩個月只到 7 月 17 日，(C) 三個月只到 8 月 17 日，都還沒到出事那天。

stem: According to Dom, the main reason for the accident was that ______.

options.A: Tim and Dom were too careless
options.B: nobody on the fishing ship saw them
options.C: the speed of the fishing ship was too fast
options.D: their rowboat was not strong enough

ev.t: A fishing ship came towards us with nobody on the bridge and ran us down.

note: 第 4 段 Dom 說漁船朝他們開過來時，駕駛台（bridge）上一個人都沒有（nobody），就這樣把他們撞翻了；後來漁船上的人出現了，才看到他在水裡。駕駛台上沒有人，所以沒有人看到他們，答案是 (B)。這裡的 bridge 是船上的駕駛台，不是橋。(C) 原文說一切發生得太快（It all happened so quickly），說的是事情發生得很突然，不是漁船開得太快；(A) 兩人太粗心、(D) 划艇不夠堅固，Dom 都沒有這樣說。

stem: Dom said that the most important thing in this accident was ______.

options.A: both of them survived
options.B: they enjoyed this journey
options.C: their rowboat was not damaged
options.D: they failed to reach San Francisco

ev.t: But we are alive.
That above everything is the most important.

note: 第 4 段最後 Dom 說：我們還活著（we are alive），這比什麼都重要，選項換成兩人都活了下來（survived），所以是 (A)。(D) 照抄 San Francisco，沒能抵達舊金山是讓他們失望的事，不是最重要的事；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 damaged，原文說船嚴重損壞，正好相反；(B) 原文沒有說他們很享受這趟航程。

stem: People enter the world of fantasy for the following reasons EXCEPT that ______.

options.A: the world of fantasy frightens us
options.B: the real world is often disappointing
options.C: we can find happy endings there
options.D: we can always have our wishes fulfilled

ev.t: It is not always fair or kind.
And in the real world there are not always happy endings.
a place where things always go our way and there is always a happy ending.

note: 第 1 段說現實世界不一定公平、也不一定友善，是 (B) 現實世界常令人失望；奇幻世界總是有快樂的結局（happy ending），是 (C)；事情總是順著我們的意（go our way），是 (D) 願望總能實現。文章沒有說奇幻世界讓人害怕，而且人們是想逃進去，不會因為害怕而進去，所以選 (A)。

stem: Superman, Peter Pan, and Harry Potter have charmed many people, because ______.

options.A: the bad guys always have the upper hand
options.B: they end up getting married to beautiful princesses
options.C: their solutions are anything but magical
options.D: they possess powers that ordinary people don’t have

ev.t: allow us to find some magical solutions to our problems.

For example, Superman always arrives in the nick of time to prevent a disaster from happening, Peter Pan can fly at will to tease the bad guy Captain Hook, and Harry Potter has his magic power to take revenge on his uncle, aunt and cousin, who always ill-treat him.

note: 第 3 段說這些故事讓我們為問題找到神奇的解決方法，接著用 For example 舉例：超人及時阻止災難、彼得潘想飛就飛、哈利波特有魔法。三個主角都有一般人沒有的能力，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄 magical，原文說解決方法很神奇，anything but magical 是「一點都不神奇」，正好相反；(A) 照抄 bad guy，原文是彼得潘捉弄壞人，占上風的不是壞人；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 beautiful princess，贏得公主芳心是第 2 段說我們幻想的事，不是這三個主角的故事。

stem: This article about fantasy literature is intended to ______.

options.A: criticize its unrealistic concepts
options.B: ridicule those people reading it
options.C: explain why people like to read it
options.D: teach people to avoid disasters

note: 第 1 段用 That is why 說明我們為什麼想逃進奇幻世界；第 2 段說我們想相信哪些奇幻的事；第 3 段用 The main reason is that 說明超人、彼得潘、哈利波特吸引人的原因。全文在解釋人們為什麼喜歡奇幻文學，所以是 (C)。(D) 阻止災難只是第 3 段超人的例子，過於狹隘；(A) 批評、(B) 嘲笑，文章對奇幻文學和讀者都沒有負面的評價，偏離主題。

stem: According to this passage, what did Marian Anderson do between 1917 and 1929?

options.A: She studied at a music school.
options.B: She sang for religious activities.
options.C: She sang at Town Hall in New York.
options.D: She studied voice in Europe.

ev.t: Unable to attend music school, she began her career as a singer for church gatherings.

note: 第 1 段說她 1917 年申請音樂學校，學校卻因為她是黑人而拒絕了她；她沒辦法上音樂學校，就開始在教會的聚會（church gatherings）中擔任歌手；1929 年才到歐洲。所以 1917 到 1929 年之間，她在宗教活動中唱歌，是 (B)。(A) 照抄 music school，她正是上不了音樂學校；(D) 照抄 Europe，到歐洲學聲樂是 1929 年以後的事；(C) 照抄 Town Hall，在紐約 Town Hall 演出是 1935 年回到美國以後的事。

stem: Toscanini thought that Marian Anderson ______.

options.A: had a very rare voice
options.B: sang occasionally in public
options.C: sang only once in many years
options.D: was seldom heard by people

ev.t: The famous conductor Toscanini praised her voice as “heard only once in a hundred years.”

note: 第 2 段說托斯卡尼尼稱讚她的歌聲一百年才聽得到一次（heard only once in a hundred years），也就是說這樣的歌聲非常少見，選項換成 a very rare voice，所以是 (A)。(C) 照抄 only once，原文說的是這樣的歌聲一百年才出現一次，不是她多年才唱一次；(D) 照抄 heard，原文是稱讚，不是說很少人聽過她唱歌；(B) 偶爾公開演唱，原文沒有提到。

stem: Anderson’s beautiful voice was first recognized ______.

options.A: at the Lincoln Memorial
options.B: in Washington, D.C.
options.C: in Europe
options.D: at the United Nations

ev.t: Her voice was widely praised throughout Europe.

note: 第 1 段說她 1929 年到歐洲學聲樂、演出，歌聲在歐洲各地（throughout Europe）廣受讚揚；1935 年回到美國以後，才成為頂尖的音樂會歌手。她的歌聲最早是在歐洲得到肯定，所以是 (C)。另外三個選項都照抄第 2 段：(B) 華盛頓特區、(A) 林肯紀念堂都是 1939 年的事，(D) 聯合國是 1958 年以後的事，都比歐洲晚。

stem: This passage shows that Anderson finally defeated racism in the U.S. by ______.

options.A: protesting to the government
options.B: appealing to the United Nations
options.C: demonstrating in the streets
options.D: working hard to perfect her art

ev.t: In 1929, she went to Europe to study voice and spent several years performing there.
In 1955, Anderson became the first black soloist to sing with the Metropolitan Opera of New York City.
Anderson eventually triumphed over racism.

note: 文章列出她每一次遇到種族歧視時的做法：上不了音樂學校，就到教會唱歌，再到歐洲學聲樂；不能在憲法大廳演唱，就改在林肯紀念堂唱給 75,000 人聽。她靠的是繼續學習、繼續演唱，最後成為第一位和大都會歌劇院同台的黑人獨唱家，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 United Nations，擔任聯合國代表、得到聯合國和平獎，是她成功之後得到的肯定，不是向聯合國申訴；(A) 向政府抗議、(C) 上街示威，原文都沒有提到。

stem: David Smith refers to himself as having been “a clothes addict,” because ______.

options.A: he often wore khaki pants and a sports shirt
options.B: he couldn’t stand a clean appearance
options.C: he wanted his clothes to look neat all the time
options.D: he didn’t want to spend much money on clothes

ev.t: I used to carry a fresh suit to work with me so I could change if my clothes got wrinkled.

note: 第 1 段 David 說他以前上班都會多帶一套乾淨的西裝，衣服皺了就換。他連衣服皺了都受不了，可見他要衣服隨時看起來整齊，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 khaki pants and a sports shirt，那是他現在的穿著，不是以前；(D) 照抄第 3 段的 money，省錢是支持休閒服的人說的理由，David 以前每天穿昂貴的西裝，正好相反；(B) 受不了整潔的外表，和原文正好相反。

trap.t: khaki pants and a sports shirt

stem: David Smith wears casual clothes now, because ______.

options.A: they make him feel at ease when working
options.B: he cannot afford to buy expensive clothes
options.C: he looks handsome in casual clothes
options.D: he no longer works for any company

ev.t: and I need to feel comfortable.

note: 第 1 段 David 說他工作比以前更賣力，所以需要穿得舒服（feel comfortable），選項換成 feel at ease，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 expensive，原文說他以前每天穿昂貴的西裝，沒有說他現在買不起；(D) 他現在還是穿休閒服到辦公室上班；(C) 穿休閒服比較帥，原文沒有提到。

stem: According to this passage, which of the following statements is FALSE?

options.A: Many employees don’t like a conservative dress code.
options.B: Comfortable clothes make employees more productive.
options.C: A casual clothes code is welcomed by young employees.
options.D: All the employers in the U.S. are for casual office wear.

ev.t: In a study conducted by Levi Strauss and Company, 85 percent of employers said that they believe that casual dress improves employee morale.
Only 4 percent of employers said that casual dress has a negative impact on productivity.

note: 第 3 段的研究說 85% 的雇主相信休閒服裝能提振士氣，另有 4% 的雇主說休閒服裝對生產力有負面影響。既然有雇主不贊成，就不是所有（All）雇主都支持，所以和原文不符的是 (D)。其他三個選項都和原文相符：軟體公司老闆說服裝規定保守就很難請到人，是 (A)、(C)；人穿著舒服的衣服時工作效率比較高，是 (B)。

stem: According to this passage, which of the following statements is TRUE?

options.A: Company workers started to dress down about twenty years ago.
options.B: Dress-down has become an everyday phenomenon since the early 90s.
options.C: “Dress-down Friday” was first given as a favor from employers.
options.D: Many workers want to wear casual clothes to impress people.

ev.t: What started out as an extra one-day-a-week benefit for employees has really become an everyday thing,

note: 第 2 段 Maisly Jones 說，「便服星期五」一開始只是每週多給員工一天的福利（benefit），選項換成雇主給的恩惠（favor），所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄 everyday，1990 年代初只限星期五，每天都穿休閒服是後來才變成的；(A) 1990 年代初開始，到這份考卷的年代只有十年左右，不是二十年；(D) 原文說員工想穿得舒服，不是想讓人留下好印象。

stem: In this passage, the following advantages of casual office wear are mentioned EXCEPT ______.

options.A: saving employees’ money
options.B: making employees more attractive
options.C: improving employees’ motivation
options.D: making employees happier

ev.t: Supporters of casual office wear also argue that a casual dress code helps them save money.
85 percent of employers said that they believe that casual dress improves employee morale.
Another reason is that people seem happier and more productive when they are wearing comfortable clothes.

note: 第 3 段提到的好處在選項裡都換了說法：休閒的服裝規定能幫他們省錢（save money），是 (A)；能提振員工士氣（morale），是 (C) 提高員工的幹勁；穿舒服的衣服時比較快樂（happier），是 (D)。同一段的 attract 說的是公司容易吸引新員工，不是員工變得更有吸引力，所以選 (B)。

stem: According to this passage, mass production of potato chips was made possible when ______.

options.A: potatoes could be peeled by machines
options.B: potatoes were peeled by a large number of cooks
options.C: there was a growing demand for them
options.D: they first appeared in a Saratoga restaurant

ev.t: In the 1920s a mechanical potato peeler was invented and soon there were potato chips in abundance.

note: 原文說因為馬鈴薯得用手削皮，洋芋片常常缺貨；1920 年代發明了削皮機（a mechanical potato peeler），很快洋芋片就多得是了（in abundance）。能夠大量生產，是因為馬鈴薯可以用機器削皮，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 peeled，原文說用手削皮很費時，正是缺貨的原因，找再多廚師也沒有解決；(D) 照抄 Saratoga，洋芋片最早出現在薩拉托加的餐廳，那時還在用手削皮；(C) 需求愈來愈大，造成的是缺貨，不是大量生產。

stem: According to this passage, the cook of the Moon Lake Restaurant ______.

options.A: enjoyed making potato chips very much
options.B: planned to sell potato chips everywhere
options.C: wanted to silence a complaining diner
options.D: was pleased that other guests liked the chips

ev.t: The cook’s plan to stop the dinner guest from complaining did not turn out as he had planned.

note: 原文說廚師火大了，想把馬鈴薯切得薄到客人沒辦法用叉子吃，計畫是要讓客人別再抱怨（stop the dinner guest from complaining），選項換成 silence a complaining diner，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄 pleased，感到滿意的是那位客人，不是廚師；(B) 照抄 sell，原文說的是餐廳後來開始賣小包裝，不是廚師一開始就打算到處賣；(A) 原文說廚師是在火大之下做出洋芋片的，不是很喜歡做。
map: stop the dinner guest from complaining

stem: Potato chips have been popular in the U.S. ______.

options.A: for more than 200 years
options.B: ever since 1920
options.C: for less than 100 years
options.D: since the 19th century

ev.t: Picture an elegant restaurant in Saratoga Springs, New York, in 1853.
A few years later, they were selling all over the United States.

note: 原文說洋芋片是 1853 年在紐約州的餐廳做出來的，幾年後就在美國各地都買得到，所以洋芋片從 19 世紀就在美國流行，是 (D)。(B) 照抄 1920，1920 年代是發明削皮機、洋芋片開始大量生產的時候，不是開始流行的時候；從 1853 年到這份考卷的年代，大約是 150 年，所以 (A) 超過 200 年、(C) 不到 100 年都不對。

stem: Which of the following statements about Alexander Dumas is FALSE?

options.A: He was a victim of racism.
options.B: He was well-educated.
options.C: He was the son of a general.
options.D: He was the grandson of a slave.

ev.t: But Dumas overcame poverty, the lack of formal education, and the hardship of racism to become one of the world’s most popular writers.

note: 第 3 段說大仲馬克服了貧窮、沒有受過正規教育（the lack of formal education）和種族歧視，才成為最受歡迎的作家之一。他沒有受過正規教育，所以和原文不符的是 (B)。其他三個選項都在第 3 段：同一句說他克服了種族歧視，是 (A)；他的父親當上將軍，是 (C)；他是海地奴隸的孫子，是 (D)。

stem: Alexander Dumas’s novels ______.

options.A: have lasted for less than 100 years
options.B: have been translated into more than 100 languages
options.C: have not been well received until recently
options.D: have fascinated readers for many years

ev.t: Even though they were written 150 years ago, Alexander Dumas’ action novels still excite millions of readers around the world, in close to a hundred languages.

note: 第 1 段說大仲馬的小說雖然是 150 年前寫的，至今仍讓（still excite）全世界數百萬的讀者看得興奮不已，選項換成多年來一直吸引讀者（have fascinated readers for many years），所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 languages，原文說將近（close to）一百種語言，不是超過一百種；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 recently，最近拍成電影的是《鐵面人》，小說一直都受歡迎；(A) 原文說是 150 年前寫的，不是不到 100 年。

stem: We may infer from the article that Dumas ______.

options.A: did not lead a colorful life
options.B: was a man who kept money to himself
options.C: was a generous and kind-hearted man
options.D: was a peace-loving writer

ev.t: After making a fortune by writing novels, he built a mansion outside Paris and kept it open to starving artists, friends, and even strangers.

note: 第 4 段說大仲馬寫小說發了財，在巴黎郊外蓋了一棟豪宅，開放給挨餓的藝術家、朋友，甚至陌生人。願意把自己的房子讓窮藝術家和陌生人來住，可見他慷慨又好心，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄 kept，原文是 kept it open，讓豪宅一直開放給別人，選項卻說他把錢留給自己，正好相反；(A) 同一段說他的人生就像他的動作小說，參加過三次革命，生活一點都不平淡；(D) 他參加革命，有人侮辱他就跟人打架，不是愛好和平的人。

stem: Zoe was trucked to an elephant orphanage because ______.

options.A: Tsavo National park needed a baby elephant
options.B: she could not find her way home
options.C: she was very young when she lost her mother
options.D: Daphne wanted to keep her as a pet

ev.t: Zoe was just 2 weeks old
Zoe’s mother had died and the baby was left alone.

note: 第 1 段說 Zoe 才出生兩週，媽媽就死了（mother had died），留下牠孤零零的，於是送到孤兒院，選項換成 she lost her mother，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 Tsavo National Park，察沃國家公園只是發現 Zoe 的地點附近，原文沒有說公園需要小象；(B) 原文說牠在市集裡四處遊蕩，送到孤兒院是因為失去了媽媽，不是找不到路回家；(D) 原文沒有說 Daphne 想把牠當寵物養，最終目標反而是把牠放回野外。

stem: The elephant orphanage is ______.

options.A: supported by the government
options.B: located inside Tsavo National Park
options.C: home to many kinds of animals
options.D: operated with personal funds

ev.t: the orphanage, which depends on private contributions,

note: 第 2 段說這家孤兒院靠私人捐款（private contributions）維持，選項換成 personal funds，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 Tsavo National Park，察沃國家公園是 Daphne 的丈夫創立的，孤兒院設在她奈洛比的家裡；(A) 靠私人捐款，就不是政府資助；(C) 原文說的是大象孤兒院，沒有說收容許多種動物。

stem: At Tsavo National Park, Zoe has been ______.

options.A: released to a wild herd to be protected
options.B: taught to adjust to life in the wild
options.C: allowed to wander in the village market
options.D: accompanied all the time by her keepers

ev.t: There her keepers have gradually introduced her to the ways of the wild, helping her to find food and water.

note: 第 3 段說在察沃國家公園的保護區，飼養員逐步帶 Zoe 認識野外的生活方式（the ways of the wild），幫牠找食物和水，選項換成學著適應野外的生活，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄 wild herd，放回野生象群是最終目標，可能還要好幾年，現在還沒有做到；(C) 照抄第 1 段的 village market，在村莊市集遊蕩是 Zoe 剛找到時的事；(D) 原文說和人類家人朝夕相處是在孤兒院的那一年，到了保護區是逐步學習獨立。

stem: According to this passage, Daphne would like to ______.

options.A: make elephants live in their own groups
options.B: set up as many orphanages as possible
options.C: sell ivory for maintaining the orphanage
options.D: send Zoe to a zoo in Europe or America

ev.t: the final aim is to release all of them to a wild herd.

note: 第 3 段說最終的目標是把小象全部放回野生的象群（a wild herd），讓大象和自己的同類生活在一起，選項換成 live in their own groups，所以是 (A)。(C) 照抄第 4 段的 ivory，Daphne 的夢想是禁止象牙、銷毀庫存的象牙，正好相反；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 orphanage，原文沒有說她想開更多孤兒院；(D) 把 Zoe 送到歐美的動物園，原文沒有提到。

stem: The ordinary woman’s leather shoe is considered unusual because ______.

options.A: it was an important clue to life in the past
options.B: it was found near a famous trail
options.C: it at one time belonged to a VIP
options.D: it was a fashionable shoe at that time

ev.t: But what is unique about this shoe is where it was found.
It was discovered on the Chilkoot Pass, the famous trail used by the people seeking gold in Alaska.

note: 第 1 段說這隻鞋特別（unique）的地方，在於它是在哪裡找到的：在奇爾庫特山徑，一條有名的山路（the famous trail），所以是 (B)。(D) 原文說這隻鞋是 1890 年代流行的款式，流行正是它普通的地方，不是特別的原因；(C) 原文說沒有人知道鞋子是誰的，看不出主人是重要人物；(A) 舊物品能讓人想像過去的生活，是第 1 段開頭講的一般道理，這隻鞋特別是因為發現的地點。

stem: According to this passage, many people who went to Alaska ______.

options.A: eventually became millionaires
options.B: brought with them many shoes
options.C: had conflicts with the Eskimos
options.D: were not properly equipped

ev.t: Unprepared for such a dangerous journey, many died of starvation and exposure to the cold weather.

note: 第 2 段說許多人對這麼危險的旅程毫無準備（Unprepared），死於飢餓和寒冷，選項換成 not properly equipped，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 millionaires，原文說他們希望（hoping）成為百萬富翁，沒有說後來真的發財；(B) 照抄第 1 段的 shoe，博物館裡只有一隻鞋，原文沒有說淘金客帶了很多鞋；(C) 和愛斯基摩人起衝突，原文沒有提到。

stem: The Canadian government made gold seekers bring one year’s supplies with them so that ______.

options.A: they would not die of hunger and cold
options.B: the army would have enough food for fighting a war
options.C: they could trade these goods with the Eskimos
options.D: the supplies would make Alaska prosperous

ev.t: Unprepared for such a dangerous journey, many died of starvation and exposure to the cold weather.
The Canadian government finally started requiring the gold seekers to bring one ton of supplies with them.
This was thought to be enough for a person to survive for one year.

note: 第 2 段先說許多人毫無準備，死於飢餓和寒冷（starvation and exposure to the cold weather），接著用 finally 說加拿大政府最後規定要帶一噸的補給品，足夠一個人活一年（survive for one year）。規定帶補給品，是為了讓淘金客不再餓死、凍死，選項換成 die of hunger and cold，所以是 (A)。(D) 照抄 Alaska，阿拉斯加是淘金客要去的地方，補給是給人活命用的，不是要讓阿拉斯加繁榮；(B) 軍隊打仗、(C) 和愛斯基摩人交易，原文都沒有提到。

stem: No matter what happened to the woman who owned the shoe, ______.

options.A: she must have lived a happy life
options.B: she certainly dropped the shoe on purpose
options.C: her adventurous spirit is definitely admirable
options.D: her other shoes were equally fashionable

ev.t: Whoever dropped the shoe must have been a brave and determined woman.
No one will ever know for sure, but what we do know is that she took part in one of the greatest adventures in the 19th century.

note: 第 2 段說掉了這隻鞋的人，一定是個勇敢又堅決（brave and determined）的女人；不管她最後成功還是折返，我們確實知道她參與了 19 世紀最偉大的冒險之一。題幹的 No matter what happened 對應原文的 Perhaps…Perhaps…No one will ever know，作者肯定的是她勇於冒險的精神，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄第 1 段的 dropped，原文用兩個問句猜測鞋子是不小心掉的還是故意丟的，沒有確定（certainly）；(A) 原文說她可能失望地折返，看不出一定過得快樂；(D) 她的其他鞋子，原文沒有提到。

stem: The author of this passage would like us to remember that ______.

options.A: “gold fever” was not worth the lives of many people
options.B: simple objects can stimulate our imagination
options.C: lost shoes should be sent to museums for exhibition
options.D: Alaska was not a place suitable for making a living

note: 第 1 段開頭就說每件物品都在訴說一個故事，即使最普通的物品也能帶給我們強烈的意象；接著以一隻舊皮鞋為例，作者從鞋子發現的地點，想像鞋子的主人怎麼掉了鞋、淘金客走過怎樣的旅程、她最後是成功還是折返。作者要我們記得的是，簡單的物品能激發我們的想像力，所以是 (B)。三個錯誤選項都偏離主題：(A) 第 2 段雖然說許多人死於飢餓和寒冷，但作者沒有評論淘金值不值得；(C) 文章沒有說遺失的鞋子應該送到博物館展覽；(D) 文章談的是淘金的旅程，沒有說阿拉斯加不適合謀生。

stem: Nasreddin gave Ali an extra small pot in the beginning because ______.

options.A: he and Ali were really good friends
options.B: he had too many pots at home
options.C: he wanted to have more baby pots
options.D: he wanted to trick Ali

ev.t: While your pot was staying with me, it had a baby.
you believed me when I told you that your pot had a baby

note: 第 1 段 Nasreddin 多還了一個小鍋，說是大鍋生的寶寶；第 2 段他再借走大鍋，就說大鍋死了，還反問 Ali 當初不是相信鍋子會生寶寶嗎。一開始多給小鍋，是要讓 Ali 相信鍋子會生寶寶，之後才能用鍋子死了的說法騙走大鍋，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄 baby，鍋子生寶寶是 Nasreddin 編出來騙 Ali 的說法，他並不是想要更多小鍋；(A) 兩人的交情，原文沒有提到，從結局看 Nasreddin 是在騙鄰居；(B) 原文沒有說他家裡的鍋子太多。

stem: Why did Ali take Nasreddin’s words that his pot had a baby?

options.A: He had no reason to doubt it.
options.B: He wanted to keep the small pot.
options.C: He had seen pots having babies before.
options.D: He believed in whatever Nasreddin said.

ev.t: “That's not mine,” said Ali.
Ali gladly agreed and waited to see if Nasreddin would again give him back two pots.

note: Ali 在第 1 段先說小鍋不是他的；到了第 2 段 Nasreddin 再借鍋時，他很樂意地答應，還等著看會不會又拿回兩個鍋子。可見 Ali 接受鍋子生寶寶的說法，是因為想留下那個小鍋，所以是 (B)。(D) 照抄 believed，Nasreddin 最後說的是 Ali 相信了鍋子生寶寶這件事，原文沒有說 Ali 什麼話都相信；(A) Ali 一開始就說小鍋不是他的，他其實有理由懷疑；(C) 鍋子不會生寶寶，Ali 不可能看過。

stem: It can be inferred that Ali had ______ at the end of the story.

options.A: neither of the pots
options.B: the big pot
options.C: the small pot
options.D: both pots

ev.t: The next day he returned the pot with a small one inside.
your pot has died

note: 第 1 段 Ali 拿回了大鍋，也多拿到一個小鍋；第 2 段 Nasreddin 再借走大鍋，最後說大鍋死了，不還了。Ali 手上只剩第一次多拿到的小鍋，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄 big pot，大鍋第二次借出去以後，Nasreddin 就說它死了，沒有還給 Ali；(D) 兩個鍋子都在 Ali 手上，是第 1 段結束時的情形，不是故事的結局；(A) 小鍋第一次就留在 Ali 那裡，所以他不是什麼都沒有。

stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a way to deal with dead mail?

options.A: To search for clues.
options.B: To throw dead mail away.
options.C: To open dead mail.
options.D: To list dead mail on a computer.

ev.t: The post office cannot just throw the mail away

note: 第 1 段說郵局不能把郵件直接丟掉（cannot just throw the mail away），所以處理死信的方法不包括 (B)。其他三個選項都在第 2 段：找線索（look for clues），是 (A)；打開包裹，是 (C)；登錄在電腦上，是 (D)。

stem: The staff in a dead mail office may open a package in order to find ______.

options.A: some money
options.B: some missing objects
options.C: an address
options.D: a computer

ev.t: they open packages in the hope that something inside will show where the package came from or is going to.

note: 第 2 段說員工打開包裹，是希望裡面有東西能看出包裹從哪裡寄來、要寄到哪裡（where the package came from or is going to），也就是寄件人或收件人的地址，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄 missing，原文的 missing item 是民眾打電話來查的遺失物品，不是員工拆包裹要找的東西；(D) 照抄 computer，電腦是用來登錄死信、方便民眾查詢的；(A) 錢，原文沒有提到。
map: where the package came from or is going to

stem: The passage indicates that dead mail auctions are held ______.

options.A: once a year
options.B: twice a year
options.C: three times a year
options.D: four times a year

ev.t: Every three months, the public is invited to the offices

note: 第 3 段說每三個月（Every three months）舉行一次拍賣，一年有 12 個月，所以一年舉行四次，是 (D)。(C) 把「每三個月」看成「一年三次」；(A)、(B) 的次數都太少。

stem: Which is the best title for the passage?

options.A: Dead Mail
options.B: Mail Auction
options.C: Unknown Mail
options.D: The Dead Mail Office

note: 第 1 段說明什麼是死信、死信送到哪裡，第 2 段寫員工怎麼處理死信，第 3 段寫死信太多時的拍賣，每一段都圍繞著死信，所以最好的標題是 (A)。(B) 拍賣只在第 3 段，過於狹隘；(D) 死信辦公室是死信送去處理的地方，標題只談辦公室，等於只講第 2、3 段辦公室怎麼處理死信，沒有涵蓋第 1 段死信是怎麼來的，過於狹隘；(C) 文章談的是沒辦法投遞的郵件，不是來歷不明的郵件，偏離主題。

stem: Where was the poet?

options.A: In a garden.
options.B: In a dance hall.
options.C: In the countryside.
options.D: In a space ship.

ev.t: That floats on high o'er vales and hills,
Beside the lake, beneath the trees,
Along the margin of a bay:

note: 詩人說自己飄過山谷和丘陵（vales and hills），在湖邊、樹下看到水仙花，第 2 段又寫到海灣，這些都是野外的景色，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄第 2 段的 dance，跳舞的是隨風搖動的水仙花，詩人不在舞廳裡；(D) 銀河和星星是用來比喻水仙花連綿不斷，詩人不在太空船上；(A) 上萬朵水仙花沿著湖邊、海灣生長，不是庭院花園裡的景象。

stem: Which of the following is most likely true about the poet?

options.A: He was a great dancer.
options.B: He liked to be close to Nature.
options.C: He enjoyed the company of people.
options.D: He was a very lonely person.

ev.t: When all at once I saw a crowd,
Ten thousand saw I at a glance,

note: 詩人獨自在山谷丘陵間漫遊，看到湖邊上萬朵水仙花隨風起舞，還用星星、跳舞來描寫這些花，看得出他喜歡親近大自然，所以是 (B)。(D) 照抄 lonely，lonely as a cloud 是詩人形容自己像雲一樣獨自漫遊，只說那時候他一個人，看不出他是個很孤單的人；(A) 照抄 dance，跳舞的是水仙花，不是詩人；(C) 詩裡的 a crowd 指的是一大群水仙花，不是人群。

stem: Why did the author ask his friends to count from one to twenty?

options.A: He wanted them to think that was all he wanted to record.
options.B: He wanted to record how they pronounced numbers.
options.C: He had to check whether his tape-recorder was working.
options.D: He wanted to discover who had the best accent.

ev.t: I explained that all I wanted was for them to count from one to twenty.
The participants, having seen the visible tape-recorder turned off, paid no more attention to the microphones

note: 作者真正要錄的是朋友們自然的閒聊。第 1 段他說只要大家從一數到二十，數完就喝酒放鬆；第 3 段說朋友們看到錄音機關了，就不再注意麥克風。要大家數數，是要讓他們以為要錄的只有這些，所以是 (A)。(D) 照抄第 2 段的 best accent，大家拿出最標準的口音數數，是因為以為作者要錄口音，作者並不是要比誰的口音最好；(C) 照抄 tape-recorder，數數不是在測試錄音機；(B) 作者說對口音有興趣只是藉口，他要的不是數字的發音。

stem: Why did the author leave the room in the middle of the evening?

options.A: He had to make a phone call to order some drinks.
options.B: He didn’t like to be criticized for being idiotic.
options.C: He wanted to turn off a tape recorder in another room.
options.D: He wanted the others to have a conversation without him.

ev.t: And my lengthy absence meant that I was able to obtain as natural a piece of conversation as it would be possible to find.

note: 第 2 段作者說他得到另一個房間接電話，第 3 段馬上說「至少表面上看起來是這樣」，接著說他離開很久，才能錄到最自然的對話。作者離開，是要讓朋友們在他不在的時候自在地聊天，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 phone call，接電話只是藉口，而且原文是接電話，不是打電話訂飲料；(B) 照抄 idiotic，朋友們批評他的工作很蠢，但他離開不是因為不想聽批評；(C) 廚房裡的錄音機要一直錄，作者不會去關掉它。

stem: How did the author have the conversation recorded?

options.A: On the tape-recorder in the middle of the floor.
options.B: Through hidden microphones.
options.C: On a tape-recorder in another room.
options.D: In a studio.

ev.t: but to another one, which was turning happily away in the kitchen.

note: 第 3 段說麥克風根本沒有接到房間中間那台錄音機，而是接到另一台在廚房裡（in the kitchen）運轉的錄音機，選項換成 in another room，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 middle of the floor，地板中間那台錄音機是給朋友們看的，早就關掉了；(B) 照抄 microphones，麥克風就擺在椅子前面，朋友們都看得到，並沒有藏起來；(D) 照抄 studio，客廳只是布置得像錄音室。

stem: How did his friends react when the author told them what he had done?

options.A: They wanted him to destroy the recordings he had made.
options.B: They didn’t really feel offended.
options.C: They were upset because they felt he had cheated them.
options.D: They made him pay them for the recordings.

ev.t: None of them wanted to

note: 第 4 段說作者事後讓朋友們選擇要不要銷毀錄音帶，結果沒有人要銷毀（None of them wanted to），可見他們並沒有真的生氣，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄 destroy，朋友們可以選擇銷毀，卻沒有人這麼做；(D) 原文說後來每次買酒總是輪到作者請客，這是朋友們要他還的人情，不是要他付錄音的錢；(C) 原文沒有說朋友們覺得受騙而生氣。

stem: What was Shaw trying to say to Churchill on his card?

options.A: Churchill should not go to the play alone.
options.B: Churchill should not bring too many people.
options.C: Churchill may have to waste the two tickets.
options.D: Churchill did not have any friend.

ev.t: Bring a friend (if you have one).

note: 卡片上寫「帶一位朋友來（如果你有的話）」，括號裡的話是在暗諷邱吉爾可能根本沒有朋友，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 bring，蕭伯納只說帶一位朋友，和帶太多人無關；(C) 照抄 two tickets，蕭伯納沒有說票會浪費掉；(A) 叫邱吉爾帶朋友來只是字面上的意思，蕭伯納真正要說的是括號裡的話。

stem: Why didn’t Churchill want the tickets for the first night?

options.A: He didn’t want to take Shaw’s insult.
options.B: The theater would not be as crowded the second night.
options.C: He was busy on the first night of the show.
options.D: He couldn’t find a friend to go with him the first night.

ev.t: Churchill, however, managed to get the better of this exchange.
Please send me two tickets for the second night (if there is one).

note: 第 2 段用 however 說這一回合邱吉爾占了上風（get the better of），他退回首演的票，反過來暗諷蕭伯納的戲可能演不到第二晚。可見他退票是不肯白白接受蕭伯納的嘲諷，還回敬了一句，所以是 (A)。(C) 照抄 busy，「那天晚上我很忙」只是他退票的說法，括號裡的「如果有第二晚的話」才是重點；(B) 照抄 second night，邱吉爾要第二晚的票，是在暗諷這齣戲可能演不到第二晚，和戲院擠不擠無關；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 friend，邱吉爾沒有說找不到朋友。

stem: What is the best title for this article?

options.A: What’s a Friend for
options.B: Seashells and Mollusks
options.C: Appropriate Topics for Writing
options.D: Writing for Different Purposes

note: 第 1 段說作者寫作的理由不只一種，可以是娛樂讀者，也可以是提供資訊；第 2 段說下面兩段是這兩類的例子。全文談的是寫作的不同目的，所以最好的標題是 (D)。(A) 只講第 3 段 Nelson 和 Adam 的故事，過於狹隘；(B) 只講第 4 段的貝殼，過於狹隘；(C) 文章談的是寫作的目的，不是哪些題材適合寫，偏離主題。

stem: Regarding the first example, which of the following is FALSE?

options.A: Nelson was not a responsible person.
options.B: Adam and Nelson are military officers.
options.C: Nelson left his empty boxes in Adam’s office.
options.D: Adam played a practical joke on Nelson.

ev.t: Later in the afternoon, Nelson came to Adam’s office with Peter for their biology project.

note: 第 3 段說 Nelson 和 Peter 下午到 Adam 的辦公室做生物科的專題，看得出他們是一起做作業的學生；原文的 office 只是辦公室，沒有說他們是軍官，所以和原文不符的是 (B)。其他三個選項都和原文相符：Nelson 沒時間把空箱子拿去垃圾場，就丟在 Adam 的辦公室，是 (C)，這樣做也很不負責任，是 (A)；掉下來的除了空箱子，還有籃球和玩具青蛙，可見 Adam 故意把東西堆在門後捉弄 Nelson，是 (D)。

stem: Which of the following is TRUE according to the first example?

options.A: Nelson and Adam never liked each other.
options.B: Adam didn’t know what Nelson put into his office.
options.C: Peter complained to Nelson about the empty boxes.
options.D: Nelson was taught a lesson by Adam.

ev.t: The empty boxes and many other things fell all over them the minute he opened the door.
This is no way to treat a friend!

note: Nelson 把空箱子丟在 Adam 的辦公室，下午他一打開門，空箱子和許多其他東西就砸在他身上，他大叫「怎麼可以這樣對待朋友」。Adam 用同樣的方法回敬 Nelson，給了他一個教訓，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄 Peter，Peter 只是和 Nelson 一起去做專題，大叫抱怨的是 Nelson；(A) Nelson 說 Adam 是朋友，看不出兩人一直合不來；(B) 東西又堆回門後砸下來，可見 Adam 知道 Nelson 放了什麼。

stem: According to the author, the second example is intended to

options.A: express opinions about seashells.
options.B: present facts about seashells.
options.C: show us the beauty of seashells.
options.D: describe the shapes of seashells.

ev.t: Authors also write about these things to inform by giving facts or ideas.
The following two paragraphs are examples of these two kinds.

note: 第 1 段說作者寫作，有時是為了娛樂讀者，有時是為了提供事實或想法（giving facts or ideas）；第 4 段的第二個例子介紹貝殼的種類、形狀和軟體動物，屬於提供資訊的一類，選項換成 present facts，所以是 (B)。(D) 照抄 shape，貝殼的形狀只是第 4 段提供的事實之一，不是整段的目的；(A) 這一段沒有發表對貝殼的看法；(C) 這一段也沒有讚美貝殼有多美。

stem: What is the theme of this passage?

options.A: Introduction to a foreign culture.
options.B: Historical background of a region.
options.C: Discussion of environmental problems.
options.D: Geographical information of a place.

note: 全文介紹考艾島：第 1 段寫河流、懸崖和峽谷，第 2 段寫山和雨量，第 3 段寫颶風過後的復原，第 4 段寫適合在島上從事的戶外活動，都是這個地方的地理資訊，所以是 (D)。(B) 文章只在第 3 段提到 1992 年的颶風，沒有談這個地區的歷史背景，過於狹隘；(A) 文章沒有介紹當地的文化，偏離主題；(C) 颶風是天災，文章也沒有討論環境問題，偏離主題。

stem: What is Kauai famous for?

options.A: Cold weather.
options.B: Natural beauty.
options.C: Active volcanoes.
options.D: Amusement parks.

ev.t: has some of the state’s most stunning scenery

note: 第 1 段說考艾島有夏威夷州幾處最令人驚嘆的景色（most stunning scenery），接著介紹叢林、懸崖和峽谷，選項換成 Natural beauty，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 volcano，第 2 段說懷亞萊阿萊山是死火山（extinct volcano），不是活火山；(A) 原文沒有談到天氣冷；(D) 第 4 段說主要的吸引力在戶外，原文沒有提到遊樂園。

stem: What is the rainfall condition of Kauai?

options.B: It rains a lot except in high mountains.
options.C: There is a lot of rain everywhere most of the year.
options.D: The rainfall changes much with seasons.

ev.t: Yet this amount of rain is surprisingly localized.
Just a few miles west, there’s a dry region that receives a mere 6 inches of rain annually.

note: 第 2 段說懷亞萊阿萊山每年降雨將近 500 英寸，接著用 Yet 說這麼多的雨出乎意料地集中在小範圍裡（surprisingly localized），往西幾英里一年只下 6 英寸，選項換成 concentrates in some spots，所以是 (A)。(B) 正好相反，雨下得最多的就是山區的懷亞萊阿萊山；(C) 原文說西邊有乾燥地區，不是到處都多雨；(D) 原文沒有談雨量隨季節變化。

stem: Which of the following statements is FALSE about the island of Kauai?

stem: Which of the following statements is NOT true?

options.A: Small living things like bacteria provide food for other living things.
options.B: Carbon dioxide is produced during the process of decomposition.
options.C: Plants are important for supporting the life of animals.
options.D: Decomposers play a minor role in the recycling of nature.

ev.t: The decomposers are a vital link in the natural cycle of life and death.

note: 原文最後說分解者是大自然生死循環中不可或缺的一環（a vital link），不是次要的角色，所以和原文不符的是 (D)。其他三個選項都和原文相符：細菌這類分解者把化學物質釋放出來，讓其他生物可以利用，是 (A)；分解的過程會釋放二氧化碳，是 (B)；沒有植物提供的氧氣和食物，動物都會餓死，是 (C)。

stem: According to the passage, death is not the end of life, but rather

options.A: supports many forms of life.
options.B: borrows material from the Earth.
options.C: shows how bacteria become chemicals.
options.D: controls the amounts of soil.

ev.t: The dead material and waste matter form the diet of a group of living organisms called decomposers.
making them available to other living things

note: 原文說死去的生物是分解者的食物，分解者再把化學物質釋放到空氣、土壤和水中，讓其他生物利用（available to other living things）；植物靠二氧化碳生長，動物又靠植物的氧氣和食物活下去。死亡養活了許多生命，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 borrow，原文說生物身上的化學物質是向地球借來的，死的時候是還回去，不是借；(C) 照抄 bacteria，細菌是分解者，原文沒有說細菌變成化學物質；(D) 照抄 soil，土壤是化學物質釋放的地方之一，原文沒有說死亡控制土壤的多寡。

stem: This is a report about John Glenn after he

options.A: successfully accomplished his 1962 Mercury flight.
options.B: became the first man to land on the moon.
options.C: was welcomed in New York the second time.
options.D: retired from the U.S. Senate.

note: 這篇報導從第 1 段 Glenn 第二次參加紐約英雄谷的遊行寫起，接著拿兩次遊行比較，寫觀眾少了、熱情也少了，全篇報導的是 Glenn 第二次在紐約接受歡迎的情形，所以是 (C)。(A) 1962 年水星計畫的飛行和第一次遊行，只在第 2 段當作對照，過於狹隘；(D) 第 7 段說 Glenn 下個月才要從參議院退休，報導寫的不是他退休以後的事，過於狹隘；(B) Glenn 是第一位環繞地球軌道飛行的美國人，不是第一位登陸月球的人，偏離主題。

stem: What impressed Glenn most in the 1962 parade?

options.A: The huge crowd of people around him.
options.B: The huge amount of paper poured over him.
options.C: The Christmas tree in front of the Rockefeller Center.
options.D: The key to the city he received from the mayor.

ev.t: I remember just a blizzard of paper.

note: 第 6 段 Glenn 回憶 1962 年的遊行，說他記得紙片多得像暴風雪一樣（a blizzard of paper），一抬頭眼睛就會有東西掉進去，選項換成 the huge amount of paper，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 Christmas tree，替洛克斐勒中心的聖誕樹裝飾是這一次的行程，不是 1962 年的事；(A) 照抄第 3 段的 crowd，那裡說的是這次遊行華爾街的午餐人潮，Glenn 回憶 1962 年時說的是紙片；(D) 市長送他城市的鑰匙，原文沒有提到。

stem: Which of the following statements is TRUE?

options.A: John Glenn is admirable in that he has been to the moon more than once.
options.B: Only John Glenn has received the ticker-tape parade more than once.
options.C: Many Americans are no longer excited about space achievements.

ev.t: too many Americans take the achievements of the space program for granted

note: 第 5 段一位觀眾說，太多美國人把太空計畫的成就視為理所當然（take … for granted），已經沒有人在乎了，選項換成美國人不再對太空成就感到興奮，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄第 7 段的 more than，原文說 Glenn 加入了許多獲得不只一次紙花遊行的個人和隊伍，不是只有他一個人；(D) 第 3、4 段說第二次遊行人少、路線短，第一次比較熱烈；(A) Glenn 是環繞地球軌道飛行，原文沒有說他上過月球。

no longer excited about space achievements

stem: According to the passage, how many space flights has Glenn taken?

options.A: One
options.B: Two
options.C: Three

ev.t: saluting his return to space 36 years after he became America’s first man in orbit.
Glenn’s first ticker-tape parade on March 1, 1962, after his Mercury flight

note: 第 1 段說這次遊行是慶祝 Glenn 在成為美國第一位環繞地球軌道飛行的人 36 年以後重返太空（his return to space），第 2 段說第一次飛行是 1962 年水星計畫的飛行。1962 年一次，36 年後再一次，所以是 (B)。(A) 只算到 1962 年那一次；他參加了兩次遊行，每次都是在太空飛行之後，所以 (C)、(D) 的次數都太多。

stem: Why does the report say that the figure of Glenn’s second parade was “inflated”?

options.C: Because the crowd of the second parade seemed to be far less than 500,000.

ev.t: the turnout Monday was sparse by New York standards
a figure that appeared generously inflated.

note: 第 3 段說週一出來看遊行的人以紐約的標準來說稀稀落落（sparse），警方卻說有 50 萬人，記者認為這個數字誇大了不少（generously inflated）。實際人數看起來遠少於 50 萬，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄第 4 段的 enthusiastic，比較熱烈的是 1962 年那一次；(A) 正好相反，第二次的人比第一次少；(B) 原文只提到一位兩次都參加的觀眾，記者說數字誇大，和有沒有人參加兩次無關。

stem: Robot Redford’s speech was discussed in this article mainly because ______.

options.A: it was political
options.B: it was psychological
options.C: it was controversial
options.D: it was insensitive

note: 第 1 段說機器人當畢業演講者非常不尋常，第 4 段說選機器人當演講者引起不少爭議（controversy），有人覺得不妥，有人覺得有創意，第 5 段再用畢業生的話收尾。這場演講會寫成報導，主要是因為它引起爭議，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄 insensitive，那只是第 4 段部分學生的看法，過於狹隘；(A) 照抄 political，第 5 段的畢業生只是拿政治領袖和機器人比較，演講內容和政治無關，偏離主題；(B) 文章沒有談到心理學，偏離主題。

stem: Which of the following statements is NOT true?

ev.t: a robot who delivered the commencement address at a community college in suburban Maryland.

note: 第 1 段說 Robot Redford 是在馬里蘭州一所社區大學的畢業典禮上致詞（delivered the commencement address），它是演講者，不是畢業生，所以和原文不符的是 (D)。其他三個選項都和原文相符：第 2 段說這個機器人可以設定程式說話，是 (A)；它靠自己的動力走上講台（under its own power），是 (B)；第 1 段說這是 1983 年的畢業典禮季，是 (C)。

stem: Which of the following statements can be supported by the passage?

note: 第 3 段說 Bakaleinikoff 製造了 Robot Redford（he had created Robot Redford），選項的 brainchild 指的是某人構想出來的心血結晶，所以是 (B)。(A) 第 2 段說機器人能幫助人類完成更多工作，不是降低生產力；(C) 第 4 段說這個安排引起爭議，有學生覺得不妥，不是每個人都滿意；(D) 原文沒有說演講太難懂。

stem: As used in the passage, “navigation” clearly means ______.

options.C: the act of piloting an airplane

ev.t: part of which consisted of tying several knots in a given time limit
I was required to formally plot our course, using the tide table

note: 原文說航海課要在規定時間內打好幾種繩結，接著搭父親的船出海過夜，還要用潮汐表規劃航線。這些都是駕船出海的本事，所以 navigation 指的是駕駛船隻，是 (B)。(D) 照抄 formal examination，飯廳裡的正式考試只是航海課的一部分；(A) 照抄 summer school，夏季學校是父親辦的整套課程，航海只是其中一門；(C) 文中出海用的是船，和開飛機無關。

stem: Why is Paris building a new Eiffel Tower?

The mayor said new buildings would be illuminated

stem: What is “the Seine” mentioned in the passage?

stem: Why is the new tower made of wood?

stem: The phrase dispose of in the first paragraph can best be replaced by ______.

options.A: put up with
options.B: get rid of
options.C: look down upon

ev.t: wondered how to dispose of the old items

stem: The purpose of setting up The Carpenters’ Shop was ______.

options.A: to help those who could not afford certain household items

Many have been helped through the scheme

stem: What is the author’s opinion of an item that someone doesn’t need any longer?

options.A: It's normally out of style.
options.B: It should be donated to charity.
options.C: It's an admirable project.
options.D: There may be something wrong with it.

ev.t: Participation costs the donor nothing and can make such a difference to others.

stem: What does the word rescued in the second paragraph mean?

options.B: prescribed
options.C: examined

It would be difficult to put a value on the things rescued by the Disk Doctor.

stem: Why did the architect send Jack a blank check?

options.A: The architect did not have any money
options.B: The architect did it for security reasons
options.C: The architect always followed the doctor's advice
options.D: The architect thought Jack's service was priceless

stem: Which of the following statements is NOT true?

options.A: Jack’s Disk Doctor Service has only one standard fee.
options.B: Jack and his company have made a fortune from their service.
options.C: Margaret Thatcher is a very important person.
options.D: Jack’s clients are from all walks of life.

stem: When did the “Kawasaki” first get into trouble during the voyage?

sailed from an unnamed eastern Russian seaport on August 18
had been smooth until four days ago

stem: Mary is a typical left-brained learner. Which of the following descriptions does NOT fit her?
