note: 文章開頭說大型車造成的事故比小型車多，接著用一場車禍說明大型車比較危險，最後說大型車還造成石油枯竭、環境汙染和交通擁擠。作者的主要論點是大型車比小型車不安全、也不經濟，所以是 (B)。大考中心公布的答案是 (B) 或 (C)，選 (C) 小型車對乘客比大型車安全，也算答對。(D) 這位女士心臟病發只是作者舉的例子，作者要怪的是她開的大型車，過於狹隘；(A) 文章沒有說政府應該禁止大型車，偏離主題。

stem: The author's statement about the highway fence's ability to retain a smaller and lighter car

options.A: is the author's assumption.
options.B: derives from scientific evidence.
options.C: rests upon fact.
options.D: can never be verified.

ev.t: A lighter and smaller car probably wouldn't have gone through the fence
it might have missed the other car completely

note: 作者說換成輕一點、小一點的車，「大概」（probably）就不會衝破護欄，下一句又用 might have missed，這些都是作者自己的推測，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 scientific evidence，開頭的科學證據說的是大型車造成的事故比較多，不是小車能不能擋在護欄內；(C) 小車會不會衝破護欄並沒有真的發生，不是事實；(D) 原文沒有說這種說法永遠無法證實。

stem: The 60 pilot whales swam ashore as a result of

options.A: a large winter storm off the coast of Cape Cod.
options.B: a behavior currently unknown to scientists.
options.C: a genetic phenomenon currently being studied by whale experts.
options.D: the return to their annual spawning ground near Cape Cod.

ev.t: Scientists are still trying to find out why whales have this self-destructive behavior.

note: 第 2 段說多達 60 隻領航鯨游上岸，科學家還在設法找出鯨魚為什麼會有這種自我毀滅的行為（still trying to find out why），也就是原因目前還不清楚，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 whale experts，鯨魚專家是發現三隻小鯨魚還活著的人，原文沒有說他們在研究遺傳現象；(A) 擱淺發生在 12 月，但原文沒有提到暴風雨；(D) 原文沒有說鱈魚角是鯨魚每年產卵的地方。
map: still trying to find out why

stem: The pilot whales died on the beaches of Cape Cod due to

options.A: the lack of salt water to facilitate their respiration.
options.B: the lack of nutrition to maintain their enormous body weight.
options.C: their body structure unable to support their body weight out of water.
options.D: a phenomenon yet to be figured out by scientists.

ev.t: Many of the whales died on the beach—crushed by their own weight.

note: 第 2 段說很多鯨魚死在海灘上，是自己的體重把自己壓死的（crushed by their own weight）。鯨魚離開了水，身體承受不了自己的重量，選項換成 unable to support their body weight out of water，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄 weight，原文說的是體重壓死了自己，不是缺乏營養；(D) 科學家還不清楚的，是鯨魚為什麼游上岸，不是牠們為什麼死；(A) 原文沒有提到海水和呼吸。

stem: The three whales Tag, Notch, and Baby were rescued because

options.A: younger whales have a greater chance of survival than the others.
options.B: amongst the many whales found beached, these three were deemed the healthiest.
options.C: they were alive when the rescue team found them.
options.D: the rescue crew liked them very much.

ev.t: Whale experts found Tag, Notch, Baby alive.

note: 第 2 段說鯨魚專家發現 Tag、Notch 和 Baby 還活著（alive），這三隻才送到水族館照顧，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 young，原文說這三隻年紀太小，沒辦法自己活下去，正好和選項說年紀小比較容易活下去相反；(B) 原文沒有說牠們是最健康的三隻；(D) 原文沒有說救援人員特別喜歡牠們。

stem: Which of the following is NOT true?

options.A: Scientists are studying the suicidal behavior of pilot whales.
options.B: Tag, Notch, and Baby were too young to survive by themselves in the sea.
options.C: Pilot Whales are mammals that can become used to human beings.
options.D: After their release, Tag, Notch, and Baby were never seen again.

ev.t: A month after their release, the whales were spotted.

note: 第 4 段說野放一個月後，有人看到了牠們（the whales were spotted），牠們和一群 50 隻鯨魚在一起，所以和原文不符的是 (D)。其他三個選項都和原文相符：第 2 段說科學家還在研究鯨魚自我毀滅的行為，是 (A)；三隻鯨魚年紀太小，沒辦法自己活下去，是 (B)；第 3 段說只讓少數人照顧，以免牠們太習慣人類，可見鯨魚是會習慣人類的，是 (C)。

stem: The Carnegie Medal is given to those who are

options.A: sick and poor.
options.B: rich and famous.
options.C: young and brave.
options.D: unselfish and courageous.

ev.t: It is given to people who act bravely and face danger to save the lives of others.
They put someone else's safety ahead of their own.

note: 第 2 段說卡內基獎章頒給勇敢行動（act bravely）、冒著危險救人性命的人；第 4 段說這些英雄都把別人的安全放在自己的安全之前。勇敢又無私，選項換成 unselfish and courageous，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄第 3 段的 young，William Hunter 是年輕人，但獎章並不限年輕人；(B) 照抄 rich，有錢的是設立獎章的 Carnegie；(A) 第 3 段說英雄如果生活困難或受了傷，還會另外得到錢，生病、貧窮不是頒獎的條件。

stem: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.A: William Hunter was a very brave boy.
options.B: Hunter saved Carnegie from drowning.
options.C: Some heroes have been rewarded for their bravery.
options.D: Carnegie was a rich businessman and liked to help people.

note: 第 1 段說英雄是在緊急時刻勇敢出手的人，第 2 段說英雄有時候會因為勇敢的行為得到獎勵，接著第 3、4 段介紹卡內基獎章的由來和得獎的人。全文的主旨是有些英雄因為勇敢得到表揚，所以是 (C)。(A) William Hunter 的故事只在第 3 段，是獎章的由來，過於狹隘；(D) Carnegie 是富有的商人，也只在第 3 段，過於狹隘；(B) 原文說 Hunter 是為了救兩個男孩而死，不是救了 Carnegie，偏離主題。

stem: Which of the following statements is NOT true?

options.A: Carnegie knew Hunter in person.
options.B: Brave deeds can take many different forms.
options.C: Over 6,000 people are Carnegie Medal recipients.
options.D: Some heroes have received money as well as the Medal.

ev.t: Carnegie heard about a young man by the name of William Hunter

note: 第 3 段說 Carnegie 是「聽說」（heard about）William Hunter 的事，看不出他認識 Hunter 本人，所以和原文不符的是 (A)。其他三個選項都和原文相符：第 4 段說有人從水裡、火場救人，有人把人從火車前拉開，英勇的行為有很多種形式，是 (B)；已經有 6,000 多人獲得獎章，是 (C)；第 3 段說生活困難或受傷的英雄，除了獎章還會得到一筆錢，是 (D)。

stem: George Willig reached the top of the World Trade Center in New York at

options.A: six thirty in the morning of May 26, 1977.
options.B: six thirty in the evening of May 26, 1977.
options.C: ten o'clock in the morning of May 26, 1977.
options.D: ten o'clock in the evening of May 26, 1977.

ev.t: His climb, which began at 6:30 a.m., took three and a half hours to finish.

note: 第 1 段說 Willig 早上 6 點 30 分（6:30 a.m.）開始爬，花了三個半小時才爬完。6 點 30 分加上三個半小時是 10 點，所以他在早上 10 點到達頂端，是 (C)。(A) 6 點 30 分是他開始爬的時間；(B)、(D) 是晚上，原文寫的是 a.m.，指的是上午。

stem: This passage is a story about

options.A: a man who enjoys dangers and risks.
options.B: a human being who can fly like a fly.
options.C: a man who has escaped from the jail.
options.D: a fly which climbs like a human being.

note: 第 1 段說 Willig 不搭電梯，貼著 110 層樓的外牆爬上世界貿易中心，第 2 段說他爬到頂樓後，警方要控告他未經許可攀爬大樓，市政府也打算向他求償，第 3 段說市政府隔天改變態度，把他當成敢於挑戰不可能的英雄。這是一個喜歡冒險、不怕危險的人的故事，所以是 (A)。三個錯誤選項都偏離主題：(B) 照抄 fly，human fly 是形容他像蒼蠅一樣爬牆，他並不會飛；(D) 也照抄 fly，故事的主角是人，不是蒼蠅；(C) 照抄 jail，第 2 段說警方想把他關進監獄，但他沒有坐牢，更沒有越獄。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?

options.A: Willig was fined $250,000.
options.B: Willig was sent to prison for a year.
options.C: Willig was honored in a party and fined only $1.10.
options.D: Willig climbed the World Trade Center with permission.

ev.t: a ceremony in George Willig's honor
Instead, he would be fined a penny for each of the 110 floors he had climbed.

note: 第 3 段說市長舉行的記者會變成了表揚 Willig 的典禮（a ceremony in George Willig's honor），而且只照他爬的 110 層樓，每層罰一美分。110 美分就是 1.10 美元，所以是 (C)。(A) 25 萬美元是市政府原本打算向他求償的金額，第二天就改了；(B) 警方原本想把他關進監獄，但原文沒有說他坐了一年牢；(D) 第 2 段說他是未經許可（without a permit）攀爬大樓。

stem: Printing is important because

options.A: it is a Chinese invention.
options.B: it has made reading books possible.
options.C: it has helped to develop radio and television.
options.D: William Caxton printed 80 books in English.

ev.t: Without it you would not now be reading this passage.

note: 第 1 段說要是沒有印刷，你現在就不會在讀這篇文章（would not now be reading this passage），也就是印刷讓閱讀成為可能，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 radio and television，原文說即使有了廣播和電視，印刷的重要性也沒有減少，沒有說印刷幫助了廣播、電視的發展；(D) 照抄第 4 段的 William Caxton，他印書是印刷發展的一段歷史，不是印刷重要的原因；(A) 照抄第 3 段的 Chinese，中國人發明的是活字，這也不是印刷重要的原因。

stem: The use of movable type was first introduced by

options.A: William Caxton.
options.B: the Europeans.
options.C: Johannes Gutenberg.
options.D: The Chinese.

ev.t: The Chinese discovered this in the 11th century, but it was not known in Europe until about 1440.

note: 第 3 段說中國人在 11 世紀就發明了活字（The Chinese discovered this），歐洲一直到 1440 年左右才知道，所以最早使用活字的是中國人，是 (D)。(B) 照抄 Europe，歐洲知道活字比中國晚了大約四百年；(C) 照抄第 4 段的 Gutenberg，古騰堡的聖經是歐洲最早用活字印刷的書之一；(A) 照抄第 4 段的 Caxton，他印的是第一本用活字印刷的英文書，時間更晚。

stem: According to the passage, the use of movable type was considered as a "great step forward" because

options.A: it did not need a lot of wood.
options.B: it required less skill and patience.
options.C: the printing letters could be reused.
options.D: every page of every book required individual carving.

ev.t: the letters could be taken apart and rearranged to print something else.

note: 第 3 段說用活字印完以後，字母可以拆開來重新排列，印別的東西（rearranged to print something else），選項換成 could be reused，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄第 2 段的 every page of every book，每一頁都得分開來刻，是木板印刷的缺點；(B) 照抄 skill and patience，需要很多技巧和耐心的也是木板印刷，原文沒有比較活字需要的技巧；(A) 照抄 wood，木板是舊的印刷方法，原文沒有說活字的好處是省木材。

stem: The first English book printed in movable type was

options.A: done from wood blocks one letter at a time.
options.B: done in a printing press at Westminster.
options.C: Johannes Gutenberg's 42-line Bible.
options.D: about the history of Troy.

ev.t: The first book to be printed likewise in English was about the history of Troy.

note: 第 4 段說第一本同樣用活字印刷的英文書，內容是特洛伊的歷史（about the history of Troy），所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄 Gutenberg，古騰堡的聖經是歐洲最早的活字印刷書之一，不是英文書；(B) 照抄 Westminster，那本書 1474 年在法蘭德斯印製，Caxton 1476 年回英國以後，才在西敏設立印刷廠；(A) 照抄第 2 段的 wood blocks，用木板一個字母一個字母刻，是活字出現以前的方法。
